### BF-105a93f

**An extension that calls `newSession`, `fork`, `navigateTree`, `switchSession` or `reload` from an event, tool…**

- **Source:** A Pi defect that PiG fixed first (divergence D617)
- **Symptom:** An extension that calls `newSession`, `fork`, `navigateTree`, `switchSession` or `reload` from an event, tool or shortcut handler, for example a `session_start` handler, no longer replaces the session in the middle of the emit, which made the built-in MCP extension panic on a stale context and `pig` exit 1.
- **Root cause:** A call with no live parent request was allowed, so a handler that stored its event context and called later replaced the session; Pi never allows that. The Go, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs mark every call made through a command handler's or a withSession callback's context (command_context) for the context's whole life, and the host refuses newSession, fork, navigateTree, switchSession and reload without the mark. The Node runtime gives only those contexts the five members, so an event context has none: typeof is undefined and a call throws Pi's TypeError (D617).
- **User impact:** Crash, hang or runaway process
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Pi issue:** none recorded
- **Removed when Pi fixes it:** the Go, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs hand event, tool and shortcut handlers a context type that has no command-only session actions (a separate command-context type), so the call cannot be written.
- **Fix commits:** `105a93fed1` (2026-11-11), `b1e177314f` (2026-11-11), `c99165dfe0` (2026-11-11), `f482e4ff75` (2026-11-11), `0b617e08be` (2026-11-12)
- **Tests:** `coding/extension/host/subprocess/callpayload_shape_test.go::TestCallPayloadKeepsUnkeyedLiteralShape`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/command_only_calls_test.go::TestCommandOnlyCallErrorIsPisMissingFunctionError`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/command_only_calls_test.go::TestCommandOnlyCallsAreThePiCommandContextSessionActions`, `test/extension-conformance/session_actions_event_context_test.go::TestConformance_CommandOnlySessionActionsRefusedFromEventContext`
- **Release note:** An extension that calls `newSession`, `fork`, `navigateTree`, `switchSession` or `reload` from an event, tool or shortcut handler, for example a `session_start` handler, no longer replaces the session in the middle of the emit, which made the built-in MCP extension panic on a stale context and `pig` exit 1. A handler that stores its event context and calls one of them after its request ended is refused as well. Pi gives these only to the command context, so its handler gets a `TypeError` there and the session goes on. In the Node runtime an event, tool or shortcut context has no such member (`typeof ctx.switchSession` is `undefined` and the call throws `ctx.switchSession is not a function`); the Go, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs, whose `Context` type has the methods, get the error `not_a_command_context` and the host runs nothing (D617). A command handler and a `withSession` callback are unchanged.

### BF-10818f5

**Go extensions that receive large event payloads (`before_provider_request`, `agent_end`, `turn_end`) now…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Go extensions that receive large event payloads (`before_provider_request`, `agent_end`, `turn_end`) now decode them about four times faster and allocate about half as much.
- **Root cause:** They were slow because the Go SDK and the host scanned and copied each frame five times: a byte-at-a-time validity scan, a second scan to skip a request's arguments, a copy of them, and two more validations and scans to hand the event to a handler.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `10818f5661` (2026-11-06)
- **Tests:** `extensions/sdk/event_args_memo_test.go::TestEventArgsMemoRepeatIsCheaperThanADecode`, `extensions/sdk/frame_decode_verdicts_test.go::TestFrameDecodeVerdicts`, `extensions/sdk/frame_decode_verdicts_test.go::TestRequestArgsKeepTheirBytesAcrossFrames`, `extensions/sdk/json/decode_fast_test.go::FuzzDecodeCrossesValues`, `extensions/sdk/json/decode_fast_test.go::TestDecodeCrossesValuesWithoutLosingItsPlace`, `extensions/sdk/json/decode_fast_test.go::TestInterfaceNumbers`, `extensions/sdk/json/decode_fast_test.go::TestInterfaceStringsAreTheirOwnText`, `extensions/sdk/json/decode_fast_test.go::TestUnmarshalFrameAliasesRawMessages` and 7 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** Go extensions that receive large event payloads (`before_provider_request`, `agent_end`, `turn_end`) now decode them about four times faster and allocate about half as much. They were slow because the Go SDK and the host scanned and copied each frame five times: a byte-at-a-time validity scan, a second scan to skip a request's arguments, a copy of them, and two more validations and scans to hand the event to a handler. On a 43 MiB provider payload, the read and decode of one request frame fell from about 600-800 ms to about 225 ms and from 181 MB to 101 MB allocated, and the host's read of a frame an extension sent rose from about 130 to about 500 MB/s. Malformed frames end the connection with the same message as before, and every value decodes to the same Go value. The Lisp SDK decoded a frame with many strings containing escapes in time quadratic in the frame (a 16 MiB frame took 20 s, now 0.15 s).

### BF-108cb7d

**An extension that exits while it loads, sits idle or shuts down no longer leaves the host waiting on its…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** An extension that exits while it loads, sits idle or shuts down no longer leaves the host waiting on its socket: on Windows a socket close can miss a pending read, and the host now ends the read when the extension's process exits, reporting the same transport error as a closed socket.
- **Root cause:** The host's read loop waits on the socket with no deadline, and its heartbeat writes only while a request is in flight. A read that was pending when the peer closed can stay pending on a Windows AF_UNIX socket, so an extension that exited while it loaded, sat idle or shut down was never seen to be gone. The process reaper's exit channel now ends the read: each read waits one second of silence after the exit and then reports io.EOF, the error a closed socket gives, and bytes the process wrote before it exited are read first. Isolated and shared Node processes use the process's channel, each member of a packed process its own socket and the cell's channel. The wire is unchanged.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** Windows
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `108cb7d911` (2026-11-04)
- **Tests:** `coding/extension/host/subprocess/peer_exit_test.go::TestExtensionExitDoesNotDropWhatTheProcessWrote`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/peer_exit_test.go::TestExtensionExitEndsARequestInFlight`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/peer_exit_test.go::TestExtensionExitEndsAnIdleOrLoadingRead`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/peer_exit_test.go::TestIsolatedExtensionExitIsReportedWhenTheSocketCloseIsNotSeen`
- **Release note:** An extension that exits while it loads, sits idle or shuts down no longer leaves the host waiting on its socket: on Windows a socket close can miss a pending read, and the host now ends the read when the extension's process exits, reporting the same transport error as a closed socket.

### BF-1136763

**A lone UTF-16 surrogate is kept, as Pi keeps it, in what an extension is given and in what it hands back: the…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A lone UTF-16 surrogate is kept, as Pi keeps it, in what an extension is given and in what it hands back: the prompt, the system prompt and every system prompt option of `before_agent_start` and the system prompt a handler returns, the tool names, ids and results of the `tool_execution_start`, `tool_execution_update` and `tool_execution_end` events, the entries of `turn_end` and `agent_before_settle`, the model of `model_select`, the servers of `mcp_servers_change`, and the model name of a provider an extension registers.
- **Root cause:** the extension event types and the provider configuration encode and decode their own JSON with encoding/json, which writes each byte of a lone UTF-16 surrogate as U+FFFD and reads its escape as U+FFFD, and no test sent such a string through every event type or through a handler of every SDK
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `11367633b5` (2026-11-13)
- **Tests:** `coding/extension/host/subprocess/event_frame_surrogate_sweep_test.go::TestEventFrameSurrogateSweep`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/prompt_options_surrogate_test.go::TestPromptOptionEditsKeepALoneSurrogate`, `coding/mcp_session_lone_surrogate_test.go::TestAgentSessionMCPToolResultKeepsALoneSurrogate`, `coding/nested_call_lone_surrogate_test.go::TestSessionNestedCallErrorKeepsALoneSurrogate`, `internal/codingagent/extension_provider_surrogate_test.go::TestExtensionProviderRegistrationKeepsALoneSurrogate`
- **Release note:** A lone UTF-16 surrogate is kept, as Pi keeps it, in what an extension is given and in what it hands back: the prompt, the system prompt and every system prompt option of `before_agent_start` and the system prompt a handler returns, the tool names, ids and results of the `tool_execution_start`, `tool_execution_update` and `tool_execution_end` events, the entries of `turn_end` and `agent_before_settle`, the model of `model_select`, the servers of `mcp_servers_change`, and the model name of a provider an extension registers. PiG wrote three U+FFFD in its place in these event frames and read one U+FFFD from a handler's reply. An extension written with the Rust SDK still receives U+FFFD, because that SDK replaces the unit when it reads a frame.

### BF-1147e77

**A line an extension wrote to its stderr or stdout just before pig ended could be lost: with `--mode rpc`…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A line an extension wrote to its stderr or stdout just before pig ended could be lost: with `--mode rpc` (stdin ended, a signal, `ctx.shutdown()`), with Ctrl+C in the interactive mode, when the terminal went away, and when a replaced session's extension was still running at exit, pig stopped the extension processes and exited without waiting for the copy of their output to reach its own stderr and the extension's log.
- **Root cause:** the exit paths assumed that killing a process ends its output, but the host copies that output on its own goroutines, and only Cmd.Wait (the reaper) joins them; Pi writes in its own process, where a write made before exit cannot be lost.
- **User impact:** Lost or altered data
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `1147e7735a` (2026-11-14)
- **Tests:** None recorded.
- **Release note:** A line an extension wrote to its stderr or stdout just before pig ended could be lost: with `--mode rpc` (stdin ended, a signal, `ctx.shutdown()`), with Ctrl+C in the interactive mode, when the terminal went away, and when a replaced session's extension was still running at exit, pig stopped the extension processes and exited without waiting for the copy of their output to reach its own stderr and the extension's log. Seen as a failing listener's `Event handler error (...)` line that was sometimes missing from the output of a docs example. Pig now waits for that copy, for Node, Python, Go and Rust extensions alike, isolated or packed. The wait ends after five seconds for all extension processes of all sessions together, so an extension whose descendant keeps the output open cannot hold pig back; pig then prints one line saying how many extension processes had not finished and that their undelivered output is dropped. The extension's own log file gets the same lines. The ordinary quit paths (print mode, an interactive quit by keys, `/quit`) already waited for the processes and are unchanged.

### BF-114f195

**Chord plugins (internal, the tests' seam): a tree the plugins component's file watcher watches on request…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Chord plugins (internal, the tests' seam): a tree the plugins component's file watcher watches on request (`Plugins.WatchTree`, which only the tests' barrier `pluginstest.Settle` calls) stays watched across discoveries until the component is closed.
- **Root cause:** Plugins.WatchTree is the seam of the tests' barrier (pluginstest.Settle): the barrier has the watcher watch a directory of its own, makes a directory in it and waits until the watcher watches that one, which says every earlier file event was handled. No product path calls WatchTree.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `114f195453` (2026-11-13)
- **Tests:** `chord/nextnode/app/app_web_browser_test.go::TestThePagesLanguageWritesLangAndDirOnTheRootElementFromTheDeviceThenTheUsersPick`, `chord/nextnode/app/reload_rollout_test.go::TestARolloutAcrossHostsEndsTwoRolloutsBackToBackOnTheSecondsCodeThePageFollowingWithoutFailing`, `chord/nextnode/plugins/plugins_plugins_test.go::TestAComponentsDiscoveryKeepsTheTreeItsBarrierWatches`, `chord/nextnode/plugins/plugins_watcher_linux_test.go::TestClosingTheWatcherReleasesTheWatchesOfATreeItWasAskedToWatch`, `chord/nextnode/plugins/plugins_watcher_test.go::TestADiscoveryDropsTheTreeOfAPluginWhoseLinkIsGoneAndKeepsATreeTheWatcherWasAskedToWatch`, `chord/nextnode/plugins/plugins_watcher_test.go::TestATreeTheWatcherWasAskedToWatchStaysWatchedAcrossDiscoveries`, `chord/nextnode/plugins/plugins_watcher_test.go::TestTheBarrierReturnsWhenADiscoveryLandsBetweenItsWatchTreeAndItsDirectory`
- **Release note:** Chord plugins (internal, the tests' seam): a tree the plugins component's file watcher watches on request (`Plugins.WatchTree`, which only the tests' barrier `pluginstest.Settle` calls) stays watched across discoveries until the component is closed. A discovery dropped it with every tree that is no root's, base's or linked plugin's, so the build of an apply that ran beside a test's edit could take the barrier's watch away between the barrier's request and the event it waits for: `TestARolloutAcrossHostsEndsTwoRolloutsBackToBackOnTheSecondsCodeThePageFollowingWithoutFailing` then failed with `timed out after 15s waiting for the watcher to handle a directory made after the edits`, in about one run in ten. No product path calls `WatchTree`: the trees of the roots, of the base code and of linked plugins are watched and released as before.

### BF-1162a57

**A Piglet built with any model API stripped no longer allocates on every model catalog lookup**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A Piglet built with any model API stripped no longer allocates on every model catalog lookup.
- **Root cause:** the catalog tested whether the strip state had changed by comparing a copy of the stripped list against the list it held, and pigstrip.IDs returns a new slice whenever anything is stripped, so the comparison itself allocated; the no-allocation contract of the lookup was only ever tested in a build that strips nothing, where IDs returns nil
- **User impact:** Extra allocation or slower run
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `1162a57f06` (2026-11-16)
- **Tests:** `internal/codingagent/builtin_chat_catalog_test.go::TestBuiltinChatCatalogDoesNotAllocateWhileAnAPIIsStripped`, `internal/codingagent/builtin_chat_catalog_test.go::TestBuiltinChatCatalogListsWhatListModelsLists`, `internal/codingagent/builtin_chat_catalog_test.go::TestBuiltinChatCatalogLookupsRaceAStrip`, `internal/codingagent/builtin_chat_catalog_test.go::TestBuiltinChatCatalogSeesAStripBetweenTwoLookups`, `internal/pigstrip/pigstrip_test.go::TestGenerationChangesOnlyWhenTheStripStateDoes`
- **Release note:** A Piglet built with any model API stripped no longer allocates on every model catalog lookup. The built-in chat catalog asked the strip state for a fresh copy of the stripped API list each time it was read, to see whether the list had changed; it now compares one counter that the strip state advances when it changes, and reads the list only to rebuild. A strip applied after the first lookup (a Piglet's strip list is applied at start-up) is still seen by the next lookup. Stock PiG strips nothing and is unchanged. The bug was present since v0.7.0.

They are now settled at the commit and only wake after the listeners.

### BF-11b199d

**Session lines (and every other JSON.stringify-mode encode) now write ill-formed UTF-8 the way Pi does: one…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** PiG used to write one `\ufffd` escape per bad byte, so `"a\xe2\x82b"` became `"a\ufffd\ufffdb"` where Pi writes `"a�b"`.
- **Root cause:** JSON.stringify of a string decoded from ill-formed UTF-8 writes one raw U+FFFD per WHATWG maximal subpart; PiG's session lines wrote one \ufffd escape per bad byte. The codec now counts one replacement per maximal subpart in every mode, writes it raw in the JSON.stringify mode, and rewrites nested \ufffd escapes to raw there. Marshal and MarshalJS keep the escape form. Session files written before keep their form and read back the same.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `11b199d645` (2026-10-12), `4e17838ae9` (2026-10-12)
- **Tests:** `ai/errors_pool_test.go::TestSafeJsonStringifyPoolDropsLargeBuffers`, `extensions/sdk/json/append_string_swar_test.go::TestAppendStringMatchesBytewise`, `extensions/sdk/json/decode_trusted_test.go::TestUnmarshalTrustedMatchesUnmarshal`, `extensions/sdk/json/decode_trusted_test.go::TestUnmarshalTrustedVerifiesInTests`, `extensions/sdk/json/lw_budget_norace_test.go::TestAppendString200KBudget`, `extensions/sdk/json/lw_budget_norace_test.go::TestEncodeStatePoolDropsLargeBuffers`, `internal/jsonstringify/fast_node_test.go::TestFastPathKeyStackBound`, `internal/jsonstringify/large_object_test.go::TestIsCanonicalAcceptsLargeObjects` and 10 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** Session lines (and every other JSON.stringify-mode encode) now write ill-formed UTF-8 the way Pi does: one raw U+FFFD per WHATWG maximal subpart (what a JavaScript string decoded from those bytes holds, and what JSON.stringify writes). PiG used to write one `\ufffd` escape per bad byte, so `"a\xe2\x82b"` became `"a\ufffd\ufffdb"` where Pi writes `"a�b"`. Nested `\ufffd` escapes from PiG's own types are written raw as well. Session files written before this change keep the old form and read back the same strings. On the extension wire (the codec's `Marshal`/`MarshalJS`), ill-formed UTF-8 also counts one replacement per maximal subpart rather than per byte; the `\ufffd` escape form there is unchanged.

**The Durable core's conversation view follows Pi f3255de7's mount: a second observer of a conversation only…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The Durable core's conversation view follows Pi f3255de7's mount: a second observer of a conversation only loads its own window and takes the one `docs` object of the mount, so attaching to a mounted view spends Pi's microtask passes and the observers of one conversation share their documents; a window the core rejects (a bound that is not an integer, `max` below `min`) reaches the host as the `RangeError` Pi throws.

TestResolveWindow checks the rejection's name.

### BF-123827b

**Go, Rust, Python and Lisp extensions: a bash tool built on `createLocalBashOperations()` now says `The shell…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Go, Rust, Python and Lisp extensions: a bash tool built on `createLocalBashOperations()` now says `The shell exited with code C after S seconds, but background processes it started kept writing output until the timeout.` when a command timed out after its shell had already exited, as Pi 1.5.1 does.
- **Root cause:** The Go, Rust, Python and Lisp SDKs reach the local shell over builtinTool.localExec, whose error reply carried only 'timeout:N'.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `01d8d08b31` (2026-11-09), `123827b998` (2026-11-09)
- **Tests:** `coding/extension/host/subprocess/shell_exit_wire_test.go::TestLocalShellTimeoutReadsAFusedSDKsError`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/shell_exit_wire_test.go::TestShellExitCrossesTheWireAsErrorInfoShellExit`, `test/extension-conformance/builtin_tool_delegate_test.go::TestConformance_BuiltinToolDelegationAcrossSDKs`
- **Release note:** Go, Rust, Python and Lisp extensions: a bash tool built on `createLocalBashOperations()` now says `The shell exited with code C after S seconds, but background processes it started kept writing output until the timeout.` when a command timed out after its shell had already exited, as Pi 1.5.1 does. The local operations of these SDKs reach the host over `builtinTool.localExec`, whose error reply carried only `timeout:N`; it now carries Pi's `shellExit` (the shell's exit code and run time), which the SDK passes on when its exec returns that error unchanged. An error wrapped around it, or a new error with its message, gives the plain `Command timed out after N seconds`, as in Pi.

### BF-154d2c5

**The terminal title that a session sets (the session name, or an extension's title) is written where Pi writes…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The terminal title that a session sets (the session name, or an extension's title) is written where Pi writes it when PiG ends: for a quit by keys (Ctrl+D, Ctrl+C twice, `/quit`) before the "To resume this session" line, and for SIGTERM and SIGHUP before the terminal is restored.
- **Root cause:** Pi's dispose() (agent-session-runtime.ts:415-424) runs session.abort(), session_shutdown, beforeSessionInvalidate (which writes the title through resetExtensionUI) and session.dispose(), and Pi's shutdown() calls it after stop() on a quit (title, then the resume hint) and first on a signal (title, then the terminal restore). pig ran the hook only at Runtime.Close, after Run returned and after the hint. Runtime.EmitQuitShutdown, where the mode calls the dispose, now runs the hook once after session_shutdown; Close runs it only when no dispose did (print and RPC emit through EmitQuitShutdownContext).
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `154d2c5776` (2026-11-16)
- **Tests:** `coding/runtime_quit_invalidate_test.go::TestQuitContextEmitLeavesTheInvalidateHookToClose`, `coding/runtime_quit_invalidate_test.go::TestQuitDisposeRunsBeforeSessionInvalidateAfterSessionShutdown`, `internal/codingagent/interactive_exit_bytes_pty_test.go::TestExitBytesChild`, `internal/codingagent/interactive_exit_dispose_test.go::TestQuitWritesTheTitleInTheDisposeBeforeTheResumeHint`, `internal/codingagent/interactive_exit_dispose_test.go::TestSignalDisposeDoesNotWaitForAnOwnerLoopThatWaitsForItsLock`, `internal/codingagent/interactive_exit_title_pty_test.go::TestExitTitleIsWrittenInTheDisposeAtPisPlace`
- **Release note:** The terminal title that a session sets (the session name, or an extension's title) is written where Pi writes it when PiG ends: for a quit by keys (Ctrl+D, Ctrl+C twice, `/quit`) before the "To resume this session" line, and for SIGTERM and SIGHUP before the terminal is restored. PiG wrote it only when the runtime closed, after the exit had restored the terminal and, for a quit, after the resume hint, so a terminal or a recording of the exit saw the title last. A signal that arrives while the quit's last steps are running, or a terminal that has stopped taking output, no longer holds the title write or the exit behind each other. Present in v0.3.0 through v0.7.0 (checked by tag: each runs the title hook only when the runtime closes).

### BF-155d0f3

**In RPC mode, SIGTERM or SIGHUP during a tool call likewise stops the run while the `session_shutdown`…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** In RPC mode, SIGTERM or SIGHUP during a tool call likewise stops the run while the `session_shutdown` handlers finish without waiting, as Pi does: a handler that throws no longer lets the run persist the tool result and send another provider request before the exit.
- **Root cause:** Pi's RPC signal handler kills tracked children and awaits runtimeHost.dispose on its one event loop (rpc-mode.ts:366-376,726-744). The killed bash call's exit is I/O, so the run reaches its tool result only after a session_shutdown handler awaits a timer or I/O. PiG's run went on concurrently: with a throwing handler it persisted the tool result and an assistant turn and sent a second provider request before exiting. RPC mode now registers the same termination prelude as print mode: Session.HoldAgentEvents from the moment the signal arrives until a handler reports its yield or the Session is disposed.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `155d0f33a0` (2026-10-11), `329c4e7f7e` (2026-10-11), `34f7594aa5` (2026-10-11)
- **Tests:** `coding/cli/print_signal_shutdown_test.go::TestPrintModeSignalDeliversSessionShutdown`, `coding/cli/rpc_signal_disposal_test.go::TestRPCSignalDisposalHoldsTheRunLikePisEventLoop`, `internal/codingagent/extension_ui_phase_shutdown_test.go::TestAwaitedExtensionPhaseWithoutShutdownReturnsItsResult`, `internal/codingagent/extension_ui_phase_shutdown_test.go::TestNewSessionEndedByShutdownIsNotAFatalRuntimeError`, `internal/codingagent/extension_ui_phase_shutdown_test.go::TestShutdownDuringAwaitedExtensionPhaseDoesNotWaitForAHandlerThatIgnoresCancellation`, `internal/codingagent/extension_ui_phase_shutdown_test.go::TestShutdownDuringAwaitedExtensionPhaseEndsThePhase`, `test/parity/scenarios/extensions-runtime/73-shutdown-from-session-before-fork.toml`, `test/parity/scenarios/extensions-runtime/73-shutdown-from-session-before-switch.toml` and 1 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** In RPC mode, SIGTERM or SIGHUP during a tool call likewise stops the run while the `session_shutdown` handlers finish without waiting, as Pi does: a handler that throws no longer lets the run persist the tool result and send another provider request before the exit.

### BF-15a5c0b

**The Kimi Code, Meta and xAI device logins judge the verification URI the way Pi does, and Meta and xAI open…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The Kimi Code, Meta and xAI device logins judge the verification URI the way Pi does, and Meta and xAI open the URL Pi opens.
- **Root cause:** A differential test runs Pi's three private functions in Node (testdata/trusted_urls.mjs cuts them out of the pinned source) over 91 URLs and found 42 differences. Pig used url.Parse, which keeps the URL as received and accepts what the WHATWG parser rejects, and rejects forms the WHATWG parser accepts: - 'https:example.com', 'https:/example.com', 'https:///example.com' and backslash forms are valid in Pi and were refused; - ports above 65535, 'https://:443', numeric hosts out of range, a space in the host were refused by Pi and accepted; - Meta and xAI returned the URL as written, where Pi returns the href (lowercase scheme and host, default and empty port and empty userinfo dropped, empty…
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `15a5c0b670` (2026-10-09), `7c4d874438` (2026-10-09)
- **Tests:** `ai/githubcopilot_oracle_test.go::TestGitHubCopilotHelpersMatchPi`, `ai/trusted_url_oracle_test.go::TestTrustedVerificationURLsMatchPi`
- **Release note:** The Kimi Code, Meta and xAI device logins judge the verification URI the way Pi does, and Meta and xAI open the URL Pi opens. A `https:host` or backslash form is read as a URL; a port above 65535, an out-of-range numeric host, or a space in the host is refused. The opened URL is normalized as `new URL` does (lowercase scheme and host, default port and empty userinfo dropped, an empty path becomes `/`) instead of being echoed as received.

### BF-15b13fc

**A compaction, branch summary or bug report summary no longer fails with "Summarization failed: 401…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A compaction, branch summary or bug report summary no longer fails with "Summarization failed: 401 Unauthorized" when the short-lived token it started with (a GitHub Copilot API token lives about 30 minutes) expires before its last request: after a retry's backoff, or on a later chunk.
- **Root cause:** A compaction, branch summary or bug report on a Session the CLI builds pinned the credential it resolved when it started into every request it made, so a retry after a backoff, or a later chunk, sent a derived token (GitHub Copilot's lives about 30 minutes) after it had expired and got the provider's 401: "Auto-compaction failed: Summarization failed: 401 Unauthorized".
- **User impact:** Credential or permission exposure
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `15b13fcae5` (2026-11-11)
- **Tests:** `coding/session_summary_auth_refresh_test.go::TestAutoCompactionSurfacesRefreshFailureOnce`, `coding/session_summary_auth_refresh_test.go::TestCompactionResolvesCredentialWhenItStartsFreshAndExpired`, `coding/session_summary_auth_refresh_test.go::TestSummarizationRequestResolvesNoCredentialForARuntimeSession`, `coding/session_summary_auth_refresh_test.go::TestSummaryAttemptsEachSendAFreshCredentialAfterExpiry`
- **Release note:** A compaction, branch summary or bug report summary no longer fails with "Summarization failed: 401 Unauthorized" when the short-lived token it started with (a GitHub Copilot API token lives about 30 minutes) expires before its last request: after a retry's backoff, or on a later chunk. A Session started from the command line resolved its credentials once, when the summary began, and sent that token with every request of it. Each request now resolves its own credentials when it is sent, as a turn does and as Pi's sessions do.

### BF-160d95a

**In RPC mode, a run that an extension command starts with `sendMessage` or `sendUserMessage` now emits…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** In RPC mode, a run that an extension command starts with `sendMessage` or `sendUserMessage` now emits `agent_start` after the command's response, as in Pi, when the command is written with the Go, Python or Rust SDK, not only on Node.
- **Root cause:** Fix 2: rpcAdmission holds the start while a command's handler runs (rpcCommandRuns). The transport reports the handler's phase in frame order (invocation.RunPhase, Conn.reportRequestPhase): a sendMessage or sendUserMessage call resumes its parent request, because the runtime reports the call's own suspension before it sends the call, and a later blocked or suspended state suspends it. The start proceeds once the command answers (after its response is written) or awaits. In-process commands are not tracked and keep the hop placement, so TestRPCInlineCommandTurnStartOrderMatchesPi is unchanged. A Node handler that awaits something other than a host call after a send that follows its first…

### BF-165cf58

**`pig package publish --to npm` and `pig piglet publish --to npm` no longer run an `npm` that the published…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Windows' `cmd.exe` could pick a Package's own `npm.cmd` ahead of the author's npm, and a relative `npmCommand` was resolved inside the Package directory.
- **Root cause:** The bash tool on Windows puts the shell in a job object. When the shell exits, `processGroupMayHoldOutput` asks Windows whether the job still has processes (`QueryInformationJobObject`, `JobObjectBasicAccountingInformation`). If the answer is zero, `childwait.waitIdle` waits for the output pipe to reach EOF with no further bound, because an empty job means no process can still hold the pipe.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** Windows
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `2e0f88f794` (2026-10-06, #160), `9a95b36b11` (2026-10-06, #162), `ba9c37b247` (2026-10-06, #171), `c019ea9155` (2026-10-06, #163), `165cf5884d` (2026-10-07, #180), `9b63b2bc4e` (2026-10-07, #176), `ce8587ef40` (2026-10-07, #179)
- **Tests:** `coding/cli/extension_cache_gc_binary_test.go::TestEverySessionModeStartsTheAutomaticExtensionCacheCollection`, `coding/cli/extension_cache_gc_test.go::TestAutomaticExtensionCacheGCCancelledAtTheLastEntryWritesNoMarker`, `coding/cli/extension_cache_gc_test.go::TestAutomaticExtensionCacheGCCancelledWritesNoMarker`, `coding/cli/extension_cache_gc_test.go::TestAutomaticExtensionCacheGCMarkerSuppressesTheNextRunWithinTheInterval`, `coding/cli/extension_cache_gc_test.go::TestAutomaticExtensionCacheGCRecordsFailureInsteadOfPrinting`, `coding/cli/extension_cache_gc_test.go::TestAutomaticExtensionCacheGCWritesMarkerWhenAnEntryIsBusy`, `coding/cli/extension_cache_gc_test.go::TestAutomaticExtensionCacheGCWritesNoMarkerOnRealFailure`, `coding/cli/extension_cache_gc_test.go::TestExtensionsCacheStatsShowsTheLastAutomaticPruneFailure` and 100 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** `pig package publish --to npm` and `pig piglet publish --to npm` no longer run an `npm` that the published directory contains. PiG finds npm in the absolute directories on `PATH`, so publishing from inside a Package that ships its own `npm` works and uses your npm (or resolves a relative `npmCommand` against the directory you run `pig` in) and starts that file. Before, Windows' `cmd.exe` could pick a Package's own `npm.cmd` ahead of the author's npm, and a relative `npmCommand` was resolved inside the Package directory.

### BF-1662063

**When a provider's server resets or closes the connection before it answers, the retry notice and the turn's…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** When a provider's server resets or closes the connection before it answers, the retry notice and the turn's error now name what happened the same way every time, as Pi does: `Connection error.: read ECONNRESET` for a reset and `Connection error.: other side closed (UND_ERR_SOCKET)` for a close.
- **Root cause:** net/http returns the request body write's error and drops the read side's, and the error mapping named only the "write" and "read" operations, not the vectored "writev" of a request body
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `1662063665` (2026-11-13)
- **Tests:** `ai/socket_failure_test.go::TestSocketFailureReportsTheConnectionsEndInNodesOrder`, `ai/socket_failure_test.go::TestSocketFailureWaitEndsWhenTheConnectionIsClosed`, `ai/socket_failure_test.go::TestSocketFailureWriteWaitsForAReadThatHasNotBegun`, `ai/socket_failure_test.go::TestSocketFailureWriteWaitsForTheReadInFlight`
- **Release note:** When a provider's server resets or closes the connection before it answers, the retry notice and the turn's error now name what happened the same way every time, as Pi does: `Connection error.: read ECONNRESET` for a reset and `Connection error.: other side closed (UND_ERR_SOCKET)` for a close. A reset that arrived while the request was still being sent was shown, depending on timing, as a bare `Connection error.`, as `other side closed (UND_ERR_SOCKET)`, as `write ECONNRESET` or as `write EPIPE`; with a large request that was nearly every time. The turn was retried in each case and still is.

### BF-16c1901

**A full disk or a killed process while pig saved `settings.json` or the project trust store could leave the…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A full disk or a killed process while pig saved `settings.json` or the project trust store could leave the file empty, and the next change then saved it with that one setting or decision alone, so every other setting or trust decision was lost.
- **Root cause:** settings.json and trust.json were written with os.WriteFile, which truncates the file before it writes, so a write that failed after it began left an empty or cut-short file and the next change was saved on top of that.
- **User impact:** Lost or altered data
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `16c1901a48` (2026-11-14)
- **Tests:** None recorded.
- **Release note:** A full disk or a killed process while pig saved `settings.json` or the project trust store could leave the file empty, and the next change then saved it with that one setting or decision alone, so every other setting or trust decision was lost. Both files are now replaced as a whole through a temporary file in the same directory, so where one can be replaced a failed write leaves the old file untouched; the bytes written are the same. Where one of them cannot be replaced atomically, for example a single file mounted into a container, pig writes it in place as before, and a failure half way through that write can still leave the file empty or cut short.

### BF-16f41f0

**The provider bridge (`pig` `--provider-bridge`), the Durable core's `model_context` effect and an extension…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The provider bridge (`pig` `--provider-bridge`), the Durable core's `model_context` effect and an extension host's `modelStream` call now send a `start` event whose partial is the pending, empty message the provider built, as Pi does (the durable generation task reads the same pending partial but skips content-less partials before its observer, so it publishes no start partial): Pi attaches its consumer before any response I/O can complete.
- **Root cause:** Not recorded.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `16f41f045e` (2026-11-09, #443)
- **Tests:** `coding/cli/provider_bridge_test.go::TestProviderBridgeStartIsSerializedBeforeTheResponseFillsItsPartial`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/model_stream_attach_test.go::TestModelStreamForwardsStartBeforeTheResponseFillsItsPartial`, `durable/core/driver/model_test.go::TestModelContextSendsStartBeforeTheResponseFillsItsPartial`, `durable/harness/observe_response_test.go::TestObserveResponseSkipsTheStartEventWhoseProviderPartialHasNoContentYet`
- **Release note:** The provider bridge (`pig` `--provider-bridge`), the Durable core's `model_context` effect and an extension host's `modelStream` call now send a `start` event whose partial is the pending, empty message the provider built, as Pi does (the durable generation task reads the same pending partial but skips content-less partials before its observer, so it publishes no start partial): Pi attaches its consumer before any response I/O can complete. Each created the provider's stream and read it from an ordinary goroutine, so under load the goroutine could start reading after the provider had filled the shared partial, and a `start` event reached the wire carrying the finished message (`toolUse`, the whole content and the final usage) where Pi sends `stopReason: "pending"` and no content. Each now creates the stream and reads it inside one stream continuation, as the Agent does; event content, order, cancellation and errors are unchanged.

### BF-1724c9e

**Two pig processes that reach the same `auth.json` through different paths, such as an agent directory whose…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Two pig processes that reach the same `auth.json` through different paths, such as an agent directory whose `auth.json` is a symlink to a shared file, now take one lock instead of two, so they no longer refresh the same single-use OAuth token at the same time and fail with `invalid_grant`.
- **Root cause:** The auth lock resolved the file with filepath.EvalSymlinks. On Windows that expands 8.3 short names (RUNNER~1 -> runneradmin) and looks up a component a '..' cancels, where Node's fs.realpath (what proper-lockfile and Pi main use) keeps the spelling and resolves the path first. The walk moves to internal/noderealpath so pilock can use it; codingagent keeps its callers. The five new testenv.Symlink callers are file links and join the registry. The OAuth abort fixture writes its started path as a JSON (JavaScript) string literal.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** Windows
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `1724c9e834` (2026-11-05), `72e19b38b8` (2026-11-06)
- **Tests:** `ai/auth_storage_lock_error_upstream_test.go::TestAuthStorageLockErrorIsProperLockfileErrorUpstream`, `ai/auth_storage_lock_error_upstream_test.go::TestFileModelsStoreLockErrorIsProperLockfileErrorUpstream`, `internal/codingagent/session_continue_test.go::TestSessionCwdMatches_ResolvesSymlinks`, `internal/noderealpath/noderealpath_test.go::TestSyncFollowsADirectoryLink`, `internal/noderealpath/noderealpath_test.go::TestSyncResolvesDotSegmentsBeforeWalking`, `internal/noderealpath/realpath_windows_test.go::TestVolumeGUIDPathClassification`, `internal/noderealpath/win32_test.go::TestNodeRealpathWin32KeepsComponentSpelling`, `internal/noderealpath/win32_test.go::TestNodeRealpathWin32MatchesNode` and 4 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** Two pig processes that reach the same `auth.json` through different paths, such as an agent directory whose `auth.json` is a symlink to a shared file, now take one lock instead of two, so they no longer refresh the same single-use OAuth token at the same time and fail with `invalid_grant`. The lock of `auth.json`, `models.json` and `mcp-auth.json` now follows symlinks to the real file, as Pi main does (D236), and resolves the path as Node's `fs.realpath` does: a `..` step cancels a directory that need not exist, and on Windows the case and 8.3 short names (`RUNNER~1`) of components that are not links stay as given, so a lock error names the path as Pi's does.

### BF-1886bcb

**`--mode json` no longer writes what an extension's `session_shutdown` handler emits after `agent_settled`…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** `--mode json` no longer writes what an extension's `session_shutdown` handler emits after `agent_settled`: the `entry_appended` line for `pi.appendEntry`, the `session_info_changed` line for `pi.setSessionName` and the `message_start` / `message_end` lines for `pi.sendMessage` are saved in the session file and not written, as in Pi, which detaches the JSON stream before it runs `session_shutdown` handlers.
- **Root cause:** the normal teardown detached the JSON writer after closing the runtime (session_shutdown), and the entry_appended line was written outside the subscription without checking that the writer was detached
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `1886bcbfd3` (2026-11-17)
- **Tests:** None recorded.
- **Release note:** `--mode json` no longer writes what an extension's `session_shutdown` handler emits after `agent_settled`: the `entry_appended` line for `pi.appendEntry`, the `session_info_changed` line for `pi.setSessionName` and the `message_start` / `message_end` lines for `pi.sendMessage` are saved in the session file and not written, as in Pi, which detaches the JSON stream before it runs `session_shutdown` handlers. The stream ends with `agent_settled`, in a normal run and after a termination signal; lines already queued still reach a slow reader, and an extension error from the handler still goes to stderr. The bug has been in every release since v0.3.0.

### BF-18e1649

**A `message_start`, `turn_end` or `agent_end` handler that edits the event's message in place and returns…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A `message_start`, `turn_end` or `agent_end` handler that edits the event's message in place and returns nothing now changes the message the next handlers, the saved session entry and the next provider request hold, as it does in Pi, in every extension SDK: the `message` of a `turn_end` event and a member of its `toolResults`, a message of an `agent_end` event's `messages`, and a user or system message at `message_start`.
- **Root cause:** message_end moves onto {_pigEventEdits:[{at,message}], _pigEventResult}, the pair message_start, turn_end and agent_end will carry. _pigMessageEndMessage, _pigMessageEndResult and MessageEndResponsePayload are removed; every SDK sends the new pair and the host reads it.
- **User impact:** Lost or altered data
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `10c7dc1da2` (2026-11-16), `18e1649ef2` (2026-11-16), `6f3ca3d155` (2026-11-16), `75f10dda50` (2026-11-16)
- **Tests:** `coding/extension/host/subprocess/event_edits_test.go::TestAgentEndReplyEditsTheMessageAtItsIndex`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/event_edits_test.go::TestAgentEndReplyRefusesAMisfitAndAppliesNone`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/event_edits_test.go::TestMessageStartReplyEditsAUserMessageAndTheEventsAssistantMessage`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/reply_unwrap_test.go::TestEventReplyRefusesEditsThatDoNotFitTheEventAndAppliesNone`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/reply_unwrap_test.go::TestMessageEndReplyWithAMessageEditsTheEventsMessage`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/reply_unwrap_test.go::TestNoEditReplyIsUnwrappedWithoutAllocation`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/reply_unwrap_test.go::TestReplyUnwrapAgreesWithTheStrictDecode`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/reply_unwrap_test.go::TestResultMemberNamesAreTheWrappersJSONTags` and 5 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** A `message_start`, `turn_end` or `agent_end` handler that edits the event's message in place and returns nothing now changes the message the next handlers, the saved session entry and the next provider request hold, as it does in Pi, in every extension SDK: the `message` of a `turn_end` event and a member of its `toolResults`, a message of an `agent_end` event's `messages`, and a user or system message at `message_start`. An edit of the assistant message at `message_start` reaches the later handlers of that event only, as in Pi, where the event holds a copy of the partial. Until now the edit stayed in the handler's own copy of the event and was lost, for every out-of-process handler of these events, in every extension SDK. Each SDK sends back the messages as the handler left them when they differ from the ones it received, and the host refuses a malformed edit before it applies any. The loss was present in every release since v0.3.0.

### BF-18e3b43

**After an answer, interactive mode no longer draws three more frames that repaint nothing and only move and…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** After an answer, interactive mode no longer draws three more frames that repaint nothing and only move and hide the cursor (two direct renders at the end of the turn and one requested by `agent_settled`).
- **Root cause:** After each answer PiG wrote three more frames that repaint nothing and only move and hide the cursor: two direct renders at the end of the turn (the pending message refresh and the turn flush, each after the turn had already rendered) and a RequestRender from agent_settled, 16 ms later. The extra frames made a harness that waits for output silence wait longer (interactive session wall 581 vs 512 ms for Pi-Bolt 1.2.1) and wrote 29 bytes per answer.
- **User impact:** Wrong display

### BF-1a6b1ab

**A tool whose name, description or parameter schema holds a lone UTF-16 surrogate now reaches the provider…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A tool whose name, description or parameter schema holds a lone UTF-16 surrogate now reaches the provider, the session file, RPC output and an HTML export as Pi writes it.
- **Root cause:** An earlier change made the tool definitions of three API kinds write a lone surrogate as its escape in MarshalJSON, one type at a time, and left the tip red. Each of those types also has a MarshalJSONTo, which the request encoder calls first and which still wrote U+FFFD, so the two methods of one type disagreed and the request was right only through the second encode. Mistral's tool definition was not changed, and since a declaration is now read with the unit kept, its one U+FFFD became three.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `1a6b1ab3ed` (2026-11-13), `e95b1a4f11` (2026-11-13)
- **Tests:** `agent/system_message_surrogate_test.go::TestStoredSystemMessageKeepsAToolsLoneSurrogate`, `ai/marshaler_census_test.go::TestEveryMarshalerWritesALoneSurrogateAsItsEscape`, `ai/providers/bedrock/bedrock_payload_oracle_test.go::TestBedrockConversePayloadMatchesPi`, `ai/providers/bedrock/bedrock_request_body_oracle_test.go::TestBedrockRequestBodyMatchesPi`, `ai/tool_schema_surrogate_test.go::TestToolParametersWithoutRecordedOrderKeepALoneSurrogate`, `ai/tool_schema_surrogate_test.go::TestToolSchemaJSONKeepsALoneSurrogate`, `ai/tool_surrogate_wire_test.go::TestCalledToolNameKeepsALoneSurrogateOfTheStream`, `ai/tool_surrogate_wire_test.go::TestToolLoneSurrogatesReachTheWireAsPi` and 6 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** A tool whose name, description or parameter schema holds a lone UTF-16 surrogate now reaches the provider, the session file, RPC output and an HTML export as Pi writes it. A JavaScript, Python or Lisp extension can register such a tool, and so can a Go extension that builds the string. PiG wrote U+FFFD in the unit's place (three for a name or a description, one inside the schema), so two tools whose names differed only in that unit reached the provider under one name, a property name no longer matched its `required` entry, and a call the model made by that name ended in `Tool ... not found`. Now the request of the Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, Azure OpenAI Responses, Google Generative AI, Mistral and Bedrock kinds holds the unit as the `\uXXXX` escape `JSON.stringify` writes, in the tools it declares and in a history that names a called tool or holds the unit in a call's arguments, also when the body is written from a payload a Go `OnPayload` hook handed back; the system message's session line and its RPC lines hold the same escape. The name of a called tool is read with the unit kept from the Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, Azure OpenAI Responses, Google Generative AI and Mistral streams, so the call finds its tool. A session Pi wrote with the escape is read and sent with it; a session an earlier PiG wrote with U+FFFD is sent as it is. ECMAScript specifies that `JSON.stringify` writes a lone surrogate as its escape, and Anthropic's prompt caching documentation says a cache hit needs an identical prompt prefix. No provider documents whether it accepts a tool name or description that holds such an escape, and this was not tried against a live provider. The Google Vertex and OpenAI Codex requests go through the same encoders as the Google Generative AI and OpenAI Responses ones and were not compared with Pi's. Not changed: an extension in a subprocess still receives U+FFFD in the unit's place in what the host sends it (so a payload its `before_provider_request` handler returns holds U+FFFD), tools of an MCP server are still read with U+FFFD, and so is the name of a called tool in the Bedrock stream.

### BF-1b699a5

**extensions: a session leaked one goroutine and the state of the replaced generation (about 14 KiB for an…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** extensions: a session leaked one goroutine and the state of the replaced generation (about 14 KiB for an extension in its own process, about 30 KiB for a cell of two) for every `/reload` of an unchanged subprocess extension, until the extension's process ended.
- **Root cause:** A reload keeps the process of an unchanged extension and runs its factory again in it. Each generation it replaced left one goroutine that waited for that process to exit, holding the generation's state: the connection loop of a Node extension in its own process (it waited before it removed the stderr log), and the watcher of a packed cell's process state (Node, Go, Python, Rust and Lisp cells). A session that reloaded n times held n of them, about 14 KiB each for an isolated extension, until the process ended. They also removed the stderr log the moment the process died, before the crash report of the running generation kept it, so the report of a process that had been reloaded did not…
- **User impact:** Crash, hang or runaway process
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `1b699a5442` (2026-11-12)
- **Tests:** None recorded.
- **Release note:** extensions: a session leaked one goroutine and the state of the replaced generation (about 14 KiB for an extension in its own process, about 30 KiB for a cell of two) for every `/reload` of an unchanged subprocess extension, until the extension's process ended. A reload keeps that process and runs the extension's factory in it again; each generation it replaced kept a goroutine that waited for the process to exit. The same goroutines removed the extension's stderr log the moment the process died, so the crash notice of a process that had been reloaded did not name its log. The end of a process is now handled once: over a hundred reloads the host's goroutines do not grow and its live heap stays within 512 KiB, for every SDK (Node, Go, Python, Rust, Lisp), isolated and packed, and the crash notice names the log as it does for a process that was never reloaded. Present in releases 0.3.0 to 0.7.0.

### BF-1c1b349

**A write to a terminal that went away (`EIO` after a hang-up, `EPIPE`, `ENOTCONN`, `ENOTTY`) now ends the…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A write to a terminal that went away (`EIO` after a hang-up, `EPIPE`, `ENOTCONN`, `ENOTTY`) now ends the session with exit 129, as Pi's stdout error listener does, instead of being discarded while the session keeps running (#397).
- **Root cause:** Pi adds an error listener to process.stdout and process.stderr that exits 129 through emergencyTerminalExit when the error is EIO, EPIPE, ENOTCONN or ENOTTY. ProcessTerminal.write discarded its error, so a session on a hung-up or revoked terminal kept running. The handler runs the exit once: the exit's own restore writes fail on the same terminal.
- **User impact:** Crash, hang or runaway process
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `1c1b349dbd` (2026-11-02, #397)
- **Tests:** None recorded.
- **Release note:** A write to a terminal that went away (`EIO` after a hang-up, `EPIPE`, `ENOTCONN`, `ENOTTY`) now ends the session with exit 129, as Pi's stdout error listener does, instead of being discarded while the session keeps running (#397).

### BF-1ceb9fb

**A title an extension sets (`ctx.ui.setTitle`, or the session name an extension sets), the OSC 52 sequence of…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A title an extension sets (`ctx.ui.setTitle`, or the session name an extension sets), the OSC 52 sequence of an extension's `copyToClipboard` and the progress indicator's keepalive are written between frames now, as in Pi: Pi writes each of them with `terminal.write` (the keepalive from a `setInterval` callback) on its one event loop, so each is before the bytes of a frame or after them.
- **Root cause:** the process terminal's own writes (title, progress keepalive) and the clipboard helper's direct OSC 52 write take no lock of the renderer, and the callers that run off the owner loop (an extension's host call, the keepalive's ticker) were not handed to the loop that writes the frames, as Pi's terminal.write calls are on its one event loop
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `1ceb9fb95a` (2026-11-16)
- **Tests:** `internal/codingagent/terminal_write_order_test.go::TestExtensionClipboardOSC52FromAHostGoroutineIsWrittenBetweenFrames`, `internal/codingagent/terminal_write_order_test.go::TestExtensionSessionNameTitleFromAHostGoroutineIsWrittenBetweenFrames`, `internal/codingagent/terminal_write_order_test.go::TestExtensionTitleFromAHostGoroutineIsWrittenBetweenFrames`, `internal/codingagent/terminal_write_order_test.go::TestOwnerLoopClipboardOSC52IsWrittenWhereItIsMade`, `internal/codingagent/terminal_write_sites_test.go::TestEveryTerminalWriteOutsideTheFrameIsOrdered`, `tui/terminal_progress_keepalive_order_test.go::TestProgressKeepaliveIsBeforeAFrameOrAfterIt`
- **Release note:** A title an extension sets (`ctx.ui.setTitle`, or the session name an extension sets), the OSC 52 sequence of an extension's `copyToClipboard` and the progress indicator's keepalive are written between frames now, as in Pi: Pi writes each of them with `terminal.write` (the keepalive from a `setInterval` callback) on its one event loop, so each is before the bytes of a frame or after them. PiG wrote them from the extension host's call or the keepalive's ticker goroutine, so they could land between two writes of a frame, and the race detector reported the writer. The interactive mode's loop writes them now. Released in v0.7.0 and earlier.

### BF-1d5b4bb

**The Go SDK's start-order tests no longer fail on a loaded machine since v0.5.2 (a test-claim fix: the SDK is…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The Go SDK's start-order tests no longer fail on a loaded machine since v0.5.2 (a test-claim fix: the SDK is unchanged).
- **Root cause:** the tests asserted first-statement order, which is more than the SDK's invocation-order contract, and a goroutine descheduled between the release of its place and its handler's first statement is overtaken
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `1d5b4bb0fe` (2026-11-18)
- **Tests:** `extensions/sdk/request_start_order_test.go::TestEventAndCommandHandlersStartInArrivalOrder`, `extensions/sdk/request_start_order_test.go::TestOvertakenHandlerKeepsItsInvocationPlace`, `extensions/sdk/tool_prepare_arguments_test.go::TestToolCallHandlersStartInArrivalOrder`
- **Release note:** The Go SDK's start-order tests no longer fail on a loaded machine since v0.5.2 (a test-claim fix: the SDK is unchanged). The SDK guarantees the order in which handlers are invoked: a handler is invoked only after every earlier request's handler was invoked or its request ended without one. The tests asserted the order of the handlers' first statements, which is more than that, and a goroutine the operating system holds back after its place was released is overtaken by the handlers behind it, so one of 300 runs failed under one-CPU pressure. The tests now read the order where the SDK keeps it, and a new test holds one handler back to show that the invocation order stays intact while the first statements do not.

### BF-1e2d25f

**A `turn_end` handler's in-place edit of `event.message` (an `agent_end` handler's of `event.messages`) no…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A `turn_end` handler's in-place edit of `event.message` (an `agent_end` handler's of `event.messages`) no longer races with the consumer of `Session.Events`, and no longer reaches the `message_end` and `turn_end` events published before it.
- **Root cause:** ReplaceMessageInPlace (introduced by 0bed50c8ff) overwrites the members of the one message value the transcript, the saved entry and the message_end and turn_end events hold, and Session.publishAgentEvent sent those events to the consumer of Events, which reads them on its own goroutine, with that same value; a handler's edit at turn_end ran while the consumer read the events published before it.
- **User impact:** Lost or altered data
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `1e2d25f161` (2026-11-20)
- **Tests:** `agent/event_view_test.go::TestEventViewIsNotChangedByAReplacementOfTheMessage`, `agent/event_view_test.go::TestEventViewIsRaceFreeWithAReplacementOfTheMessage`, `coding/session_event_view_test.go::TestEventsConsumerReadsMessagesAsPublishedAcrossLaterInPlaceEdits`, `test/extension-conformance/in_place_message_events_test.go::TestInPlaceMessageEventEditsMatchPi`
- **Release note:** A `turn_end` handler's in-place edit of `event.message` (an `agent_end` handler's of `event.messages`) no longer races with the consumer of `Session.Events`, and no longer reaches the `message_end` and `turn_end` events published before it. The session publishes those two events with the message as it was when the event was published, which is what Pi's listeners, running at the event, see; the transcript, the saved entry, the events published after the edit and the payloads of the extensions follow the edit as before. The consumer reads on its own goroutine and held the one message object the edit overwrites: the race detector reported it (`go test -race`, `TestInPlaceMessageEventEditsMatchPi/subprocess-node-packed/turn_end/deep`), a message serialized during the edit could mix the old and the edited content, and the edit of a custom message clears and refills its member map, a map read while it is written, which is a fatal error in Go.

### BF-1f4ce56

**On Windows, saving `auth.json`, the settings, trust, keybindings and MCP files, or any other file pig writes…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** On Windows, saving `auth.json`, the settings, trust, keybindings and MCP files, or any other file pig writes through a temporary file, now leaves the whole security descriptor of the file as it was, as Pi's in-place write does.
- **Root cause:** the helper left the security descriptor of a replaced file to ReplaceFileW and copied only the DACL with its protected flag, and no test compared the whole descriptor before and after a write on Windows
- **User impact:** Credential or permission exposure
- **Platform:** Windows
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `1f4ce560a8` (2026-11-15), `950803e7b7` (2026-11-15)
- **Tests:** `internal/atomicfile/atomicfile_windows_test.go::TestWindowsReplaceKeepingBackupFinishesAReplacementThatStoppedHalfWay`, `internal/atomicfile/atomicfile_windows_test.go::TestWindowsReplaceKeepingBackupRestoresTheOriginalWhenItCannotFinish`, `internal/atomicfile/carry_access_test.go::TestCarryAccessChoosesTheCallsByWhatTheReadBackShows`, `internal/atomicfile/carry_access_test.go::TestCarryAccessReturnsAFailedReadBack`, `internal/atomicfile/carry_decision_test.go::TestWriteFileWritesInPlaceWhereTheTemporaryFileCannotTakeTheAccess`, `internal/atomicfile/descriptor_matrix_windows_test.go::TestWindowsInheritanceDoesNotReachAProtectedFileAfterAWrite`, `internal/atomicfile/descriptor_matrix_windows_test.go::TestWindowsSecurityDescriptorMatrix`, `internal/atomicfile/replace_backup_test.go::TestCarryVerdict` and 7 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** On Windows, saving `auth.json`, the settings, trust, keybindings and MCP files, or any other file pig writes through a temporary file, now leaves the whole security descriptor of the file as it was, as Pi's in-place write does. The replacement kept the owner-only access of a credential file only as far as `ReplaceFileW` merged it: it always marked the file as auto-inherited and could rewrite the inherited flag of entries or add explicit copies of inherited ones, so a login or token refresh could change who may open `auth.json`. The access (the entries with their flags, and the protected flag) is now put on the temporary file before anything is written to it and read back, and again after the replacement, which puts the old file back and fails if the access still differs; a file system that cannot take it gets the in-place write, as before. Run on NTFS on the GitHub Windows runner by the main-side branch that carries the same files (run 43709055821); no other file system has been run (divergence D651).

### BF-1f7fa2f

**In print and JSON mode, an extension in its own Node process no longer runs its callbacks with a stale ctx…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** In print and JSON mode, an extension in its own Node process no longer runs its callbacks with a stale ctx when a later extension's handler awaits a timer or I/O.
- **Root cause:** Pi's runner awaits each extension's handler in turn on one event loop (runner.ts:1089-1116). When a later extension's session_shutdown or agent_settled handler awaits a timer or I/O, that loop runs the immediate or timer an earlier extension's handler queued, with a live ctx, before print mode invalidates the runner (agent-session-runtime.ts:404-410, agent-session.ts:1393-1406). With isolated Node processes the earlier process waited for the host's next step after answering (), so its callbacks ran only after invalidate, or never, because the host stopped the process first. Packed processes share one loop and matched Pi.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `311609427b` (2026-10-07), `382156cdb7` (2026-10-07), `49798a80d2` (2026-10-07), `8723a419d7` (2026-10-07), `8d990c5d54` (2026-10-07), `a79de03e7f` (2026-10-07), `1f7fa2fe22` (2026-10-09)
- **Tests:** `coding/cli/resource_loader_gaps_upstream_test.go::TestPrintModeInvalidDiscoveredFileURLFailsBind`, `coding/extension/host/inproc/upstream_scoped_models_test.go::TestContextThinkingLevelReadsTheBoundRuntimeLive`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/runtime_node_loop_turn_test.go::TestNodeLoopTurnRunsQueuedImmediatesBeforeLaterFrames`, `coding/extension/widget_placement_test.go::TestPowerShellToolInputIsTheBashInputShape`, `coding/mcpext/extension_test.go::TestAgentSessionMCPHoldsTheFirstPromptForServersWithDirectToolsOnlyUpToTheStartupWait`, `coding/session_extend_resources_test.go::TestSessionExtendsItsLoaderAfterExtensionReplacement`, `coding/session_extend_resources_test.go::TestSessionExtendsItsLoaderFromResourcesDiscover`, `coding/session_extend_resources_test.go::TestSessionWithNoResourcesDoesNotEmitResourcesDiscover` and 9 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** In print and JSON mode, an extension in its own Node process no longer runs its callbacks with a stale ctx when a later extension's handler awaits a timer or I/O. Pi runs every extension on one event loop, so the immediate or timer that one extension's `session_shutdown` or `agent_settled` handler queues runs while the next extension's handler waits, before the runner is invalidated. The Node runtime now reports such a wait with a `loop_turned` notification, which the host forwards to every other Node process as its next step. Packed extensions already shared one loop and behave as before; RPC and interactive mode are unchanged.

### BF-202b8f1

**On arm64 and other CPUs with a fused multiply-add, the OKHSL saturation of a color (used when generating the…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** It differed from Pi's in the last bit for about 9% of sRGB colors.
- **Root cause:** rgbToOkhsl assigns k1 := 0.8 * c0 and adds it in k1 + (1 - k1/cMid) * chroma. Assigning a product does not round it in Go: on arm64 the compiler fused 0.8 * c0 into that addition (FMADD), so ColorToOkhsl's saturation, which the system theme generator reads, differed from Pi's oklab.ts:225-226 in the last bit for 1523533 of the 16.7M sRGB colors (633339 of those then match Pi exactly; the others differ from Pi through Go's Pow/Cbrt/Atan2 as well).
- **User impact:** Wrong display
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `202b8f1943` (2026-10-13), `7633906d03` (2026-10-13), `a00dbe6901` (2026-10-13), `bd3e8ab24b` (2026-10-13)
- **Tests:** `ai/device_code_poll_oracle_test.go::TestDeviceCodePollDeadlineRoundsTheProductLikePi`, `ai/oauth_expiry_arithmetic_test.go::TestBuiltinOAuthExpiryUsesJavaScriptArithmetic`, `ai/openai_codex_http_error_test.go::TestCodexHTTPErrorResetMinutesRoundTheProductFirst`, `internal/codingagent/cache_warmer_test.go::TestCacheWarmingExpectedSavingsRoundsTheProductLikePi`, `internal/codingagent/pig_egg3d_test.go::TestPig3dFlightHomeOffsetsRoundLikePi`, `internal/codingagent/radius_login_oracle_test.go::TestRadiusLoginMenuRendersLikePi`, `internal/jsmath/log_oracle_test.go::TestLogMatchesNode`, `tui/colors_test.go::TestColorToOkhslRoundsTheChromaStopProduct`

### BF-20aee29

**The crash notice prints the year of a crash time the way Node's toLocaleString does: unpadded, and counted…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The crash notice prints the year of a crash time the way Node's toLocaleString does: unpadded, and counted back from 1 for years before 1 CE.
- **Root cause:** interactive-mode.ts:1222 prints `new Date(crash.timestamp).toLocaleString()`. The Go notice used the layout "1/2/2006, 3:04:05 PM", whose year is zero padded to four digits and signed before 1 CE; en-US toLocaleString prints the Gregorian era year unpadded and, before 1 CE, counted back from 1 without a sign ("4/15/151", "10/13/1721" for 1721 BCE). enUSDateTime now builds the string. A crash record's year is the current one in practice, so this shows only for a forged or damaged record. The locale stays en-US: Node uses the process locale (LANG=de_DE gives "31.12.1969, 16:00:00"), which is not modelled and not recorded as a divergence pending the owner.
- **User impact:** Crash, hang or runaway process
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `20aee29744` (2026-10-11)
- **Tests:** `internal/codingagent/crash_notice_date_oracle_test.go::TestCrashNoticeTimeMatchesToLocaleString`
- **Release note:** The crash notice prints the year of a crash time the way Node's toLocaleString does: unpadded, and counted back from 1 for years before 1 CE.

### BF-20b9d05

**`pig piglet build` planned a Common Lisp extension as packed into the Piglet Binary but did not embed its…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** `pig piglet build` planned a Common Lisp extension as packed into the Piglet Binary but did not embed its SBCL image: it warned `[not-embedded]`, a Piglet with no other member to fuse failed with "nothing to embed or fuse", and a Piglet with a fused member built a Binary that exited at startup with `baked Piglet Binary binary-packed extensions do not match its plan: missing [<extension>]`.
- **Root cause:** The component plan records a Lisp extension as binary-packed, but buildNativeArtifact had no packed-lisp case: the cell fell to the default branch, which warned [not-embedded] and embedded nothing. The Binary then refused to start because its plan named an extension its cells lacked, and a Piglet with no other member to fuse failed with "nothing to embed or fuse". Build the SBCL image through runtimecell.BuildLispPackedCell, as the Go and Rust cells are built, and embed it; the startup path already starts an embedded packed-lisp cell.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `20b9d0592b` (2026-11-05)
- **Tests:** `coding/pigletbuild/lisp_binary_test.go::TestPigletBinaryRunsItsLispExtension`
- **Release note:** `pig piglet build` planned a Common Lisp extension as packed into the Piglet Binary but did not embed its SBCL image: it warned `[not-embedded]`, a Piglet with no other member to fuse failed with "nothing to embed or fuse", and a Piglet with a fused member built a Binary that exited at startup with `baked Piglet Binary binary-packed extensions do not match its plan: missing [<extension>]`. The build now builds the Lisp image and embeds it, the Binary starts it without SBCL, and a Piglet whose only extensions are Lisp extensions builds.

### BF-20bdd2c

**Markdown text that holds a lone UTF-16 surrogate (a paragraph, heading, emphasis, code span, link, table…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Markdown text that holds a lone UTF-16 surrogate (a paragraph, heading, emphasis, code span, link, table cell, list item, quote or link reference definition) now measures and wraps as Pi does: the unit is one code point of no width instead of three replacement characters, and a reference definition whose label holds one still resolves.
- **Root cause:** The stand-in scheme left the inline lexer reading each lone surrogate as three U+FFFD, so link reference definitions stopped resolving (the block pass stored a stand-in label) and a destination printed a private-use character; text that already held a stand-in fell back to U+FFFD too, and paragraphs, headings, emphasis, code spans, links, tables, lists and quotes with a lone surrogate differed from Pi on every build.
- **User impact:** Wrong output or ordering
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `20bdd2c341` (2026-11-06)
- **Tests:** `internal/jsstring/codepoints_test.go::TestCodePointStringAndAppend`, `internal/jsstring/codepoints_test.go::TestCodePointsKeepLoneSurrogates`, `internal/jsstring/codepoints_test.go::TestCodePointsOfAnAdjacentPairOfHalvesStayTwo`, `tui/markdown_inline_surrogates_oracle_test.go::TestMarkdownInlineLoneSurrogatesMatchPi`
- **Release note:** Markdown text that holds a lone UTF-16 surrogate (a paragraph, heading, emphasis, code span, link, table cell, list item, quote or link reference definition) now measures and wraps as Pi does: the unit is one code point of no width instead of three replacement characters, and a reference definition whose label holds one still resolves.

### BF-211af49

**`/hotkeys` lists extension shortcuts, and the extension shortcut listener tries them, in the order of Pi's…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** `/hotkeys` lists extension shortcuts, and the extension shortcut listener tries them, in the order of Pi's `getShortcuts` Map (load order, registration order, a re-registered key keeps its first position) instead of path then key / Go map order (`coding/extension/host/inproc/runner.go` OrderedShortcuts, `internal/codingagent/interactive_hotkeys.go`, `interactive_helpers.go`; `TestRunnerShortcutsMatchPi` now compares Map order, regression `TestHotkeysCommandListsExtensionShortcutsInRegistrationOrder`).
- **Root cause:** Runner.OrderedShortcuts returns getShortcuts' entries in Map iteration order (first-registration position, last value); Shortcuts is the map view. /hotkeys sorted by extension path then key and the listener ranged a Go map, so Pi's registration order and first-match-wins for overlapping spellings of one key were lost.
- **User impact:** Wrong output or ordering

### BF-2173cc1

**A Node extension's handler that wrote the session (`pi.setSessionName`, `pi.setLabel`, `pi.sendMessage`)…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A Node extension's handler that wrote the session (`pi.setSessionName`, `pi.setLabel`, `pi.sendMessage`) after an `await` read back a session log without the entry it had just written (`ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()` still ended in the earlier entry), and the replicated log later lost all but one entry, where Pi's in-process log shows every write to the next read.
- **Root cause:** The runtime applied the host's state push for a write after the push for the next write, because the receive loop that held the first push (handed to it while it waited, or taken from its queue) is unable to read it during the synchronous call that follows an `await`.
- **User impact:** Lost or altered data
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `2173cc13ed` (2026-11-07)
- **Tests:** `test/extension-conformance/replicated_accessors_test.go::TestNodeReplicatedWritesReadBackAfterAwait`, `test/extension-conformance/replicated_accessors_test.go::TestReplicatedAccessorsReadYourWritesAcrossSDKs`
- **Release note:** A Node extension's handler that wrote the session (`pi.setSessionName`, `pi.setLabel`, `pi.sendMessage`) after an `await` read back a session log without the entry it had just written (`ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()` still ended in the earlier entry), and the replicated log later lost all but one entry, where Pi's in-process log shows every write to the next read. Every handler of an extension that registers `pi.onLoaded` is such a handler: its requests first await the loaded handlers. The runtime applied the host's state push for a write after the push for the next write, because the receive loop that held the first push (handed to it while it waited, or taken from its queue) is unable to read it during the synchronous call that follows an `await`. The runtime now applies the state in the order the host sent it.

### BF-21c27bf

**A user message, a branch or compaction summary, a custom message, a skill invocation, the startup changelog…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A user message, a branch or compaction summary, a custom message, a skill invocation, the startup changelog, the `/hotkeys` block, the text a slash command appends and an extension's Markdown view no longer keep the memos a streamed Markdown holds for its next delta.
- **Root cause:** A user, summary, custom or skill message is complete when it is built, but its Markdown never called FinishStreaming, so the memos that only speed up the next streamed delta stayed for the life of the message. Each owner now finishes its Markdown at construction.
- **User impact:** Wrong display
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `21c27bf578` (2026-10-30), `6c29071cad` (2026-10-31)
- **Tests:** None recorded.
- **Release note:** A user message, a branch or compaction summary, a custom message, a skill invocation, the startup changelog, the `/hotkeys` block, the text a slash command appends and an extension's Markdown view no longer keep the memos a streamed Markdown holds for its next delta. They arrive whole and never call `FinishStreaming`, so the wraps, inline renderings and resume point stayed for the life of the message: a 1.2 KB user message retained 17.5 KB, and a transcript of 10,000 of them about 175 MB. Each now finishes its Markdown when it builds it: a user message keeps 9.2 KB (its 6.1 KB of padded, colored rows are the rest) and a boxed message 16 to 18 KB instead of 21 to 23 KB. The rows are unchanged.
