### BF-7c140b3

**Starting the interactive mode no longer writes cursor placements between its frames or frames of its own that…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A terminal that answers nothing used to see the header frame, two bare cursor placements (`ESC[<n>G ESC[?25l`), the window title, and the same again after each later frame: `frame, cursor, cursor, title, frame, cursor, frame, cursor, cursor`; it now sees Pi's `frame, cursor, title, frame, cursor, frame, cursor`.
- **Root cause:** PiG painted a frame right after binding the session and painted each startup notice, warning and status line at once, where Pi only requests a frame and lets the next one carry them; it also took a turn of the event loop for every `session_start` handler, because the registry could not tell a handler that returns without awaiting (the built-in MCP one) from one that can wait, and no test compared the kinds of write around the startup frames, only the bytes up to the first frame
- **User impact:** Crash, hang or runaway process
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `5edf81f2ab` (2026-11-17), `7c140b3c41` (2026-11-17), `b4b67844c7` (2026-11-17)
- **Tests:** `coding/extension/factoryload/session_start_without_await_test.go::TestSessionStartRegisteredAsReturningWithoutAwaitingDoesNotMakeTheRunnerAwait`, `coding/extension/factoryload/session_start_without_await_test.go::TestSessionStartReturningWithoutAwaitFallsBackToOnSessionStart`, `coding/extension/handler_await_test.go::TestHandlerRegistrationSurvivesRemovalAndReplacement`, `coding/extension/handler_await_test.go::TestHasEventHandlersThatMayAwaitAsksTheRegistrationOfEachHandler`, `coding/extension/host/inproc/registry_test.go::TestHasHandlersThatMayAwaitLeavesOutTheHandlersThatReturnWithoutAwaiting`, `coding/mcpext/session_start_without_await_test.go::TestBuiltinMCPSessionStartHandlerReturnsWithoutAwaiting`, `coding/piglet/session_start_without_await_test.go::TestPigletSessionStartHandlerReturnsWithoutAwaiting`, `internal/codingagent/bind_may_pend_test.go::TestBindMayPendAsksWhetherAHandlerCanPend` and 6 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** Starting the interactive mode no longer writes cursor placements between its frames or frames of its own that Pi does not write. A terminal that answers nothing used to see the header frame, two bare cursor placements (`ESC[<n>G ESC[?25l`), the window title, and the same again after each later frame: `frame, cursor, cursor, title, frame, cursor, frame, cursor, cursor`; it now sees Pi's `frame, cursor, title, frame, cursor, frame, cursor`. The start now builds the header, binds the extensions and paints one frame at the end of its start, as Pi does, and the notices that follow it (resource diagnostics, the model fallback message, the crash notice) each request a frame. A plain start also no longer waits on the built-in MCP extension: its `session_start` handler returns without awaiting what it starts, as Pi's does, and an extension handler can now say the same of itself, so the session binds without taking a turn of the event loop. A handler of a subprocess extension, which can always wait, keeps the wait.

### BF-7c24a92

**extensions: when the Node process that several TypeScript or JavaScript extensions share was killed or…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** extensions: when the Node process that several TypeScript or JavaScript extensions share was killed or crashed, an extension could be reported twice: first as disabled (`packed member connection closed; /reload restarts it`), then as crashed and restarting, so one exit read as an error that asked for `/reload` and a warning that the extension restarts by itself.
- **Root cause:** A member of a Node cell whose connection closed was disabled at once, with "packed member connection closed; /reload restarts it", and the watcher of the process then restarted the cell and reported the same member again, as restarting. What a user saw depended on which of the two the host saw first: two, three or four notices for a cell of two, four in 86 of 100 kills, and for each doubled member an error that told them to run /reload beside a warning that the extension restarts by itself.
- **User impact:** Crash, hang or runaway process
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `7c24a924a9` (2026-11-12)
- **Tests:** `coding/extension/host/subprocess/retention_dead_share_reload_test.go::TestReloadOfAKilledNodeCellRefusesItsUnreapedProcess`
- **Release note:** extensions: when the Node process that several TypeScript or JavaScript extensions share was killed or crashed, an extension could be reported twice: first as disabled (`packed member connection closed; /reload restarts it`), then as crashed and restarting, so one exit read as an error that asked for `/reload` and a warning that the extension restarts by itself. How many notices appeared depended on whether the host noticed the closed connections or the exited process first: two, three or four for two extensions, four in 86 of 100 kills. The host now reports the exit once for each extension, as restarting, in the order the extensions load, whichever it notices first. The extensions of a Go, Python or Rust cell that stops are reported in load order too, where the order varied from one exit to the next. Present in releases 0.3.0 to 0.7.0.

### BF-7d225e5

**`pig login` and `pig logout` end on Ctrl+C, SIGTERM and SIGHUP at the provider menu, the logout menu and…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** `pig login` and `pig logout` end on Ctrl+C, SIGTERM and SIGHUP at the provider menu, the logout menu and inside a provider's login.
- **Root cause:** discoverAuthContributionsFor (auth_contributions.go:83) installed signal.NotifyContext for SIGINT and SIGTERM and held it until the contributions closed, so the runtime delivered both signals to a context nothing read; the login ran under context.Background (auth_commands.go:397), so nothing ended it.

Ctrl+C and SIGTERM were ignored there before; the process now ends by the signal after its cleanup, as Pi's does. `pig auth login` restores the terminal before ending on SIGTERM and SIGHUP (it left the terminal raw), and Ctrl+C still prints "Login cancelled." and exits 1. Affects 0.5.0 through 0.7.0.

### BF-7d34ee2

**durable harness: `ConversationTranscript.LoadEarlier` and `FillGap` waited for good once an entry loader had…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** durable harness: `ConversationTranscript.LoadEarlier` and `FillGap` waited for good once an entry loader had panicked: the load that call ran stayed registered and never ended.
- **Root cause:** The call whose loader did not return now settles its load on the way out: the callers that share it fail with "ConversationTranscript: the entry loader panicked", the load is unregistered, and the panic goes on to the caller whose call ran the loader. The path of a loader that returns is unchanged.
- **User impact:** Crash, hang or runaway process
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `7d34ee2c6c` (2026-11-12)
- **Tests:** `durable/harness/transcript_loader_panic_test.go::TestConversationTranscriptFailsTheCallersSharingALoadWhoseLoaderPanicked`, `durable/harness/transcript_loader_panic_test.go::TestConversationTranscriptLoadsAgainAfterItsLoaderPanicked`
- **Release note:** durable harness: `ConversationTranscript.LoadEarlier` and `FillGap` waited for good once an entry loader had panicked: the load that call ran stayed registered and never ended. A load whose loader does not return is now settled, as Pi's shared promise settles when its loader throws: the calls that share it fail with `ConversationTranscript: the entry loader panicked`, the next call loads again, and the panic still reaches the caller whose call ran the loader.

### BF-7d798ce

**fix(testenv): the shared Cargo target is keyed by the absolute path of the SDK as well as its lock**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** fix(testenv): the shared Cargo target is keyed by the absolute path of the SDK as well as its lock
- **Root cause:** rustc bakes env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR") into a test binary, and Cargo reuses a cached binary whenever the sources' mtimes are older than it, whatever the checkout's path. SharedCargoTargetDir hashed only the package name and the lock and manifest contents, so a second checkout (a copy, a worktree, a clone older than the cached build) took the first one's target and ran the binary that opens the first checkout's fixtures: Type.json not found once that checkout was deleted (TestTypeEngineVectorsThroughTheHost/rust). A copy of a checkout kept the deleted path baked in, reproduced with two paths and identical mtimes. The hash now includes the absolute path of each input.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `7d798ced1d` (2026-10-31)
- **Tests:** `internal/testenv/cargotarget_test.go::TestSharedCargoTargetDirIsKeyedByTheAbsoluteRootAsWellAsTheContents`, `internal/testenv/cargotarget_test.go::TestSharedCargoTargetDirResolvesARelativeRootToTheSameTarget`, `test/extension-conformance/type_engine_vectors_host_test.go::TestTypeEngineVectorsThroughTheHost`

### BF-7db4bd0

**Resizing an image sends the smaller of the PNG and the JPEG at the configured quality instead of the PNG…**

- **Source:** A fix Pi shipped that PiG ported
- **Symptom:** Resizing an image sends the smaller of the PNG and the JPEG at the configured quality instead of the PNG whenever it fit, so a photo that needs resizing no longer goes out as a multi-MB PNG that makes the request fail or time out.
- **Root cause:** A resize returned the PNG whenever it fit, even when the JPEG was many times smaller, so photos went out as multi-MB PNGs. Each size step now tries the smaller of the PNG and the JPEG at the configured quality first (the PNG on a tie), then the other, then the lower JPEG qualities. TestResizePreservesAlpha no longer requires a PNG for a translucent image, as in Pi.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `7db4bd0867` (2026-10-30, #11551)
- **Tests:** `internal/imageprocessing/image_processing_upstream_test.go::TestFirstFittingCandidatePrefersTheSmallerOfPNGAndJPEG`, `internal/imageprocessing/image_processing_upstream_test.go::TestResizeImagePicksJPEGOverLargerPNGForPhotos`, `internal/imageprocessing/images_test.go::TestPNGCandidateKeepsAlpha`, `internal/imageprocessing/images_test.go::TestResizePreservesAlpha`
- **Release note:** Resizing an image sends the smaller of the PNG and the JPEG at the configured quality instead of the PNG whenever it fit, so a photo that needs resizing no longer goes out as a multi-MB PNG that makes the request fail or time out. Screenshots where the PNG is smaller still go out as PNG, and the lower JPEG qualities are tried only when neither fits. Carried forward from Pi e7a0df27 (earendil-works/pi#11551), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin.

### BF-7db4e68

**The alternate screen's viewport accessors (`ViewportTop`, `IsFollowingOutput`, `ScrollBy`, `ScrollToTop`…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The alternate screen's viewport accessors (`ViewportTop`, `IsFollowingOutput`, `ScrollBy`, `ScrollToTop`, `ScrollToBottom`) read the layout of the last frame under the renderer's lock.
- **Root cause:** ViewportTop, IsFollowingOutput, ScrollBy, ScrollToTop and ScrollToBottom read currentLayout through getPrimaryScrollView without t.mu, while a frame (doRender) stores a new layout under t.mu. An extension's tuiAlt host call reaches IsFollowingOutput on its own goroutine, so TestTuiAltScreenAcrossSDKs/ subprocess-python reported a data race between tui_alt_screen.go:1055 (frame write) and :400 (read) in the gate's confrace1 run. made the width and height an atomic snapshot but left the layout pointer unsynchronised.
- **User impact:** Wrong display
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `7db4e68fc4` (2026-10-31)
- **Tests:** `test/extension-conformance/tui_alt_screen_test.go::TestTuiAltScreenAcrossSDKs`, `tui/tui_alt_screen_test.go::TestAltScreenViewportAccessorsDoNotRaceWithAFrame`
- **Release note:** The alternate screen's viewport accessors (`ViewportTop`, `IsFollowingOutput`, `ScrollBy`, `ScrollToTop`, `ScrollToBottom`) read the layout of the last frame under the renderer's lock. An extension's `tuiAlt` host call reads them from its own goroutine while a frame stores a new layout, and the race detector reported the Python SDK's conformance row.

### BF-7dc9b09

**`-e <local Package>` now contributes its prompts, skills and themes, loaded before the project, user and…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** `-e <local Package>` now contributes its prompts, skills and themes, loaded before the project, user and Package resources, so they win same-name collisions as in Pi.
- **Root cause:** A -e local Package contributed only extensions. Pi's resource loader resolves the -e sources as temporary Packages and merges their prompts, skills and themes before the project, user and Package resources (cliEnabledPrompts/Skills/Themes), so they win same-name collisions and survive --no-prompt-templates, --no-skills and --no-themes.

They survive `--no-prompt-templates`, `--no-skills` and `--no-themes`. A directory with an `extensions`, `skills`, `prompts` or `themes` directory is a Package and no longer fails to load as an extension.

### BF-7ddb7c1-2

**`chord/nextnode/plugins`: the copy of a Go core facet's keyed member a plugin reads (`Files.summary`) is…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** `chord/nextnode/plugins`: the copy of a Go core facet's keyed member a plugin reads (`Files.summary`) is applied in the order the Go host committed.
- **Root cause:** The documents are the first frame the Go side sends, the commits made while they were read follow them (before, a commit that reached the Node host in the same chunk as the documents was applied first and then retired or overwritten by them), a slot that ends while it is read is read again, and a document change refused because the object ended is not reported as a fatal error of the Node host.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `7ddb7c1a27` (2026-11-10)

- **Release note:** `chord/nextnode/plugins`: the copy of a Go core facet's keyed member a plugin reads (`Files.summary`) is applied in the order the Go host committed. The documents are the first frame the Go side sends, the commits made while they were read follow them (before, a commit that reached the Node host in the same chunk as the documents was applied first and then retired or overwritten by them), a slot that ends while it is read is read again, and a document change refused because the object ended is not reported as a fatal error of the Node host.

### BF-7e16053

**`pig install /abs/path` (and `~/path` or a `file://` URL) records the path as you typed it in `packages[]`**

- **Source:** A Pi defect that PiG fixed first (divergence D215)
- **Symptom:** `pig install /abs/path` (and `~/path` or a `file://` URL) records the path as you typed it in `packages[]`.
- **Root cause:** pig install recorded every local Package relative to the agent directory as spelled at install, as Pi does. An install through a symlinked PIG_HOME wrote ../../../../../../pkgsrc/my-pkg, and a start through another spelling at another depth resolved it to nothing: the Package's tools vanished with one stderr line.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Pi issue:** none recorded
- **Removed when Pi fixes it:** Pi stores an absolute local path as typed, or the owner reverses the decision. Then the branch, the call-site marker and the tests' D215 cases go.
- **Fix commits:** `4cf8dea070` (2026-10-29, #389), `7e160533d7` (2026-10-29), `9a388567fd` (2026-10-30), `b368be57f5` (2026-10-30, #389)
- **Tests:** `coding/cli/package_commands_test.go::TestNormalizePackageSourceForSettings_UsesScopeBase`, `coding/cli/package_local_path_test.go::TestInstalledAbsoluteLocalPackageResolvesThroughAnotherAgentDirSpelling`, `coding/cli/package_local_path_test.go::TestStartupWarnsAboutAConfiguredLocalPackageThatDoesNotExist`, `coding/cli/port_wave_10_package_command_paths_test.go::TestPortWave10PackageCommandPaths`, `internal/packagemanager/package_manager_ops_gaps_test.go::TestPackageManagerAddAndRemoveSourceInTheScopeSettings`, `test/extension-conformance/session_graph_lisp_test.go::TestSessionGraphLispPackedAcrossSDKs`, `test/extension-conformance/session_graph_test.go::TestSessionGraphDefaultPackageManagerAcrossSDKs`
- **Release note:** `pig install /abs/path` (and `~/path` or a `file://` URL) records the path as you typed it in `packages[]`. It was stored relative to the agent directory as spelled at install, so a later start through another spelling of `PIG_HOME` (a symlinked `~/.local/share/...` directory, a synced config) resolved it to nothing and the Package's tools disappeared with only a stderr line. A relative path is still stored relative to the settings directory. Running `pig install <absolute path>` again rewrites an existing entry for the same Package (D215, #389).

### BF-7e42a6a

**CSS module mappings are what Node's `vm` gives, as Pi's (key order of integer-like names, no `__proto__` key…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** CSS module mappings are what Node's `vm` gives, as Pi's (key order of integer-like names, no `__proto__` key, template-literal names): `ScopeCSSModule` now takes the Node options and a context (the component's builds share one Node subprocess for the mappings), and `ScopedCSS.Classes` is the mapping's JSON text; a CSS module is decoded as UTF-8 like `TextDecoder`.
- **Root cause:** Each BuildFacet started its own evaluator and buildAll runs every facet at once, so a cold build of N plugins with CSS modules started N Node processes (a web build with a .module.css took 52.7 ms against 1.9 ms with a plain .css). The Plugins component now owns one evaluator, started by the first CSS module and ended by Close; a standalone BuildFacet still starts its own. A ctx that ends an evaluation kills the process, the build is aborted (not failed), and the next evaluation starts another; a failed process no longer fails the later ones.
- **User impact:** Wrong output or ordering
- **Platform:** All platforms

### BF-7e9a4bc

**Chord: an abort listener that ran leaves every source it listened to, and an emptied listener set is dropped**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A context that outlived its waits (a link's or a host's) kept every wait that had ended by an abort, and the memory of its busiest moment.
- **Root cause:** OnAbort registers a listener on every cancel that can abort its context: the context itself and each parent and signal behind it. A cancel clears the set of its own source only, so a listener that ran stayed in the sets of the others until its waiter called stop, and a set emptied by stop kept the buckets it grew to. A source that outlives its waits (a link's or a host's context) kept every wait that ended by an abort, and the size of its busiest moment.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `7e9a4bc8f5` (2026-11-15)
- **Tests:** `chord/context/abort_listener_leak_test.go::TestOnAbortLeavesNothingHeldByALongLivedContext`
- **Release note:** Chord: an abort listener that ran leaves every source it listened to, and an emptied listener set is dropped. Before, a context that outlived its waits (a link's or a host's) kept every wait that had ended by an abort, and the memory of its busiest moment.

### BF-7eb7d29

**The model picker (`/model`) now shows a catalog-refresh timeout or failure as soon as it happens**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The model picker (`/model`) now shows a catalog-refresh timeout or failure as soon as it happens.
- **Root cause:** Pi's Container.render calls child.render(width) for every child on every frame, so a Pi component cannot be stale because of its parent. Pig's per-child cache and the D91 settled scan asked a child that embeds a Container only for its own flag, so a change beneath it that did not call its Invalidate was never drawn: ModelSelectorComponent.SetError and SetStatus (after a catalog-refresh timeout the screen kept "Refreshing model catalogs..."), SettingsList.UpdateValue and FilterableList.SetCursor.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `7eb7d29c3f` (2026-11-09)
- **Tests:** `tui/child_cache_contract_test.go::TestAParentContainerShowsWhatAnyExportedMutatorChanged`, `tui/child_cache_contract_test.go::TestEveryExportedComponentTypeIsInTheCacheContract`, `tui/child_cache_contract_test.go::TestModelSelectorRefreshTimeoutShowsInTheNextFrame`, `tui/child_cache_contract_test.go::TestModelSelectorSetErrorReachesAParentContainersRender`, `tui/child_cache_contract_test.go::TestSettingsListUpdateValueReachesAParentContainersRender`
- **Release note:** The model picker (`/model`) now shows a catalog-refresh timeout or failure as soon as it happens. It kept showing `Refreshing model catalogs...` until the next key press, because the screen reused the picker's last drawing; `SettingsList` value updates and `FilterableList` cursor moves had the same hole. A component that embeds a container now tells its parent about a change anywhere beneath it, so the per-child render cache can no longer show a child that Pi would redraw.

### BF-7f2c05b

**A `ChordError` of code `invalid` from a failed args, result, state or input check carries TypeBox's whole…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A `ChordError` of code `invalid` from a failed args, result, state or input check carries TypeBox's whole error objects as `details` (keyword, schemaPath, instancePath, params and message), as Pi's does; it carried only instancePath and message.
- **Root cause:** Pi's assertValid throws invalid with the first three Value.Errors as details: keyword, schemaPath, instancePath, params and message of each. PiG kept only instancePath and message, so a caller reading ChordError.Details of a failed args, result, state or input check saw less than Pi shows. internal/typebox.ValueError now carries the keyword, the schema path of the failing schema and the params of every keyword TypeBox reports, and the walker threads the schema path the way the engine does (properties/<key>, items/<index>, anyOf/<index>, then, else, $ref restarting at #). chord/host assertValid builds the details from them in Pi's member order.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `7f2c05b082` (2026-10-24)
- **Tests:** `internal/typebox/value_oracle_test.go::TestValueMatchesTypeboxOnCases`
- **Release note:** A `ChordError` of code `invalid` from a failed args, result, state or input check carries TypeBox's whole error objects as `details` (keyword, schemaPath, instancePath, params and message), as Pi's does; it carried only instancePath and message.

### BF-7fc9ec3

**The pi-env daemon on macOS: a small reply (an `lstat`, a ping) could come after megabytes of queued command…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The pi-env daemon on macOS: a small reply (an `lstat`, a ping) could come after megabytes of queued command output, more than a client buffers, where Pi's daemon answers between output frames.
- **Root cause:** The writer buffered up to 1 MiB of frames and flushed only when the queue ran empty, so a reply queued behind a full buffer; Pi flushes after every frame (output.rs, frame.rs write_frame). The inherited stdin and stdout were also blocking descriptors: a goroutine reading or writing one held its scheduler slot until sysmon took it back, up to 10 ms, so a request that arrived with every slot held waited that long before a worker ran it, and 1.4 to 2 MB of command output flowed past the reply meanwhile (macOS CI, 64 KiB pipes: 2,162,688 bytes against the 1,600,000 bound). Serve now moves pipes and sockets it is given onto a poller duplicate and restores the mode on return.
- **User impact:** Wrong output or ordering
- **Platform:** macOS
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `7fc9ec3654` (2026-11-08)
- **Tests:** `env/daemon/pollable_unix_test.go::TestPollableLeavesOtherFilesAlone`, `env/daemon/pollable_unix_test.go::TestPollableMovesInheritedPipesIntoThePoller`
- **Release note:** The pi-env daemon on macOS: a small reply (an `lstat`, a ping) could come after megabytes of queued command output, more than a client buffers, where Pi's daemon answers between output frames. The writer now flushes after every frame as Pi's does instead of holding up to 1 MiB, and the daemon waits on its inherited stdin and stdout through the runtime poller, so a request that arrives while the runtime is busy with the output no longer waits up to 10 ms for a worker.

- **Release note:** Quitting while an OAuth token refresh is in flight no longer loses the new token. If pig exited after the token request went out but before the new token was written, `auth.json` kept the refresh token the provider had already spent and the next request failed with `invalid_grant`; an RPC client that stopped pig right after startup, while the background catalog refresh refreshed an expired login, hit this. Interactive, print, JSON and RPC mode now wait for a refresh that has started to be saved before the process exits, with no timeout beyond the 15 s refresh and the 30 s auth lock wait; a second signal exits at once in RPC and print mode. The wait comes before pig stops its extensions, and a refresh that has started (a subprocess extension provider's, in the catalog refresh or at request time, or the Radius gateway's) is no longer cut or discarded when its caller is cancelled, as Pi main does (D237).

### BF-8013c00

**A resumed session that could not make its private copy of the session file (no copy-on-write clone, no room…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A resumed session that could not make its private copy of the session file (no copy-on-write clone, no room or no right to write the copy, a failed first write) read its entries back from the live file, so a change another program made to the file afterwards reached the session: a branch, a tree, an export, a fork, or the prompt after a /tree switch could show other bytes, an error, or a prompt that had lost turns.

Such a session now reads the whole file once and keeps its entries in memory, as Pi does, and never reads the file again.

### BF-8048c85

**Tool-call header argument preview no longer splits a character: `truncateArg` (`tui/tool_execution.go`) cut…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Tool-call header argument preview no longer splits a character: `truncateArg` (`tui/tool_execution.go`) cut to `max-1` bytes, so a non-ASCII argument longer than the budget ended in a half character that the JSON quoting turned into a visible U+FFFD before the ellipsis (`text:"ééé…é�…"`); it now backs up to the start of a character.
- **Root cause:** JSON.parse keeps a member of any type, so Pi keeps a session message whose member has another type than Pi writes, in its entries, branch, context, projection and RPC get_messages (session-manager.ts parseSessionEntryLine, buildSessionContext). PiG's AgentMessage decode failed on such a member and dropped the message from the context, the projection and get_messages: a string timestamp, numeric content, a text block with a numeric text, a usage count written "1", isError "no", a numeric or missing role, and so on.
- **User impact:** Wrong display
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `6a6fffa638` (2026-10-10), `8048c851e3` (2026-10-11)
- **Tests:** `agent/message_json_number_spelling_test.go::TestAgentMessageDecodeKeepsANonNumberWhereAnIntegerIsExpected`, `agent/message_json_test.go::TestAgentMessageJSONRejectsInvalidUnion`, `agent/message_type_mismatch_test.go::TestDecodedMessageKeepsMembersOfAnyType`, `agent/provider_content_block_decode_test.go::TestUnknownContentBlockCostsOnlyThatBlock`, `internal/codingagent/session_context_settings_test.go::TestGetSessionContextSettingsBoundaries`, `internal/codingagent/session_messagefor_cache_test.go::TestMessageForReportsAnUnparseableEntryWithoutParsingItAgain`, `test/longsession/session_oracle_test.go::TestSessionManagerMatchesPi`, `test/parity/scenarios/rpc/58-rpc-session-wrong-typed-members.toml` and 1 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** Tool-call header argument preview no longer splits a character: `truncateArg` (`tui/tool_execution.go`) cut to `max-1` bytes, so a non-ASCII argument longer than the budget ended in a half character that the JSON quoting turned into a visible U+FFFD before the ellipsis (`text:"ééé…é�…"`); it now backs up to the start of a character. Regression `TestFormatToolArgsTruncatesAtACharacterBoundary` (red before: é, 日 and 🙂 at four byte offsets; both mutations, no back-up and cutting at `max`, red); `./tui -race` green (1,139 s). Found by scanning production code for byte `len()` comparisons against limits. `HeaderForTool`'s fallback (`FormatToolArgs`: `name path:"x"`) is PiG's own format for a tool with no builtin formatter and no definition, where Pi renders `formatToolCallWithArgs`; that mismatch is the open "tool card with no definition" ruling request in questions/lg-help-4.md.

### BF-8070fcc

**OpenAI Codex and Azure OpenAI requests parse their URL as fetch does again: an upper-case scheme, a space or…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** OpenAI Codex and Azure OpenAI requests parse their URL as fetch does again: an upper-case scheme, a space or a dot segment in a configured base URL reaches the server as the serialized URL, and the fragment is not sent.
- **Root cause:** An earlier change routed Codex and Azure through newFetchRequest, which hands its input to nodeurl.RequestURL as an already-serialized href. Codex's resolveCodexUrl text is not serialized, so a base URL like HTTP://host went out with scheme HTTPS-cased ('fetch failed'), a space went out raw, and an unparsable path sent its fragment. undici's Request parses the input first: newFetchRequest now does (TypeError 'Failed to parse URL from'), drops the fragment for the global fetch, and refuses credentials with fetch's TypeError. The openai SDK callers (completions, responses incl. Azure, openrouter-images) report any of these as 'Connection error.'; Codex, which calls fetch itself…
- **User impact:** Credential or permission exposure
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `8070fcc38b` (2026-10-10)
- **Tests:** `ai/fetch_request_url_test.go::TestCodexAndAzureRequestTargetIsParsedLikeFetch`, `ai/fetch_request_url_test.go::TestCodexRequestTargetDropsTheFragmentOfAnOpaquePath`
- **Release note:** OpenAI Codex and Azure OpenAI requests parse their URL as fetch does again: an upper-case scheme, a space or a dot segment in a configured base URL reaches the server as the serialized URL, and the fragment is not sent. Codex reports a base URL with credentials with fetch's own message.

### BF-80bb522-3

- **Symptom:** Amazon Bedrock Converse requests merge adjacent messages that have the same role.
- **Root cause:** the Converse API requires the roles of a conversation to alternate and rejects two consecutive messages of one role with a ValidationException (HTTP 400). The shape is common: aborting a turn while tools run and then sending a new prompt gives `assistant(toolUse), user(toolResult...), user(prompt)`, and every later turn of the session then fails.

- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Pi issue:** none recorded
- **Removed when Pi fixes it:** Pi merges or otherwise alternates adjacent same-role messages in its Converse converter.

- **Tests:** None recorded.
- **Release note:** Amazon Bedrock Converse requests merge adjacent messages that have the same role. A prompt sent after an abort during tool execution, or after a dropped assistant turn, no longer makes every later turn fail with a role-alternation error. Pi 1.2.0 sends two consecutive user messages (D116).

### BF-81e1a45

**Streaming a tool call's arguments allocates less per delta**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Streaming a tool call's arguments allocates less per delta.
- **Root cause:** Pi's incremental parse of tool-call arguments () costs a snapshot per delta. PiG paid more than Pi on top of it: the parser recorded the changes nobody read, and every publish of the message cell copied the arguments the parser had just copied.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `81e1a45f0b` (2026-10-25)
- **Tests:** `ai/streamed_arguments_shared_test.go::TestMutatingWhatASubscriberReceivedChangesNoSnapshotOfAStreamedCall`, `ai/streamed_arguments_shared_test.go::TestPublishedStreamedArgumentsShareTheSnapshotOnlyWhenValidAndEqualACloneAlways`, `ai/streamed_arguments_shared_test.go::TestStreamingSnapshotValidityRules`, `ai/streamed_arguments_shared_test.go::TestSubscribersMutatingConcurrentlyDoNotRaceWithAStreamingProducer`
- **Release note:** Streaming a tool call's arguments allocates less per delta. The incremental parser no longer records changes nobody reads, and a streamed message's published copy keeps the parser's validated snapshot instead of copying it again (an invalid byte in an argument string is still rewritten as before). A 250 KB `write` call streams about 13% faster with about 22% fewer allocations; the print-mode allocation ceilings per delta fall from 20 and 35 to the measured 18.5 and 18.3 (faux provider and OpenAI Completions).

### BF-82ca8da

**On Windows, the host reports the load error of a Node extension that exits right after it sends the error**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The host could report `process_exited` and lose the error.
- **Root cause:** The pipe driver sets the event that the host tested for a client later than the client's open returns, so a client whose event was not yet set was not counted.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** Windows
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `82ca8da822` (2026-10-30)
- **Tests:** `coding/extension/host/subprocess/accept_client_test.go::TestAwaitConnectionHonorsAConnectionMadeBeforeTheExit`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/accept_client_windows_test.go::TestAwaitConnectionHonorsAClientBeforeItsConnectEventIsSet`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/accept_client_windows_test.go::TestPipeListenerInterruptKeepsAClientBeforeItsConnectEventIsSet`
- **Release note:** On Windows, the host reports the load error of a Node extension that exits right after it sends the error. A Node extension whose factory fails connects to its named pipe, writes the error, closes and exits, and the host looks at the pipe only after the exit. Before this fix, the host could report `process_exited` and lose the error. The pipe driver sets the event that the host tested for a client later than the client's open returns, so a client whose event was not yet set was not counted. The host now asks the pipe's own state, which the open changes before it returns.

### BF-82d1808

**Subprocess extensions no longer slow down each streamed token in long sessions: the state sent before each…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Subprocess extensions no longer slow down each streamed token in long sessions: the state sent before each event reuses the context usage estimate and the session name until the session changes.
- **Root cause:** The host pushes a state snapshot to a subprocess extension before every event it dispatches (subprocess host.go pushStateTo), and the snapshot carries getContextUsage and getSessionName. Both walked the whole log: ContextUsage projected the branch and getSessionName scanned every entry backwards, so each event, including one message_update per streamed delta, cost O(history): 2 MB and 4.3 ms per event at 500 exchanges. Pi computes context usage only when an extension calls ctx.getContextUsage() (agent-session.ts getContextUsage).
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `10aebd5c05` (2026-10-09), `82d1808c64` (2026-10-10)
- **Tests:** `ai/complexity_scaling_norace_test.go::TestScalingProviderRequestPerTurn`, `ai/complexity_scaling_norace_test.go::TestScalingProviderStreamPerDelta`, `coding/cli/complexity_scaling_norace_test.go::TestScalingExtensionEventStatePush`, `coding/complexity_scaling_norace_test.go::TestScalingSessionTurn`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/complexity_scaling_norace_test.go::TestScalingMessageUpdatePayload`, `coding/session_context_usage_reuse_test.go::TestContextUsageReusesTheEstimateUntilTheLogOrWindowChanges`, `internal/codingagent/compaction/complexity_scaling_norace_test.go::TestScalingCompactionAndContextEstimate`, `internal/codingagent/complexity_scaling_norace_test.go::TestScalingSessionLogOperations` and 7 more in docs/bug-ledger.json

### BF-83928e2

**A `context` handler that edits a message of `event.messages` in place and then throws now leaves the edit in…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A `context` handler that edits a message of `event.messages` in place and then throws now leaves the edit in the request, as it does in Pi, where the handler works on a copy of the list over the one set of message objects: an edit to a message stays and a change to the list does not.
- **Root cause:** message_end: Pi hands every message_end handler an event over the one message (runner.ts emitMessageEnd, currentMessage) and stores that object (agent-session.ts appendMessage), so a handler that edits event.message in place and returns nothing changes the message the next handlers, turn_end, agent_end, the saved entry and the next provider request hold, also when it throws afterwards. Only the Node SDK sent the edit back. The Go, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs lost it: their reply carried only the handler's result. Each of them now sends back the message as the handler left it when its JSON text differs from the one it received, in the _pigMessageEndMessage member the Node runtime uses, with…
- **User impact:** Lost or altered data
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `83928e2246` (2026-11-16)
- **Tests:** `test/extension-conformance/in_place_context_test.go::TestConformance_InPlaceContextEditsFollowPi`, `test/extension-conformance/in_place_message_end_test.go::TestConformance_InPlaceMessageEndEditReachesTheTranscript`, `test/extension-conformance/in_place_message_end_test.go::TestConformance_InPlaceMessageEndEditsFollowPi`
- **Release note:** A `context` handler that edits a message of `event.messages` in place and then throws now leaves the edit in the request, as it does in Pi, where the handler works on a copy of the list over the one set of message objects: an edit to a message stays and a change to the list does not. Until now the failed handler's reply was dropped and the edit was lost, in every extension SDK. The loss was present in every release since v0.2.0.

### BF-8392c29

**MCP stdio servers now start in a session of their own, as Pi's stdio transport does (`detached` in Node's…**

- **Release note:** MCP stdio servers now start in a session of their own, as Pi's stdio transport does (`detached` in Node's spawn is `setsid`): a server, or a child of it, no longer keeps PiG's controlling terminal and cannot take the terminal's foreground process group from PiG. The server still leads its own process group, so closing the transport still ends its children (#427).

### BF-83ee534

**The exit's terminal restore is one uninterrupted sequence of writes now: a title an extension sets, an OSC 52…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The exit's terminal restore is one uninterrupted sequence of writes now: a title an extension sets, an OSC 52 copy and the terminal progress keepalive, which three other goroutines wrote at any moment, no longer land inside the stop's bytes (between the cursor show and the bracketed paste off, between the alternate screen's leave and the transcript print) and, when SIGTERM or SIGHUP ended the session, no longer follow them.
- **Root cause:** An extension's ctx.ui.setTitle, an OSC 52 copy and the OSC 9;4 progress keepalive are written by goroutines of their own. The exit's stop (cursor show, bracketed paste off, keyboard protocol pop, alternate screen leave) did not hold the terminal against them, so their bytes could land between the stop's writes, and after a signal's stop, where Pi's process.exit(0) leaves no callback to run (tui.ts stop() :1046-1056 is one synchronous call; interactive-mode.ts :4491-4494 ends the process right after it).
- **User impact:** Wrong display
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `83ee534a7d` (2026-11-16)
- **Tests:** `internal/codingagent/interactive_exit_storm_pty_test.go::TestExitStopSequenceHoldsNoWriterOfAnotherGoroutine`, `internal/codingagent/terminal_stop_transaction_test.go::TestHostWriteMadeAfterTheStopIsDroppedForASignalOnly`, `internal/codingagent/terminal_stop_transaction_test.go::TestHostWriteRequestedBeforeTheStopIsWrittenBeforeIt`, `tui/stop_transaction_test.go::TestForeignWriteStormHoldsNoByteInsideAStop`, `tui/stop_transaction_test.go::TestSealedStopDropsTheForeignWritesMadeDuringItAndAfterIt`
- **Release note:** The exit's terminal restore is one uninterrupted sequence of writes now: a title an extension sets, an OSC 52 copy and the terminal progress keepalive, which three other goroutines wrote at any moment, no longer land inside the stop's bytes (between the cursor show and the bracketed paste off, between the alternate screen's leave and the transcript print) and, when SIGTERM or SIGHUP ended the session, no longer follow them. Pi's `stop()` is one synchronous call on a single thread, so nothing of its own event loop writes inside it and, after a signal, `process.exit(0)` follows it at once. A recording of the exit, or a terminal that handles the bytes in order, saw an `OSC 0`, an `OSC 52` or an `OSC 9;4` between PiG's reset sequences or after the last of them; the screen a user sees is the same. A write requested before the stop begins is still written, before it (a copy requested just before quit reaches the clipboard); one requested while it runs waits for it and, for a quit by keys, follows it as in Pi (the title Pi's dispose sets); one requested after a signal's stop is dropped, as the exit drops it in Pi. An external editor's or a suspend's stop holds the terminal the same way and gives it back when the TUI starts again. Present in every release from v0.2.0 through v0.7.0 (checked by tag: v0.2.0 and v0.7.0 each write the title, the progress keepalive and the OSC 52 copy from goroutines of their own, outside the restore).

### BF-83fea11

**On Windows, a refused connection reads as Node's `connect ECONNREFUSED` and is not retried, as in Pi; it was…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** On Windows, a refused connection reads as Node's `connect ECONNREFUSED` and is not retried, as in Pi; it was reported as a retryable `fetch failed`.
- **Root cause:** nodeNetErrorMessage accepted only the connect syscall, but Go names the Windows call connectex, so on Windows a refused connect fell through to 'fetch failed' and a retryable Bedrock error where Node reports 'connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:N', not retryable (TestNodeNetErrorMessageIsNodesText, TestBedrockRefusedConnectIsNodesErrorLikePi on the release PR's Windows native-2 job).
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** Windows
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `83fea11dbf` (2026-10-15)
- **Tests:** `ai/node_net_error_test.go::TestNodeNetErrorMessageIsNodesText`, `ai/oauth_page_corpus_test.go::TestOAuthPageCorpusMatchesThePinnedPackage`
- **Release note:** On Windows, a refused connection reads as Node's `connect ECONNREFUSED` and is not retried, as in Pi; it was reported as a retryable `fetch failed`.

### BF-844d215

**Repairing a partial tool-call arguments text follows partial-json's `obj["__proto__"] = value`: a…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Repairing a partial tool-call arguments text follows partial-json's `obj["__proto__"] = value`: a `"__proto__": null` member leaves the object without a prototype, so a later `"__proto__"` member is an ordinary member, as in Pi (it was dropped).
- **Root cause:** partial-json builds objects with obj[key] = value. A "__proto__" member runs Object.prototype's setter: null makes the prototype null, an object or array replaces it, any other value is ignored, and none creates a property. Once the prototype is null there is no setter, so a later "__proto__" member is an ordinary member. parseMembers dropped every "__proto__" member.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `844d2155d8` (2026-10-11)
- **Tests:** `ai/streaming_json_oracle_test.go::TestStreamingJSONMatchesPiOnSeededInput`
- **Release note:** Repairing a partial tool-call arguments text follows partial-json's `obj["__proto__"] = value`: a `"__proto__": null` member leaves the object without a prototype, so a later `"__proto__"` member is an ordinary member, as in Pi (it was dropped).

**Fullscreen: copying a selection with OSC 52 (when no clipboard tool is set, as an extension screen does…**

### BF-84b2fca

**Code that fails to highlight takes the code-block color, as in Pi: `highlightCode` returns it in the…**

- **Fix commits:** `84b2fcadd1` (2026-11-01)

**A `tool_call` handler that assigns a new object to `event.input` now gives it to the next handlers of the…**

The call itself still runs with the input it carried, as in Pi, so nothing a released extension could rely on is lost; a Rust handler keeps its own behaviour, which is unchanged in every released version: the Rust SDK holds the event as one value, so assigning the input and editing it in place are the same edit and the tool runs with what the handler left.

### BF-85c4c8f

**`pig login <provider>` now prints what Pi's `packages/ai/src/cli.ts` prints and keeps `auth.json` private**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** `pig login <provider>` now prints what Pi's `packages/ai/src/cli.ts` prints and keeps `auth.json` private.
- **Root cause:** pig login printed a blank line after every authorization URL, listed select options as "1) label" and read the default option on an empty answer, prefixed "Error:" to every login failure except an unknown provider, and left an existing auth.json at its old permissions while it stored OAuth tokens in it. Pi's packages/ai/src/cli.ts prints neither the blank line nor "1)", asks "Enter number (1-N): " and fails an answer that is not a listed number with "Invalid selection", prefixes every failure with "Error:", and chmods an existing auth.json to 0600 before it saves.
- **User impact:** Credential or permission exposure
- **Platform:** All platforms

- **Tests:** `coding/cli/ai_cli_pi_oracle_test.go::TestAICLILoginMatchesPi`
- **Release note:** `pig login <provider>` now prints what Pi's `packages/ai/src/cli.ts` prints and keeps `auth.json` private. It left a blank line after every authorization URL, listed a provider's select options as `1) label` and took the first option for an empty answer, and printed an unknown provider without the `Error:` prefix that every other login failure has. Pi asks `Enter number (1-N): ` for a select option, lists `1. label`, and fails an answer that is not a listed number with `Invalid selection`. An existing `auth.json` keeps the permissions an older version gave it while the new OAuth tokens are written into it; login now sets it to owner-only (`0600`) before it saves, as `cli.ts` does.

### BF-85c98be

**`durable/interop/bench.mjs` and `sqlhost-bench seed|sample` report the process's own peak RSS on Linux…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** `durable/interop/bench.mjs` and `sqlhost-bench seed|sample` report the process's own peak RSS on Linux (`VmHWM`), as `bench/durableperf` already did. getrusage's maxRSS lagged it by 6 to 20 MiB, and it took on the launcher's peak when that was larger: Go, Python and Node all spawn with vfork, so the child's maxRSS starts from the parent's.
- **Root cause:** durable/interop/bench.mjs read process.resourceUsage().maxRSS and sqlhost-bench getrusage's ru_maxrss. On Linux that value carries the RSS high-water mark of the address space the process was exec'd from, and every launcher of these samples spawns with vfork: with a 512 MiB parent, a bench.mjs sample whose own VmHWM is 110.5-111.6 MiB reports 512.8-521.5 MiB from Go (exec.Command, also through taskset), Python (subprocess.run) and Node (spawnSync).
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** Linux
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `85c98bed2b` (2026-10-13)
- **Tests:** None recorded.
- **Release note:** `durable/interop/bench.mjs` and `sqlhost-bench seed|sample` report the process's own peak RSS on Linux (`VmHWM`), as `bench/durableperf` already did. getrusage's maxRSS lagged it by 6 to 20 MiB, and it took on the launcher's peak when that was larger: Go, Python and Node all spawn with vfork, so the child's maxRSS starts from the parent's. `peakRss` in the pi and pig-native lines of earlier Linux runs is low by that lag.

### BF-86376a7

**Draining a model collection while it refreshes no longer starts provider work after the drain began, and a…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Draining a model collection while it refreshes no longer starts provider work after the drain began, and a streaming request's blocked auth callback no longer holds the drain.
- **Root cause:** Drain took its snapshot of the collection's owned work without stopping the collection from admitting more. A refresh loop with providers still queued kept starting them after Drain began, and any owned worker added while Drain waited (or at a zero count) raced the WaitGroup. Drain now sets a draining flag under the lock that admission takes, so work is admitted before it or not at all: the refresh loop starts no further provider, a late publication writes nothing, and the loop's own settle wait is a counter instead of one more owned goroutine.
- **User impact:** Credential or permission exposure
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `86376a7777` (2026-11-11)
- **Tests:** `ai/models_runtime_drain_test.go::TestModelsDrainDoesNotWaitForAStreamsAuthCallback`, `ai/models_runtime_drain_test.go::TestModelsDrainJoinsTheCredentialWriteOfACancelledStream`, `ai/models_runtime_drain_test.go::TestModelsPublicationAfterDrainWritesNothing`, `ai/models_runtime_drain_test.go::TestModelsRefreshLoopStartsNoQueuedProviderAfterDrainBegan`, `ai/models_runtime_drain_test.go::TestModelsRefreshStartsNoProviderWorkOnceDrainBegan`
- **Release note:** Draining a model collection while it refreshes no longer starts provider work after the drain began, and a streaming request's blocked auth callback no longer holds the drain. `ai.Models.Drain` now stops the collection admitting owned work under the lock the work is admitted under, so a refresh with providers still queued starts none of them, a publication made afterwards writes nothing, and no worker is added to the group the drain is waiting on. A stream's auth callbacks run outside the work `Drain` joins, as a login's do, while the credential write of a stored OAuth refresh, which a cancelled stream leaves running, is joined.

### BF-8677279

**Closing an RPC client's input while a `bash` command is running, or quitting interactive mode with Ctrl+D…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Closing an RPC client's input while a `bash` command is running, or quitting interactive mode with Ctrl+D while a `!` command is running and an extension's `session_shutdown` handler never settles (the drained-loop quit), left that shell command and its descendants running after `pig` exited 0.
- **Root cause:** exitRPC in coding/cli/rpc_mode.go and exitAtDrainedQuit in coding/cli/interactive_build.go exited via os.Exit without calling tools.KillTrackedDetachedChildren, so os.Exit raced Session.Dispose's asynchronous AbortBash kill and left the shell's process group or Windows job alive
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** Windows
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `867727906e` (2026-11-21)
- **Tests:** `coding/cli/interactive_drained_quit_bash_linux_test.go::TestInteractiveDrainedQuitKillsRunningUserBash`, `coding/cli/rpc_quit_kills_bash_unix_test.go::TestListenConnectionEOFDoesNotKillSiblingConnectionBash`, `coding/cli/rpc_quit_kills_bash_unix_test.go::TestRPCExtensionShutdownWhileBashRuns`, `coding/cli/rpc_quit_kills_bash_unix_test.go::TestRPCInputEndKillsRunningBashTree`, `coding/cli/rpc_quit_kills_bash_unix_test.go::TestRPCInputEndKillsRunningBashTreeNoExt`, `coding/cli/rpc_quit_kills_bash_windows_test.go::TestWin_RPCInputEndKillsRunningBashTree`, `internal/codingagent/tools/bash_group_windows_test.go::TestWin_KillTrackedProcessGroupsBoundedExit`, `internal/codingagent/tools/bash_group_windows_test.go::TestWin_KillTrackedProcessGroupsReapsJobDescendants` and 1 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** Closing an RPC client's input while a `bash` command is running, or quitting interactive mode with Ctrl+D while a `!` command is running and an extension's `session_shutdown` handler never settles (the drained-loop quit), left that shell command and its descendants running after `pig` exited 0. `pig` now kills tracked shell process trees before exiting on both paths, as it already does on `/quit`, and on Windows bounds the whole exit-path kill (taskkill, job termination, and waiting on job members) at 2,000 ms (following Pi 31b407dc63, #11889). Affects 0.3.0 through 0.7.0 (RPC input end; drained-loop quit was introduced after 0.7.0).

### BF-873f87d

**Chord: a context linked from two abort sources now reports the reason of the source that aborted first when…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The abort order (`chordctx.AbortOrder`) walked through the `WithoutAbortSignal` context into its parents, so the abort of a parent that never reached the derived context counted as the derived context's own, and its reason won over the other source's although that one aborted first.
- **Root cause:** abortSources and AbortOrder each walked a context's parents on their own, and only abortSources stopped at a WithoutAbortSignal context, so the two functions disagreed about which aborts reach a context.
- **User impact:** Wrong output or ordering
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `873f87dc75` (2026-11-16)
- **Tests:** `chord/context/abort_cause_oracle_test.go::TestAbortCauseMatchesPi`, `chord/context/abort_detached_order_test.go::TestAbortOrderStopsAtADetachedAncestor`, `chord/context/abort_detached_order_test.go::TestLateListenerHearsTheFirstSourceThatAbortedNotADetachedAncestorsParent`
- **Release note:** Chord: a context linked from two abort sources now reports the reason of the source that aborted first when one of the sources is derived from a `chordctx.WithoutAbortSignal` context: the host's linked abort signals do, and so does `chordctx.OnAbort` on a context derived by `WithAbortSignal`. Before, the abort order (`chordctx.AbortOrder`) walked through the `WithoutAbortSignal` context into its parents, so the abort of a parent that never reached the derived context counted as the derived context's own, and its reason won over the other source's although that one aborted first. As in Pi, where `withoutAbortSignal` leaves the context no abort signal, the walk now ends at a `WithoutAbortSignal` context. Released in: v0.7.0, and every release since (the walk came with 0b76ae5e5, which `git tag --contains` places in v0.7.0; a probe at the v0.7.0 tag ranks `WithCancel(WithoutAbortSignal(x))` before an independent source that aborted earlier).

### BF-8780292

**The footer's thinking level no longer reads `thinking off` in the first frames of an interactive start**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The footer's thinking level no longer reads `thinking off` in the first frames of an interactive start.
- **Root cause:** The footer and the editor border learned the Session's thinking level only when the startup bind ran, after the TUI had started drawing, so a startup frame painted before the bind showed 'thinking off' where Pi shows the configured level. Pi's footer reads session.state.thinkingLevel on every render (footer.ts:236, interactive-mode.ts:2351) and is built with the Session (interactive-mode.ts:659); the footer and the editor are now seeded with the Session's level when they are built.
- **User impact:** Wrong display
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `8780292204` (2026-10-29), `b48dfa93ff` (2026-10-29)
- **Tests:** `internal/codingagent/footer_startup_thinking_test.go::TestNewFooterShowsTheSessionThinkingLevelBeforeTheStartupBind`
- **Release note:** The footer's thinking level no longer reads `thinking off` in the first frames of an interactive start. PiG drew the footer and the editor border before the startup bind told them the Session's level, so a frame painted in that window showed `• thinking off` (and the neutral border) where Pi shows the configured level, `• medium` by default; with an extension loaded the bind comes later and the window is longer. The Session's level was right all along (`get_state` and the first request carry it); only the presentation lagged. Pi builds its footer with the Session and reads `session.state.thinkingLevel` on every render (`footer.ts` `render`, `interactive-mode.ts` `init`), so the footer and the editor are now seeded with the Session's level when they are built, for the default level, `--thinking` and settings overrides, and `off`, whichever extension host is loaded.

### BF-87ea4f9

**A session whose model has no known context window (a model an extension registers without a `contextWindow`…**

- **Source:** A Pi defect that PiG fixed first (divergence D660)
- **Symptom:** A session whose model has no known context window (a model an extension registers without a `contextWindow`, or one an embedding program builds without `ContextWindow`) no longer compacts its history after every reply: a window of 0 is unknown, not used up, so the threshold check is skipped for it and a known window is checked as before.

Overflow recovery, explicit compaction and known windows are unchanged.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Pi issue:** none recorded
- **Removed when Pi fixes it:** Pi guards the post-reply check against a window of 0 (checked on Pi main on 2026-11-19: not yet; `agent-session.ts:3135`, `:3251`).
- **Fix commits:** `87ea4f926e` (2026-11-19)
- **Tests:** `coding/compaction_unknown_window_shapes_test.go::TestCheckCompactionDecisionUnknownWindow`, `coding/compaction_unknown_window_shapes_test.go::TestUnknownWindowAfterReplyAcrossProviderShapes`, `coding/compaction_unknown_window_test.go::TestCompactionUnknownWindowNoThresholdCompaction`
- **Release note:** A session whose model has no known context window (a model an extension registers without a `contextWindow`, or one an embedding program builds without `ContextWindow`) no longer compacts its history after every reply: a window of 0 is unknown, not used up, so the threshold check is skipped for it and a known window is checked as before. PiG had compacted after every reply for such a model since 0.2.0, which cost a summariser request and the history of each turn; Pi still does (D660). Fix from #548 by @Cpt-Falcon.

### BF-8894a13-2

**The liveness conformance harness answers the host-parser helper calls a factory makes before the register…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The liveness conformance harness answers the host-parser helper calls a factory makes before the register frame, so the recording of the five SDK cells is unchanged.
- **Root cause:** The yaml library builds a double-quoted scalar from UTF-16 units (String.fromCodePoint per escape), so "\uD83D\uDE00" is U+1F600: Pi's parseFrontmatter reads a: "\uD83D\uDE00" as {"a":"😀"}. yaml12 turned each surrogate escape into U+FFFD on its own, so skills, prompt templates and the new frontmatter.parse host call gave two U+FFFD. doubleQuotedValue now holds a high-surrogate escape until the next thing the scalar receives and joins it with a low-surrogate escape; a surrogate left unpaired stays U+FFFD (a Go string cannot hold it).
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `15cb4f2db8` (2026-10-11), `8894a13f34` (2026-10-11), `edf4304a1c` (2026-10-11), `f51d8b4bea` (2026-10-11)
- **Tests:** `internal/codingagent/frontmatter/ordered_test.go::TestParseOrderedListsKeysInInsertionOrder`, `internal/yaml12/surrogate_escape_test.go::TestDoubleQuotedSurrogateEscapesJoinIntoOneCharacter`, `test/extension-conformance/compaction_usage_test.go::TestConformance_CompactionUsageHelpersAgreeAcrossSDKs`, `test/extension-conformance/host_parser_helpers_test.go::TestConformance_HostParserHelpersAgreeAcrossSDKs`
- **Release note:** The liveness conformance harness answers the host-parser helper calls a factory makes before the register frame, so the recording of the five SDK cells is unchanged.

### BF-88bbdd2

**A name that is also a member of JavaScript's `Object.prototype` (`constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`…**

- **Source:** A Pi defect that PiG fixed first (divergence D645)
- **Symptom:** A name that is also a member of JavaScript's `Object.prototype` (`constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, `__proto__` and the like) is treated as any other name in more places (D645).
- **Root cause:** `pig mcp add constructor -- <command>` reports the server as added (it said `Replaced` the first time), `pig mcp add __proto__ -- <command>` writes the server to `mcp.json` (it was not written at all), and `pig mcp remove` of such a name that the file does not hold says there is no such server (it said `Removed`).
- **User impact:** Wrong display

- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Pi issue:** none recorded
- **Removed when Pi fixes it:** Pi looks these names up as own properties (or with a `Map`) at the site; each row can then go alone, with its marker, and the record is retired with the last row.
- **Fix commits:** `3fb47cfd56` (2026-11-13), `43e001e9e3` (2026-11-13), `88bbdd2eaa` (2026-11-13)
- **Tests:** `ai/env_keys_prototype_names_oracle_test.go::TestAProviderNamedLikeAnObjectPrototypeMemberHasNoEnvironmentKey`, `coding/extension/mcp_servers_oracle_test.go::TestValidateMcpServerConfigMatchesPi`, `coding/extension/mcp_tool_exposure_prototype_names_oracle_test.go::TestAnMcpToolNamedLikeAnObjectPrototypeMemberGetsTheServersExposure`, `coding/mcpext/cli_oracle_test.go::TestMcpCommandMatchesPi`, `coding/mcpext/server_name_prototype_names_oracle_test.go::TestAnMcpServerOrOptionNamedLikeAnObjectPrototypeMemberIsTreatedAsAnyOtherName`, `coding/mcpext/server_name_prototype_names_oracle_test.go::TestAnMcpToolNamedLikeAnObjectPrototypeMemberIsListedWithoutAnExposure`, `coding/stored_credential_prototype_names_oracle_test.go::TestAProviderNamedLikeAnObjectPrototypeMemberHasNoStoredCredential`, `internal/codingagent/keybindings_file_oracle_test.go::TestKeybindingsFileLoadingMatchesPi` and 14 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** A name that is also a member of JavaScript's `Object.prototype` (`constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, `__proto__` and the like) is treated as any other name in more places (D645). `pig mcp add constructor -- <command>` reports the server as added (it said `Replaced` the first time), `pig mcp add __proto__ -- <command>` writes the server to `mcp.json` (it was not written at all), and `pig mcp remove` of such a name that the file does not hold says there is no such server (it said `Removed`). A `keybindings.json` key so named is left as written: it was renamed to text such as `function Object() { [native code] }` and the file was rewritten. Pi 1.5.2 does the old things. In Node extensions, `ctx.ui.theme.fg`, `bg`, `getFgAnsi` and `getBgAnsi` throw `Unknown theme color: <token>` for a token so named, as Pi does and as the other SDKs did: `fg` threw `open.endsWith is not a function`, `bg` drew the text of a native function before the text, and the two getters returned a function. `ctx.ui.setStatus("__proto__", text)` is a status the extension's own footer reads back in the same turn, a provider registered under the name `__proto__` is read like any other provider, and `pi.getSettings()` hands the settings without any `__proto__` member.

### BF-892827f

**`coding`: while the run of a session-graph client (an ExtensionRunner an extension constructed) was aborted…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** `coding`: while the run of a session-graph client (an ExtensionRunner an extension constructed) was aborted, the Host read the client's `getSignal` function again and again without end, one call to the client each, and sent every runtime a new `run_signal` frame each time.
- **Root cause:** The getSignal binding of the ExtensionRunner graph object returned context.Background() for a live run and a new cancelled context on every read of an aborted one. The Host numbers a context it has not seen as a new run and watches it with context.AfterFunc, which fires at once for a context that is already cancelled and syncs every runtime again. While a graph client's run was aborted every sync therefore saw a new context, renumbered the run, armed the watcher and read again: a busy loop of getter reads (one RPC to the client each) and run_signal frames to every runtime, until the run ended. It was not caused by the run signal numbering change before it and is present on the base too.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `892827ff8c` (2026-11-03)
- **Tests:** `coding/session_graph_signal_test.go::TestGraphAbortedRunIsReadAgainByNoSync`, `coding/session_graph_signal_test.go::TestGraphGetSignalIsOneObjectForARunAndItsAbort`
- **Release note:** `coding`: while the run of a session-graph client (an ExtensionRunner an extension constructed) was aborted, the Host read the client's `getSignal` function again and again without end, one call to the client each, and sent every runtime a new `run_signal` frame each time. The binding answered an aborted run with a new cancelled context on every read; the Host takes a context it has not seen for a new run and watches it, which fires at once for a cancelled one, so every sync renumbered the run and synced again. A run is now one context from the first read that reports it until a read reports no run, and the abort cancels that context in place, as Pi's `agent.signal` is one `AbortSignal` for a run. The run keeps its number through its abort and an aborted run costs no further read.

**A Node extension no longer keeps reading an entry the host refused**

- **Symptom:** A Node extension no longer keeps reading an entry the host refused.
- **Root cause:** Fixes #264

- **Release note:** A Node extension no longer keeps reading an entry the host refused. When the host answers `pi.appendEntry` (or `ctx.sessionManager.appendCustomEntry`) with an error, `getEntries()`, `getBranch()`, `getLeafId()`, `getEntry()` and the other session reads stop showing that entry, also after later calls the host synchronizes; before, the entry stayed in the extension's session reads although the host's log never held it. Only the refused entry is taken back: appends still in flight stay, and an entry the host appended is read with the parent the host linked it to, where the extension could show the refused entry or an older leaf instead. ### BF-8a44836

**Closing a session with an MCP server that signs in with OAuth no longer fails at random**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Closing a session with an MCP server that signs in with OAuth no longer fails at random.
- **Root cause:** Close cancelled the transport's context, which aborts the requests in flight, and sent the session DELETE at once. A response without a body (the GET stream answered 405, a 202) is handed to its round trip after the connection went back to the idle pool (net/http transport.go readLoop: tryPutIdleConn before the send on rc.ch). When the transport's context ends in that window the round trip finds no response yet and closes the connection with its context error (persistConn.roundTrip, `case <-ctxDoneChan`), although the DELETE may already have taken the connection from the pool. The DELETE then fails with the aborted request's `context canceled` after about 100 microseconds and the server…
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `320d389221` (2026-10-29), `680815deac` (2026-10-29), `8a4483647c` (2026-10-29), `d5d34e7742` (2026-10-29)
- **Tests:** `coding/mcp_oauth_session_upstream_test.go::TestAgentSessionMCPOAuthClosesTheSessionWithoutRefreshingAnExpiringToken`, `mcp/streamable_http_close_order_test.go::TestStreamableHTTPTransportSendsTheSessionDeleteOnlyAfterTheAbortedRequestsReturned`, `mcp/streamable_http_get_stream_token_test.go::TestStreamableHTTPTransportReadsTheGETStreamsTokenBeforeTheInitializedNotificationReturns`
- **Release note:** Closing a session with an MCP server that signs in with OAuth no longer fails at random. The `DELETE` that ends the session could be refused with the `context canceled` of the stream the connection opens to hear from the server, when closing began while that stream's answer was still being handed over, so the server kept the session until it expired; closing now sends the `DELETE` only after the requests it aborted have returned. The stream's first request also reads its token before the connection is reported ready, as in Pi: a stream that started late could refresh a token that was about to expire, and closing then waited up to 15 seconds for the authorization server.

### BF-8a4cf80

**A routed `pi.events.emit` no longer lets its emitter run ahead of a listener extension process**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** As in Pi, every continuation a listener queued runs before any microtask the emitter queues after `emit` returns, and the emitter's settle wait now covers every listener process of the emit: it used to end early when an earlier listener process had already answered (it was inside its own wait for an earlier emit of the same burst), failed or exited before the Host wrote the request of the next one, so that process's continuations could interleave with the emitter's later work.
- **Root cause:** The emission settled the first moment its pending map was empty, so a realm that reported before the dispatch loop had registered the next realm (a quiesce written before its dispatch response, a failed dispatch, a closed connection) closed it, and the emitter's events.settle returned without waiting for the realms the loop reached afterwards. Their continuations could then run between the emitter's later microtasks; in Pi every continuation a listener queued runs before any microtask the emitter queues after emit returns (event-bus.ts:15-17, 19-25).
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `8a4cf80a3e` (2026-11-14)
- **Tests:** `coding/extension/host/subprocess/event_bus_settle_test.go::TestDispatchEventEmissionSettlesWhenTheLoopEndsWithNoPendingListener`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/event_bus_settle_test.go::TestDispatchEventEmissionStaysOpenUntilTheLoopHasRegisteredEveryListenerRealm`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/event_bus_settle_test.go::TestHostEventBusEmitCallSettlesAfterEveryListenerRealm`
- **Release note:** A routed `pi.events.emit` no longer lets its emitter run ahead of a listener extension process. As in Pi, every continuation a listener queued runs before any microtask the emitter queues after `emit` returns, and the emitter's settle wait now covers every listener process of the emit: it used to end early when an earlier listener process had already answered (it was inside its own wait for an earlier emit of the same burst), failed or exited before the Host wrote the request of the next one, so that process's continuations could interleave with the emitter's later work.

### BF-8a88c34

**On Windows, a custom theme edited in a rapid burst of writes no longer stays on a stale version**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** On Windows, a custom theme edited in a rapid burst of writes no longer stays on a stale version.
- **Root cause:** An overflow of the native change buffer loses events but leaves the watch armed. The run loop closed the native watcher on every error, so a burst of writes that overflowed the Windows ReadDirectoryChangesW buffer ended the watch and the final write was never reloaded. An overflow now schedules a reload, as Pi does for a change without a filename, and keeps watching; any other error still closes the watcher.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** Windows
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `8a88c34d51` (2026-10-26)
- **Tests:** `tui/theme_watcher_upstream_test.go::TestThemeWatcherOtherErrorsCloseNativeWatcher`, `tui/theme_watcher_upstream_test.go::TestThemeWatcherOverflowReloadsAndKeepsWatching`
- **Release note:** On Windows, a custom theme edited in a rapid burst of writes no longer stays on a stale version. A burst that overflowed the native change buffer made the watcher treat the overflow as a failure and close its watch, so writes after the overflow were never seen and the theme kept an older version of the file (seen as `accent="#123456" want="#000064"` in Windows CI, only while the machine was loaded). An overflow now reloads the theme file, as Pi reloads on a change without a filename, and the watcher keeps watching; any other watch failure still closes it, as in Pi.

### BF-8ab5a89

**A long session no longer holds each tool result twice**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A long session no longer holds each tool result twice.
- **Root cause:** Pi's session holds the message object the agent appended (session-manager.ts appendMessage pushes it into fileEntries), so a tool result is in memory once. appendMessageEntry kept the appended message only when its record decoded DeepEqual to it, and a tool result never does: its record decodes Details to their JSON (orderedjson.Value), while the tool gave a typed value (ReadDetails, BashDetails, EditToolDetails, ...) or an extension a map. So every tool result was held twice, as the agent's message and as the record's decode, text included.
- **User impact:** Wrong output or ordering
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `06c408c21d` (2026-10-11), `8ab5a89874` (2026-10-11), `eab3caf769` (2026-10-11)
- **Tests:** `internal/codingagent/session_store_test.go::TestAppendedMessageIsHeldOnceWhenItsRecordDecodesToIt`, `internal/codingagent/session_store_test.go::TestAppendedToolResultWithTypedDetailsIsHeldOnce`, `internal/codingagent/tools/truncation_share_test.go::TestTruncatedResultDetailsShareTheReturnedText`
- **Release note:** A long session no longer holds each tool result twice. The session now keeps the tool result the agent produced instead of a second copy decoded from its record, and a truncated `read`, `ls`, `find`, `grep` or `bash` result keeps its kept output once instead of again in its truncation details. In a 75-prompt session of file reads (about 4.2M tokens of context), memory at the end drops from about 245 MB to about 170 MB.

### BF-8ab86c8

**RPC `get_state` sent right after `new_session`, `fork`, `clone`, `switch_session` or `export_html` now…**

- **Source:** A Pi defect that PiG fixed first (divergence D146)
- **Symptom:** RPC `get_state` sent right after `new_session`, `fork`, `clone`, `switch_session` or `export_html` now answers first from the old Session, as in Pi; PiG still answers the replacement when stdin ends, which Pi does not (D146).
- **Root cause:** One ordering mechanism, rpcAwaitInOrder on the executor's event-loop task queue, serves both awaited operations that Pi resumes in request order: - set_model's auth checks run concurrently and settle in input order. Two pipelined set_models used to apply in completion order, so the final model was wrong in 1 of 12 runs. - Session replacements chain: each starts after the previous one applied and answers after it, so the last one requested decides the final Session. Concurrent replacements raced in Runner.BindCommandActions and hung at stdin end about one run in two. - A fork or clone requested while an earlier replacement is pending reads its entry from the Session that was current when it…
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Pi issue:** none recorded
- **Removed when Pi fixes it:** Pi answers a replacement command that is in flight when stdin ends. The part about replacements in flight together goes when Pi runs them one after the other (it starts every line at once at `rpc-mode.ts:833` and does not guard `AgentSessionRuntime` in Pi 1.5.2, and nothing upstream says it will): until then PiG keeps its order, which cannot be dropped without copying the double `session_shutdown`.
- **Fix commits:** `8ab86c8219` (2026-10-10)
- **Tests:** `coding/cli/rpc_replacement_order_test.go::TestRPCCloneAfterNewSessionOfOneBatchUsesTheRequestingSession`, `coding/cli/rpc_replacement_order_test.go::TestRPCReplacementStartsAfterItsBatchWasDispatched`, `coding/cli/rpc_replacement_order_test.go::TestRPCReplacementsOfOneBatchRunInRequestOrder`, `coding/cli/rpc_replacement_order_test.go::TestRPCSessionReplacementAnswersAfterALaterCommandOfItsBatch`, `coding/cli/rpc_replacement_order_test.go::TestRPCSessionReplacementsOfOneBatchSettleInDispatchOrder`, `coding/cli/rpc_resume_integration_test.go::TestRPCModeSessionReplacementAndExport`, `coding/cli/rpc_set_model_pipeline_test.go::TestRPCPipelinedSetModelsApplyInInputOrder`, `test/parity/scenarios/rpc/55-rpc-replacement-concurrent-get-state.toml`
- **Release note:** RPC `get_state` sent right after `new_session`, `fork`, `clone`, `switch_session` or `export_html` now answers first from the old Session, as in Pi; PiG still answers the replacement when stdin ends, which Pi does not (D146).
