### BF-bc5d1ad

**durable harness: closing a Harness on one goroutine while a commit was being published on another could start…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** durable harness: closing a Harness on one goroutine while a commit was being published on another could start a scheduler pass after the close had waited for the scheduler's passes.
- **Root cause:** kick, scheduleReconcileLocked and scheduleSweepLocked started their pass from a callback the Session runs at the end of the publication in progress (DeferUntilPublished), off the scheduler's mutex. A Close on another goroutine, while that publication ran the host's commit listeners, sealed the scheduler and let Join wait for the background group, which was empty; the pass joined the group afterwards. Join did not wait for it, and a sync.WaitGroup Add that meets a Wait at a zero counter panics ("WaitGroup is reused before previous Wait has returned"). Pi has no such group: join() waits for the invocations only (scheduler.ts:587-603), and its queued drain and reconcile find #closing and do…
- **User impact:** Crash, hang or runaway process
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `bc5d1adb08` (2026-11-12)
- **Tests:** `durable/harness/scheduler_join_test.go::TestSchedulerStartsNoPassAfterTheSealWhenAPublicationEndsAfterIt`
- **Release note:** durable harness: closing a Harness on one goroutine while a commit was being published on another could start a scheduler pass after the close had waited for the scheduler's passes. The pass ran unjoined, and the close could panic with `sync: WaitGroup is reused before previous Wait has returned`. A pass now joins the scheduler when it is scheduled, so the close waits for it.

### BF-bc8d37f

**`FileModelsStore` roots and index keys: new live-Pi oracle…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** `FileModelsStore` roots and index keys: new live-Pi oracle `TestFileModelsStoreNonObjectRootsAndIndexKeysMatchPi` (`ai/models_store_file_oracle_test.go`; 900 models-store.json files x 1-5 operations; null, array, number and boolean roots, integer-index provider ids, valid files holding null/number/string/array entries; TypeError text compared).

Upstream runs transformMessages after convertToLlm, where a branch summary, compaction summary, bash execution or custom message is already a user message and closes the pending tool calls. NormalizeMessages ran first and did not see them.

- **Fix commits:** `433d232815` (2026-10-09), `bc8d37f470` (2026-10-10)
- **Tests:** `agent/convert_custom_upstream_test.go::TestConvertToLLMCustomMessagesMatchUpstreamConvertToLlm`, `agent/convert_custom_upstream_test.go::TestConvertToLLMToolFlowMatchesUpstreamTransformOrder`, `agent/convert_custom_upstream_test.go::TestCustomMessagesReachProvidersAsUpstreamContentBlocks`, `agent/transform_custom_user_boundary_test.go::TestAnthropicRequestAfterBranchSummaryHasNoOrphanToolResult`, `agent/transform_custom_user_boundary_test.go::TestConvertToLLMCustomMessageWithoutWireOutputKeepsToolFlow`, `agent/transform_custom_user_boundary_test.go::TestConvertToLLMCustomUserMessageInterruptsToolFlow`, `agent/transform_custom_user_boundary_test.go::TestConvertToLLMHoldsSystemMessageUntilToolFlowCloses`, `ai/models_store_file_oracle_test.go::TestFileModelsStoreNonObjectRootsAndIndexKeysMatchPi` and 4 more in docs/bug-ledger.json

Real fixes: PiG rejected every non-object root where Pi accepts JSON arrays (read as an index-keyed object, written back as an array: a deleted or unset element is `null`, an index write extends the array) and numbers/booleans (read as empty, delete rewrites the scalar, write throws `Cannot create property 'x' on number '5'`), and a null root now throws the per-operation TypeErrors (`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'x')`, `Cannot set properties of null (setting 'x')`, `Cannot convert undefined or null to object`). `TestFileModelsStoreRejectsInvalidJSONAndCancelledContexts` asserted the old `[]`-is-corrupt behaviour; it now uses corrupt text. 11 mutations red (+1 untestable: the 2^32-1 array-index bound). Not compared: a stored value that is not a catalog reads back as itself in Pi (PiG's typed entry cannot hold it, so such files are only written and deleted), string-valued roots, V8 JSON parse text.

### BF-bd3e8ab

**On arm64 and other CPUs with a fused multiply-add, Kimi, Radius and xAI OAuth credentials store the `expires`…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The expiry could differ in the last digit and the minutes by one at a half-minute boundary.
- **Root cause:** Go may fuse x*y + z into one multiply-add on arm64, ppc64le, s390x and riscv64, also across statements and through an inlined return; JavaScript rounds every product and return value first. An explicit float64() conversion now rounds: - expectedSavings = continuationProbability * missCost - warmCost (cache-warmer.ts:390), which the decision event, /session and the warm threshold use; - the Radius shimmer offset (elapsedMs / 1000) * 10 before index - offset (radius-login-selector.ts:21-24); - smooth()'s return value, textFade and the fly-home arc of the easter egg (easter-egg-3d.ts:266-270, 1007, 1151-1152).
- **User impact:** Credential or permission exposure
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `a00dbe6901` (2026-10-13), `bd3e8ab24b` (2026-10-13)
- **Tests:** `ai/device_code_poll_oracle_test.go::TestDeviceCodePollDeadlineRoundsTheProductLikePi`, `ai/oauth_expiry_arithmetic_test.go::TestBuiltinOAuthExpiryUsesJavaScriptArithmetic`, `ai/openai_codex_http_error_test.go::TestCodexHTTPErrorResetMinutesRoundTheProductFirst`, `internal/codingagent/cache_warmer_test.go::TestCacheWarmingExpectedSavingsRoundsTheProductLikePi`, `internal/codingagent/pig_egg3d_test.go::TestPig3dFlightHomeOffsetsRoundLikePi`, `internal/codingagent/radius_login_oracle_test.go::TestRadiusLoginMenuRendersLikePi`
- **Release note:** On arm64 and other CPUs with a fused multiply-add, Kimi, Radius and xAI OAuth credentials store the `expires` time Pi computes for a fractional `expires_in`, the device-code login deadline matches Pi's, and the ChatGPT usage-limit message names the same "Try again in ~N min." as Pi: each `x * 1000` product is rounded before it is added, as JavaScript does. Before, the expiry could differ in the last digit and the minutes by one at a half-minute boundary.

### BF-bd9ac3b

**Releasing a session's services no longer leaves the model selector's catalog refresh running**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The refresh the selector starts and the shared catalog operation behind it were not joined by anything, so with a file-backed registry the operation could still write `auth.json` and `models-store.json` in the agent directory after the registry's model tasks were closed.
- **Root cause:** - the registry runs the shared operation as a model task, so CloseModelTasks cancels and joins it, and a closed registry returns an aborted result; - the selector's refresh is a task of its runtime's ModelSelectorTaskOwner, which the interactive mode backs with its background tasks, so Run's teardown cancels and joins it, including the runtime call it raced with the selector's signal; Dispose still cancels from the constructor's return.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `a775ab0b6d` (2026-11-09, #440), `bd9ac3b95a` (2026-11-09)
- **Tests:** `internal/codingagent/model_selector_refresh_owned_test.go::TestAbandonedModelCatalogRefreshIsJoinedByRegistryClose`, `internal/codingagent/model_selector_refresh_owned_test.go::TestModelCatalogRefreshAfterRegistryCloseIsAborted`, `internal/codingagent/model_selector_refresh_owned_test.go::TestModelSelectorRefreshDoesNotOutliveShutdown`, `tui/model_selector_owner_test.go::TestModelSelectorDisposeBeforeTheOwnerStartsTheTask`, `tui/model_selector_owner_test.go::TestModelSelectorRefreshIsJoinedByItsTaskOwner`, `tui/model_selector_owner_test.go::TestModelSelectorWaitJoinsItsOwnRefresh`, `tui/model_selector_owner_test.go::TestModelSelectorWithAShutDownOwnerShowsNoRefreshStatus`
- **Release note:** Releasing a session's services no longer leaves the model selector's catalog refresh running. Before, the refresh the selector starts and the shared catalog operation behind it were not joined by anything, so with a file-backed registry the operation could still write `auth.json` and `models-store.json` in the agent directory after the registry's model tasks were closed. The selector's refresh is now an owned task of the interactive mode, which cancels and joins it when the mode shuts down, and the operation behind it is a task of the model registry, which cancels and joins it when the session's services are released (for example on session replacement); at quit the process exits, as Pi's does. The refresh result and the picker are unchanged.

### BF-bdb7ad8

**A single server-sent-event line larger than 32 MiB (for example a base64 image chunk) no longer fails the…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A single server-sent-event line larger than 32 MiB (for example a base64 image chunk) no longer fails the stream with `token too long` on the providers that use PiG's SSE decoder.
- **Root cause:** An earlier change replaced the invented 32 MiB cap with math.MaxInt, so a server that never ends a line grows the buffer until the process runs out of memory. Pi is bounded: each of its SSE readers holds the line in a JavaScript string, and Node cannot make one longer than buffer.constants.MAX_STRING_LENGTH (2^29-24; the OpenAI SDK LineDecoder throws 'Cannot create a string longer than 0x1fffffe8 characters', string buffers throw 'RangeError: Invalid string length'). sseLineLimit is that bound.
- **User impact:** Crash, hang or runaway process
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `bdb7ad8292` (2026-10-09), `c715193fab` (2026-10-09)
- **Tests:** `ai/sse_long_line_test.go::TestSSEDecoderAcceptsALineLargerThan32MiB`, `ai/sse_long_line_test.go::TestSSEDecoderBoundsALine`, `ai/sse_long_line_test.go::TestSSELineLimitIsNodesMaxStringLength`
- **Release note:** A single server-sent-event line larger than 32 MiB (for example a base64 image chunk) no longer fails the stream with `token too long` on the providers that use PiG's SSE decoder. A line is now bounded where Pi's runtime bounds it, at Node's maximum string length (512 MiB), so a server that never ends a line cannot exhaust memory (D134).

### BF-be8900b

**A turn that ends with a provider error reading `Connection closed.`, such as a gateway cutting a stream with…**

- **Symptom:** A turn that ends with a provider error reading `Connection closed.`, such as a gateway cutting a stream with an `api_error` event, is now retried automatically like other dropped connections, instead of stopping with the error; the same applies to the agent proxy's `Connection closed by proxy server before the response completed` error, in the extension SDKs' `isRetryableAssistantError`, and for durable agents (upstream #12093).

### BF-bedd7ec

**chord: a server that is still loading its plugins refuses requests and links with 503, as Pi's does, instead…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** chord: a server that is still loading its plugins refuses requests and links with 503, as Pi's does, instead of answering them.
- **Root cause:** the Go server host loads its own facets first and its plugins after, in the Node plugin host, and its HTTP component resolved its registries once the first of the two were loaded. Pi's one host loads both in one load, and until then its HTTP component refuses every request and upgrade with 503.
- **User impact:** Lost or altered data
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `bedd7ec384` (2026-11-13)
- **Tests:** `chord/nextnode/app/app_bases_linux_test.go::TestAppRefusesRequestsAndLinksWith503WhileTheServersPluginsAreStillLoading`
- **Release note:** chord: a server that is still loading its plugins refuses requests and links with 503, as Pi's does, instead of answering them. A page that reconnected to a restarted server in that time (about 220 ms in the run that found it; the page's first retry comes after 250 ms) was connected, shown the scripts object's empty set, took its base for another one and reloaded: what the page held was lost (the server's state was kept). This happened because the Go server host loads its own facets first and its plugins after, in the Node plugin host, and its HTTP component answered once the first of the two were loaded, where Pi's one host loads both in one `load` and its HTTP component refuses until that ended (`not_ready`). The HTTP component now sees the server host's registries only once the plugins are loaded. The fix is commit aa77aa9c2f1d3eccb4597259bdf1440915b97215; its message names the divergence of the server's two hosts (number 605 in docs/parity/DIVERGENCES.md) because the defect exists only where those two hosts exist, and the fix does not close or change that divergence. In no release: the app kit (`chord/nextnode/app`) is in none of v0.2.0, v0.3.0 and v0.7.0.

### BF-beeb36a

**Running with no home directory now fails the way Pi's package manager does, instead of reading the project's…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** With no `HOME` and no entry for your user in the system's user database (a container run as a user its passwd file does not list), `pig` used to take the home directory to be empty, so the `.agents/skills` directory of the current project was listed as the user's `~/.agents/skills`, with user scope and without the project-trust prompt.
- **Root cause:** PiG's PackageManagerHomeDir ported `process.env.HOME || homedir()` (package-manager.ts:233-235, the pin's getHomeDir) with a failing branch that returned "" where Node's os.homedir() throws `SystemError [ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR]: A system error occurred: uv_os_homedir returned ENOENT (no such file or directory)`. Pi's callers are resolvePath (:2213, :2217) and addAutoDiscoveredResources (:2464, the first statement that matters in resolve()), so Pi's resolve() rejects there; PiG's collectors ignore errors and rely on ValidateAutoDiscoveredOverrides, which runs first in startup, reload and the config command (validateConfiguredResourceEntries), to report what Pi's resolve() rejects with. That…
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `beeb36afc7` (2026-10-24)
- **Tests:** `coding/cli/no_home_directory_test.go::TestResourceLoadingFailsWhereNoHomeDirectoryExists`, `coding/cli/no_home_directory_test.go::TestStartupFailsWhereNoHomeDirectoryExists`, `coding/cli/no_home_directory_test.go::TestStartupFollowsNodeWhenThereIsNoHomeDirectory`, `coding/cli/package_agents_skills_upstream_test.go::TestPackageManagerHomeDirFallsBackToSystemHome`, `internal/codingagent/home_dir_test.go::TestNoHomeDirectoryLeavesTheProjectsAgentsSkillsTheProjectsOnly`, `internal/codingagent/home_dir_test.go::TestPackageManagerHomeDirThrowsWhereNodesHomedirDoes`, `internal/codingagent/home_dir_test.go::TestValidateAutoDiscoveredOverridesRejectsWhereNoHomeDirectoryExists`, `internal/nodehome/nodehome_test.go::TestDirIsNodesOSHomedir` and 1 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** Running with no home directory now fails the way Pi's package manager does, instead of reading the project's `.agents/skills` as your own. With no `HOME` and no entry for your user in the system's user database (a container run as a user its passwd file does not list), `pig` used to take the home directory to be empty, so the `.agents/skills` directory of the current project was listed as the user's `~/.agents/skills`, with user scope and without the project-trust prompt. Startup in print and RPC mode, a reload and `pig config` now stop with `A system error occurred: uv_os_homedir returned ENOENT (no such file or directory)` and exit status 1, which is what Node's `os.homedir()`, and so Pi, reports there. Pi stops even earlier, at load, whatever the mode; PiG, which can run without a home directory by setting `PIG_HOME`, stops when it loads resources.

### BF-bf9911e

**Append ops from the Chord delta tracker and `DiffRevisions` own their text, as under Pi, instead of holding a…**

Retention at 10,000 commits drops to 1.8 MB.

- **Tests:** `chord/delta/op_text_retention_norace_test.go::TestAppendOpsDoNotRetainTheirSourceText`
- **Release note:** Append ops from the Chord delta tracker and `DiffRevisions` own their text, as under Pi, instead of holding a cut of the whole string they were taken from. A delta chain, watch backlog or replica built from appends to a growing text no longer keeps one copy of the text per commit alive (10,000 commits of 8-byte appends retained 430 MB for 80 KB of payload).

Tests now clear PIG_CODING_AGENT_DIR, PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, PIG_HOME and HOME to temporary directories through one shared helper, and make test records the agent directory named by the environment before and after the run (files, directories, lock directories and content hashes) and fails if anything changed. ### BF-c05aa12

**A `turn_end` or `agent_before_settle` handler that returns a `context_edit` draft without the `replacement`…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** PiG took the absent member for null, left the target out of model context and continued.

- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms

- **Fix commits:** `65a97c7f91` (2026-11-13), `c05aa12b6c` (2026-11-13)

- **Release note:** A `turn_end` or `agent_before_settle` handler that returns a `context_edit` draft without the `replacement` member now stops the run as it does in Pi, with Pi's message that the replacement "must be null or contain string/array content": nothing is appended and the run does not continue. Before this fix, PiG took the absent member for null, left the target out of model context and continued. The cause: the host decoded an absent member and a null one into the same value.

### BF-c0d8731

**tui: a renderer that draws on its own frame timer (one with no render dispatcher: the `tui.alt` screen of an…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** tui: a renderer that draws on its own frame timer (one with no render dispatcher: the `tui.alt` screen of an extension, a program that embeds the package) wrote a frame from the timer goroutine while `ShowOverlay`, `HideCursor`, `ShowCursor`, `WriteRaw` or a stop wrote from the caller: two goroutines were in the terminal writer at once, and a cursor or raw sequence could land among the bytes of a frame, between its rows and its cursor placement.
- **Root cause:** A frame holds the render lock for all of its writes, so two frames never ran together. HideCursor, ShowCursor, WriteRaw and QueryCellSize held nothing, and through them ShowOverlay, the hide of the last overlay, SetShowHardwareCursor and Start: on a renderer that keeps its own frame timer the caller wrote while a frame of the timer goroutine was in the writer. Pi writes from one event loop (tui.ts showOverlay: terminal.hideCursor(), then requestRender()): a cursor write is before a frame or after it.
- **User impact:** Wrong display
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `c0d873133b` (2026-11-13)
- **Tests:** None recorded.
- **Release note:** tui: a renderer that draws on its own frame timer (one with no render dispatcher: the `tui.alt` screen of an extension, a program that embeds the package) wrote a frame from the timer goroutine while `ShowOverlay`, `HideCursor`, `ShowCursor`, `WriteRaw` or a stop wrote from the caller: two goroutines were in the terminal writer at once, and a cursor or raw sequence could land among the bytes of a frame, between its rows and its cursor placement. Every write of a renderer now holds its writer lock and a frame keeps it from its first write to its last, so such a write is before the frame or after it, as on the one event loop of Pi; a write a component makes from its `Render` still goes before the bytes of its frame. The interactive mode of pig draws and calls from one loop and showed no fault.

### BF-c122088

**A durable nested call keeps its arguments in the member order the caller wrote them, as Pi does: the stored…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A durable nested call keeps its arguments in the member order the caller wrote them, as Pi does: the stored call and execute intent, the `pi.live` nested slot, tool events, validation messages, and code mode's "took a different path" message (`tools.name({...})`) no longer sort them.
- **Root cause:** codemode earlier() named the call an earlier attempt made with its arguments sorted, where Pi codemode.ts:783 writes JSON.stringify(made.arguments) in the script's member order. The order was lost before that: ExecuteTool takes a Go map, and startNestedCall stored a ToolCall with no member order, so every nested call's stored call, slot, execute intent, validation message and start event listed its arguments sorted. Session's copyTaskRecord also decoded each task record into Go maps, so a staged record lost the order of its input and checkpoint (Pi copyJson keeps it).
- **User impact:** Wrong output or ordering
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `c122088b8c` (2026-10-13)
- **Tests:** `ai/validate_arguments_order_test.go::TestValidateToolArgumentsReportsTheArgumentsInTheCallsOrder`, `durable/codemode/codemode_test.go::TestDurableCodeMode`, `durable/codemode/models_test.go::TestCodeModeModels`, `durable/core/driver/harness_nested_slots_core_test.go::TestCoreANestedSlotShowsTheArgumentsTheCallRunsWith`, `durable/harness/harness_tasks_scheduling_test.go::TestTaskClose`, `durable/harness/tool_nested_test.go::TestANestedCallKeepsTheCallersArgumentOrder`, `durable/harness/tool_nested_test.go::TestANestedCallSlotShowsTheArgumentsItRunsWith`
- **Release note:** A durable nested call keeps its arguments in the member order the caller wrote them, as Pi does: the stored call and execute intent, the `pi.live` nested slot, tool events, validation messages, and code mode's "took a different path" message (`tools.name({...})`) no longer sort them. Code mode's `models.*` calls no longer store an extra `order` argument.

### BF-c1292ec

**A PiG that runs without a model API no longer panics when a caller streams through pi-ai's compat functions**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A PiG that runs without a model API no longer panics when a caller streams through pi-ai's compat functions.
- **Root cause:** A build with pig_strip_bedrock_converse_stream, pig_strip_google_vertex or pig_strip_mistral_conversations (a Piglet Binary whose strip.apis names the API), and Stock PiG running a Piglet that strips one, panicked in ai.BuiltinProviders:
- **User impact:** Crash, hang or runaway process
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `c1292ecbab` (2026-11-12)
- **Tests:** `ai/builtin_providers_strip_test.go::TestStrippedProvidersAreNotBuilt`, `ai/providers/bedrock/bedrock_models_upstream_stripped_test.go::TestBedrockUpstreamModelCatalog`, `ai/strip_built_test.go::TestBuiltStrippedProvidersMatchTheStripState`
- **Release note:** A PiG that runs without a model API no longer panics when a caller streams through pi-ai's compat functions. This affected a Piglet Binary whose `strip.apis` names `bedrock-converse-stream`, `google-vertex` or `mistral-conversations` (build tags `pig_strip_bedrock_converse_stream`, `pig_strip_google_vertex`, `pig_strip_mistral_conversations`), and Stock PiG running a Piglet file with such a strip. In such a Binary the provider bridge subprocess (the `provider-bridge` command of the PiG executable, the transport of an extension's detached helpers such as background runs of pi-subagents) exited with status 2 and `panic: Provider <id>: at least one of "api", "images", or "classifiers" is required.` on its first stream request, whatever provider the request named. In both, an extension's pi-ai `stream` or `complete` call failed with `internal_panic: panic in HandleCall for <extension>.modelStream: Provider <id>: at least one of "api", "images", or "classifiers" is required.`. The built-in provider collection behind those calls now leaves a stripped provider out: requests to the other providers run, and a request for a model on a stripped API ends with `Provider <id>: API <api> is stripped from this Piglet (strip.apis: <api>)`. `--version`, `--help`, `--list-models`, print mode, RPC `get_available_models` and a `--model` that names a stripped provider were not affected, and neither was a build that strips only extensions or features. The defect is in every release since 0.5.0.

### BF-c13e751

**A `before_provider_request` handler of a subprocess extension (Node, Python, Go, Rust, Lisp) now receives the…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A `before_provider_request` handler of a subprocess extension (Node, Python, Go, Rust, Lisp) now receives the request a Google, Vertex or pi-messages provider is about to send with its members in the order Pi's provider creates them (the model, contents and config of Google's parameters, the part members thought, text, thoughtSignature, functionCall before thoughtSignature), where it received them sorted by name.
- **Root cause:** Pi hands before_provider_request the object buildParams created, and JSON.stringify writes its members in creation order. PiG built a map, so a subprocess extension saw the members sorted. The provider now holds the member order of the map it hands the hook (ai.HoldHookPayload) and the subprocess host writes it with ai.MarshalHookPayload. Replayed Google parts are written in the member order of Pi convertMessages.
- **User impact:** Wrong output or ordering
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `c13e751f73` (2026-11-16)
- **Tests:** `ai/google_replayed_part_order_test.go::TestGoogleReplayedPartsHavePiMemberOrder`, `ai/pi_messages_payload_oracle_test.go::TestPiMessagesPayloadMatchesPi`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/event_payload_order_test.go::TestBeforeProviderRequestWireKeepsPiMemberOrder`
- **Release note:** A `before_provider_request` handler of a subprocess extension (Node, Python, Go, Rust, Lisp) now receives the request a Google, Vertex or pi-messages provider is about to send with its members in the order Pi's provider creates them (the model, contents and config of Google's parameters, the part members thought, text, thoughtSignature, functionCall before thoughtSignature), where it received them sorted by name. A handler that returns the payload unchanged now sends the same bytes as no handler. The Google and Vertex payload has been a map since v0.3.0 and the pi-messages payload since v0.2.0; before them Google's was a struct. The Google request body itself also writes a replayed part's members in that order.

### BF-c229e1c

**A Pi Durable SQLite file written by PiG can be read by Pi, and the reverse, when a task kind, request ID, or…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A lookup by kind, request ID or document address missed rows written by the other implementation.
- **Root cause:** The SQLite differential read each file back only through the storages, and its kinds, keys and request IDs were plain ASCII. encodeIndexedString and encodeJSON used encoding/json, which escapes <, >, & and U+2028/U+2029; Pi's sqlite/storage.ts uses JSON.stringify, which writes them literally. An indexed lookup compares the stored text, so scanTasks by kind, submissionByRequest, findDocument and scanDocuments by kind missed rows the other implementation wrote. This happened in both directions: Pi read Pig's file and Pig read Pi's. Both now use jsstring.MarshalJSON. The test now dumps each file through node:sqlite right after the writes and compares the schema and every row. That exposed a…
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `97e178f7f6` (2026-10-09), `c229e1cae8` (2026-10-10)
- **Tests:** `ai/streaming_json_oracle_test.go::TestStreamingJSONMatchesPiOnSeededInput`, `durable/codecs_test.go::TestDocumentRecordMarshalsInPiStorageOrder`, `durable/storage/memory_pi_oracle_test.go::TestMemoryStorageMatchesPiOnSeededPrograms`, `durable/storage/sqlite_pi_oracle_test.go::TestSqliteStorageMatchesPiOnSeededPrograms`
- **Release note:** A Pi Durable SQLite file written by PiG can be read by Pi, and the reverse, when a task kind, request ID, or document kind or key contains `<`, `>`, `&`, U+2028 or U+2029. PiG now stores indexed columns and records as `JSON.stringify` writes them. Before, a lookup by kind, request ID or document address missed rows written by the other implementation. Stored document records list `createdAt` and `retiredAt` after the other members, as Pi stores them.

### BF-c28880a

**Follows Pi 6aab551a79ba: `--mode json` dropped the events emitted by extension `session_start` handlers, such…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Follows Pi 6aab551a79ba: `--mode json` dropped the events emitted by extension `session_start` handlers, such as `entry_appended` for entries they append, `session_info_changed` for a name they set and the `message_start` and `message_end` of a custom message they send, at startup and after an extension replaces the session (`ctx.newSession()`).
- **Root cause:** The writer subscribed after the session_start emission and a flag held back entry_appended until then, so the entry_appended, session_info_changed and custom message events a session_start handler emits were dropped at startup and after ctx.newSession(). The writer now subscribes first, as print-mode.ts rebindSession does, and the flag is gone. The writer-start fixtures of every SDK gain /writer-renew; scenario json/13 expects the startup events and json/15 compares the stream across a replacement.
- **User impact:** Lost or altered data
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `c28880ae3e` (2026-11-16)
- **Tests:** `coding/cli/json_mode_writer_after_session_start_test.go::TestJSONModeWritesSessionStartEventsOfAReplacementInEverySDK`, `coding/cli/json_mode_writer_after_session_start_test.go::TestJSONModeWritesWhatSessionStartEmitsInEverySDK`
- **Release note:** Follows Pi 6aab551a79ba: `--mode json` dropped the events emitted by extension `session_start` handlers, such as `entry_appended` for entries they append, `session_info_changed` for a name they set and the `message_start` and `message_end` of a custom message they send, at startup and after an extension replaces the session (`ctx.newSession()`). The JSON writer now subscribes before the extensions are bound, so these events follow the session header and come before the prompt's events. The fault is in v0.7.0.

### BF-c371a13

**OpenAI Responses requests keep the prompt cache across tool changes (Pi #11142)**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** OpenAI Responses requests keep the prompt cache across tool changes (Pi #11142).
- **Root cause:** resolveTranscriptTools takes a TranscriptToolSupport (none, additions, changes) and reports FoldedSystemMessages instead of AnchorsAdditions. A transport that takes additional_tools declares every tool in additional_tools items from the head of the input, precedes each later item with the incremental-tools notice, and announces removals as text with the still-unavailable tools restated. Synthetic tool search and Kimi tool messages move the top-level boundary to the last removal or redeclaration, so later loads stay anchored. The openai-responses, azure-openai-responses and openai-codex-responses paths share one converter; openai-completions counts system messages from the transcript's start.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.2
- **Fix commits:** `c371a134cc` (2026-10-20)
- **Tests:** `ai/transcript_tool_changes_test.go::TestResolveTranscriptToolsBoundaryPerTransport`, `ai/transcript_tool_changes_test.go::TestTranscriptToolChangesKimiPrefixAcrossLoadsAfterARemoval`, `ai/transcript_tool_changes_test.go::TestTranscriptToolChangesOpenAIResponsesDoesNotListAToolAsUnavailableBeforeItsRemovalIsAnnounced`, `ai/transcript_tool_changes_test.go::TestTranscriptToolChangesOpenAIResponsesKeepsPrefixAcrossRemovalAndLoads`, `ai/transcript_tool_changes_test.go::TestTranscriptToolChangesOpenAIResponsesRedefinitionIsNotARemoval`, `ai/transcript_tool_changes_test.go::TestTranscriptToolChangesOpenAIResponsesStopsListingAToolAsUnavailableOnceDeclaredAgain`, `ai/transcript_tool_changes_test.go::TestTranscriptToolChangesOpenAIResponsesToolSearchPrefixAcrossLoadsAfterARemoval`
- **Release note:** OpenAI Responses requests keep the prompt cache across tool changes (Pi #11142). Every tool is declared in `additional_tools` items from the head of the input, a removal is announced as text with the still-unavailable tools restated, and synthetic tool search and Kimi tool messages move the top-level tool list only at the last removal or redefinition, so a later tool load no longer rewrites the cached prefix. Applies to `openai-responses`, `azure-openai-responses`, `openai-codex-responses` and Kimi on `openai-completions`.

### BF-c3a6eca

**Markdown rendering follows Pi for lines made only of Unicode spaces (U+00A0, U+3000, U+2003 and the others…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Markdown rendering follows Pi for lines made only of Unicode spaces (U+00A0, U+3000, U+2003 and the others JavaScript's trim removes) in and after lists, a list item whose first line is one such space, a heading line holding U+2028 or U+2029, a table whose last line is such a space at a narrow width, and a `$$` or `\[` block whose text is only whitespace.
- **Root cause:** Go's strings.TrimSpace strips U+0085 and keeps U+FEFF; JavaScript's trim() does the opposite, and marked's blank line, /^[ \t]*$/, is neither: a line of U+00A0, U+3000, U+2003 or U+2028 is text. Pig used TrimSpace for Pi's `text.trim() === ""` and for blank lines: Text rendered a BOM-only string as a row where Pi renders nothing, an assistant text block of U+FEFF was shown, the model selector took `<U+0085>d` as a prefix of "default", and a full-width space line (common between CJK paragraphs) ended a paragraph, a code block, a table or a heading's spacing where Pi keeps it as text.
- **User impact:** Wrong display
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `c3a6eca380` (2026-10-11)
- **Tests:** `tui/assistant_message_render_oracle_test.go::TestAssistantMessageComponentRenderMatchesPi`, `tui/basic_components_oracle_test.go::TestBasicComponentsRenderLikePi`, `tui/markdown_unicode_space_oracle_test.go::TestMarkdownUnicodeSpaceLinesMatchPi`, `tui/model_selector_oracle_test.go::TestModelSelectorInputMatchesPi`, `tui/user_message_render_oracle_test.go::TestUserMessageComponentRenderMatchesPi`
- **Release note:** Markdown rendering follows Pi for lines made only of Unicode spaces (U+00A0, U+3000, U+2003 and the others JavaScript's trim removes) in and after lists, a list item whose first line is one such space, a heading line holding U+2028 or U+2029, a table whose last line is such a space at a narrow width, and a `$$` or `\[` block whose text is only whitespace.

### BF-c4d51d5

**The OpenAI Codex login reads the account id from the access token the way Pi does: the token payload is…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The OpenAI Codex login reads the account id from the access token the way Pi does: the token payload is decoded as standard base64 with Pi's padding and whitespace rules (a payload using the URL-safe `-` or `_` characters is not accepted), and the decoded bytes are read as Latin-1 characters, so a non-ASCII account id comes out as Pi's text.
- **Root cause:** A differential test runs Pi's private decodeJwt and getAccountId in Node (testdata/codex_account_id.mjs cuts them out of the pinned source) over 583 tokens and found 78 differences. Pi decodes the payload with atob(): the standard alphabet only, forgiving padding and ASCII whitespace, and one character per decoded byte, then JSON.parse. Pig used base64url (raw, then padded): it refused a payload with whitespace Pi reads, accepted '-' and '_' that make atob throw, and read a UTF-8 account id as UTF-8 where Pi reads its bytes as Latin-1. jsAtob now implements the WHATWG forgiving-base64 decode. The length-1-mod-4 and alphabet checks were equivalent mutants (the unpadded standard decoder…
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `2c04c1445a` (2026-10-09), `c4d51d5c1a` (2026-10-09)
- **Tests:** `ai/authorization_input_oracle_test.go::TestAuthorizationInputParsersMatchPi`, `ai/codex_account_id_oracle_test.go::TestCodexAccountIDMatchesPi`
- **Release note:** The OpenAI Codex login reads the account id from the access token the way Pi does: the token payload is decoded as standard base64 with Pi's padding and whitespace rules (a payload using the URL-safe `-` or `_` characters is not accepted), and the decoded bytes are read as Latin-1 characters, so a non-ASCII account id comes out as Pi's text.

### BF-c4fae28

**Provider request bodies write a lone UTF-16 surrogate as its escape, as `JSON.stringify` does, instead of…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Provider request bodies write a lone UTF-16 surrogate as its escape, as `JSON.stringify` does, instead of U+FFFD for each byte of its Go form.
- **Root cause:** marshalRequestBody used encoding/json, which writes U+FFFD for each of the three WTF-8 bytes a Go string holds for a lone UTF-16 surrogate, where JSON.stringify writes the unit's escape. Pi leaves some strings unsanitized (the Codex instructions, openai-codex-responses.ts:552; an assistant message's reasoning fields), so PiG sanitized the first and corrupted the second. A body with a U+FFFD character is now encoded with the JSON.stringify encoder (jsstring.MarshalJSON), also inside the request types' own MarshalJSON; any other body encodes as before, so the request allocation gates are unchanged.
- **User impact:** Wrong output or ordering
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `c4fae282a7` (2026-10-11)
- **Tests:** `ai/message_text_surrogate_test.go::TestMessageTextSanitizesLoneSurrogatesOnTheWire`, `ai/openai_message_marshal_test.go::TestOpenAIMessageEncodesAsItsMarshalJSON`, `ai/request_body_lone_surrogate_test.go::TestRequestBodyWritesALoneSurrogateAsItsEscape`
- **Release note:** Provider request bodies write a lone UTF-16 surrogate as its escape, as `JSON.stringify` does, instead of U+FFFD for each byte of its Go form. It matters for the strings Pi does not sanitize: the Codex `instructions`, now sent as Pi sends them, and the reasoning fields of an assistant message. A body with no U+FFFD character encodes as before.

### BF-c4fef6c

**Streaming long code blocks no longer grows memory with every frame: the syntax-highlight cache keeps one copy…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Streaming long code blocks no longer grows memory with every frame: the syntax-highlight cache keeps one copy of a streamed block and is bounded in bytes.
- **Root cause:** The main screen asks the root for the lines kept since the revision it drew last. Line resets and the differential scan start at the first line that can differ: the earlier of the kept prefix and both frames' cursor rows. The per-line reuse of earlier reset results stays, but only while the previous input array is intact: it was composed with overlays, or the root has rendered at most once since. Overlay frames keep nothing, and a frame after RestoreRenderState scans everything. Mouse dispatch reads child heights from the window.
- **User impact:** Wrong display
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `10aebd5c05` (2026-10-09), `136e3703be` (2026-10-10), `79eadcf623` (2026-10-10), `ab5be97bbe` (2026-10-10), `c4fef6c21a` (2026-10-10)

- **Release note:** Streaming long code blocks no longer grows memory with every frame: the syntax-highlight cache keeps one copy of a streamed block and is bounded in bytes.

### BF-c51c77e

**An extension that calls `registerTool({})` or `registerTool(null)` now fails to load with Pi's error text…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** An extension that calls `registerTool({})` or `registerTool(null)` now fails to load with Pi's error text (the missing parameter schema, or the TypeError of reading `parameters`), not a PiG-only message.

### BF-c551a63

**Extension SDKs: tool arguments nested thousands of levels deep no longer fail or end the extension, in any…**

- **Source:** A Pi defect that PiG fixed first (divergence D268)
- **Symptom:** Extension SDKs: tool arguments nested thousands of levels deep no longer fail or end the extension, in any SDK or on any supported Python (3.11 and later).
- **Root cause:** - Go: the extension ended on arguments nested 9998 to 10000 levels, because its reader validated the whole frame against 10000. json.UnmarshalFrame takes 64 levels more (Unmarshal keeps the standard limit, and so the host's marshal), and a frame past that is answered, not fatal: a request with the RangeError, a host call result as an error, a notification dropped with a stderr line. - Rust: the bound is 10016 levels; requests run on 64 MB threads (dropping and writing a deep Value recurses); a notification past the bound is marked, dropped with a diagnostic and does not end the connection. - Lisp: the bound is 10016 levels; a deep notification is dropped with a diagnostic, and the three…
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Pi issue:** none recorded
- **Removed when Pi fixes it:** Pi parses and returns tool arguments without a stack-bound depth limit, or the owner decides the SDKs should stop at Pi's observed depth. Then the call-site markers and this record go.
- **Fix commits:** `c551a6348d` (2026-11-05), `c1da695c1d` (2026-11-06), `e2ea65cfa3` (2026-11-06)
- **Tests:** `extensions/sdk-py/tests/test_deep_frames.py`, `extensions/sdk/json/decode_pool_test.go::TestUnmarshalFrameTakesAnEnvelopeAroundArgumentsNestedTenThousandLevels`, `extensions/sdk/protocol_deep_frame_test.go::TestFrameHeadReadsTypeAndIDWithoutDecodingWhatNests`, `extensions/sdk/protocol_deep_frame_test.go::TestReadLoopAnswersARequestNestedPastTheReaderAndGoesOn`, `test/extension-conformance/deep_event_delta_test.go::TestDeepEventStreamDeltasReachEverySDK`, `test/extension-conformance/model_stream_deep_event_test.go::TestModelStreamEventWithDeepToolArgumentsReachesEverySDK`, `test/extension-conformance/tool_params_deep_test.go::TestToolParamsNestingAcrossSDKs`
- **Release note:** Extension SDKs: tool arguments nested thousands of levels deep no longer fail or end the extension, in any SDK or on any supported Python (3.11 and later). The host sends arguments nested up to 10000 levels, and Pi's own runtime fails the call with `Maximum call stack size exceeded` only where V8 runs out of stack for `JSON.stringify` (about 4400 levels on Node 24; it moves with the Node version). The Python SDK failed the call from about 1000 levels (`maximum recursion depth exceeded`), and from about 990 on Python 3.11; the Lisp SDK ended its extension from 4000 levels; the Rust SDK ended its extension past 4096 levels and its `Context::tool_params` returned `None` from 128; the Go SDK ended its extension from about 9995 levels. Each now returns the object for every frame the host can send, a request nested past what an SDK reads fails with that error while the extension answers the next call, and a notification nested past it (a `model_stream_event` with deep tool arguments reads fine) is dropped with a line on stderr. The Rust SDK also ended its connection on a `message_update` (a tool call in the partial message) or `tool_execution_update` whose delta carried a value nested past 128 levels; both are read now. The Lisp image is built with a 64 MiB control stack per thread (address space, not resident). The difference from Pi's depth-dependent limit is recorded as D268.

### BF-c5b14a5

**The Durable core conformance gate no longer writes the reference checkout from a vitest run: its cache lives…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The Durable core conformance gate no longer writes the reference checkout from a vitest run: its cache lives in the run's output directory.
- **Root cause:** E17 and E18 run `ls` in the reference's packages/durable. The default vitest cache, packages/durable/node_modules/.vite, made the first U row add node_modules to that listing; `contract all` captures the reference once, in its first pass, before any U row, so every later pass compared a listing with node_modules against one without it and both rows failed on every fresh clone (wasm-tinygo, native and the wasm-go diagnostic, in two full runs).
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `c5b14a57be` (2026-10-28)
- **Tests:** None recorded.
- **Release note:** The Durable core conformance gate no longer writes the reference checkout from a vitest run: its cache lives in the run's output directory. The default, `packages/durable/node_modules/.vite`, added `node_modules` to the listing E17 and E18 print with `ls`, which they capture once for the reference before any U row ran, so `make durable-contract` failed both rows against every build on a fresh clone.

### BF-c5ea0d1

**A session with an extension that registers a markdown transformer no longer crashes while an assistant reply…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A session with an extension that registers a markdown transformer no longer crashes while an assistant reply streams.
- **Root cause:** interactive mode handed each assistant block's async markdown transforms block.Invalidate as their completion hook. The hook runs on the background worker that finished the extension's transform chain, and AssistantMessageComponent.Invalidate rebuilds the block's content container (updateContent: the segment list, spacers, thinking-run regions and the scratch child list) while the owner loop streams the next delta into the same block. Two goroutines in updateContent let one clear the shared scratch list while the other passed it to SetChildren, so the container held nil children and the next frame panicked in Container.renderChildLocked with a nil child interface. Only a session with an…
- **User impact:** Crash, hang or runaway process
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `c5ea0d127b` (2026-10-29), `d0d459e754` (2026-10-29)
- **Tests:** `internal/codingagent/assistant_block_async_race_test.go::TestAssistantBlockAsyncMarkdownCompletionLeavesTheBlockToTheOwnerLoop`, `tui/assistant_message_async_test.go::TestAssistantMessageAsyncCompletionMarksBlockDirty`
- **Release note:** A session with an extension that registers a markdown transformer no longer crashes while an assistant reply streams. The transformer runs on a background worker, and its completion rebuilt the reply's content from that worker while the interface was streaming the next delta into the same reply, so both could rebuild it at once and the next frame panicked in `Container.renderChildLocked` with a nil child. A finished transform now only marks the reply for redraw, as it already did for a user message, and the interface rebuilds the reply on its own loop.

### BF-c6f6953

**Wrapped text no longer starts the next line with a space when a styled word ends exactly at the wrap width…**

- **Source:** A fix Pi shipped that PiG ported
- **Symptom:** Wrapped text no longer starts the next line with a space when a styled word ends exactly at the wrap width, and strikethrough no longer runs into the right padding of a wrapped line: the wrap closes `\x1b[29m` at line end like underline and opens it again on the next line.
- **Root cause:** The code that closes a styled word attaches to the following space, so wrapping took that space for a word and moved it to the next line, and strikethrough ran into the padding of a wrapped line. A token is whitespace once its escape codes are skipped, a dropped space keeps its codes on the wrapped line, strikethrough is closed at line end like underline, and trailing spaces are trimmed before the line-end reset.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `c6f6953367` (2026-10-30, #10925)
- **Tests:** `tui/markdown_wrap_boundary_test.go::TestMarkdownStyledWordsAtTheWrapBoundaryPiCase`, `tui/widthx/wrap_boundary_test.go::TestLineEndResetClosesStrikethrough`, `tui/widthx/wrap_boundary_test.go::TestWrapTextWithAnsiStyledWordsAtTheWrapBoundaryPiCases`
- **Release note:** Wrapped text no longer starts the next line with a space when a styled word ends exactly at the wrap width, and strikethrough no longer runs into the right padding of a wrapped line: the wrap closes `\x1b[29m` at line end like underline and opens it again on the next line. The text-wrapping helpers in the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp extension SDKs wrap the same way. Carried forward from Pi 2ce9d527 (earendil-works/pi#10925), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin.

### BF-c723782

**In the Node extension runtime, `ctx.isIdle()` read on the statement after a triggering `pi.sendMessage(..., {…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** In the Node extension runtime, `ctx.isIdle()` read on the statement after a triggering `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })` is busy as in Pi, where the started run cannot end before the handler awaits; a run that settled while the read was in flight made print mode report an idle session.
- **Root cause:** Pi's pi.sendMessage with triggerTurn calls sendCustomMessage, which awaits _startRun (agent-session.ts:2404); _startRun sets _isAgentRunActive before its first await (1895), and Pi's one event loop runs nothing else until the handler awaits or returns, so the handler's next statement reads isIdle false whatever the run would do. The host runs the started run concurrently with the Node process (print mode stages no run start, rpc holds it with rpcCommandRuns), and ctx.isIdle() has read the host on every call since, so a run that settled while the read was in flight made it true.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `c7237820c1` (2026-11-01)
- **Tests:** `coding/cli/extension_send_message_binary_test.go::TestExtensionSendMessageTriggerTurnStartsTheRunAsPi`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/runtime_node_send_idle_test.go::TestNodeIsIdleStaysBusyThroughTheSynchronousRunAfterATriggeringSendMessage`
- **Release note:** In the Node extension runtime, `ctx.isIdle()` read on the statement after a triggering `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })` is busy as in Pi, where the started run cannot end before the handler awaits; a run that settled while the read was in flight made print mode report an idle session. ### BF-c7c99c6

**In fullscreen mode, a click on a message or entry that an extension renders is no longer lost when it arrives…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** In fullscreen mode, a click on a message or entry that an extension renders is no longer lost when it arrives before the extension has drawn the card.
- **Root cause:** A render proxy paints its placeholder from its first request until the frame that follows the extension's first applied answer, and knows no mouse region of the component in that time. HandleMouse answered a click there as a click outside every region, and the click was lost: with a slow extension answer (a loaded host, a slow start) a click on the card did nothing, where Pi's card, built inside the render, takes it from its first frame.
- **User impact:** Lost or altered data
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `c7c99c68c4` (2026-11-13)
- **Tests:** None recorded.
- **Release note:** In fullscreen mode, a click on a message or entry that an extension renders is no longer lost when it arrives before the extension has drawn the card. Until the extension answers its first render request the card is shown as the placeholder `[<type>]`, and a click on that row did nothing: on a slow start or a loaded machine the card stayed closed. The click now waits for the card, and the frame that draws the card gives it the click; several clicks reach the card in the order they were made. A click on a placeholder whose extension never answers still does nothing.

### BF-c80895b

**An entry read from a long session's file no longer keeps the whole shared read (up to 8 MiB) alive: each…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** An entry read from a long session's file no longer keeps the whole shared read (up to 8 MiB) alive: each entry owns its record, so a context built from scattered records retains what it holds and not the gaps between them.
- **Root cause:** An entry decoded from a joined file read kept a slice of the read (up to 8 MiB), pinning the gaps between the records while it was resident: read together, 415 entries retained 2.34 x what the same entries read one at a time do. Each entry now owns its record.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `c80895bd4f` (2026-11-02)
- **Tests:** `coding/session_replay_reads_test.go::TestReplayedTranscriptAllocatesAFractionOfTheSessionFile`, `internal/codingagent/session_run_buffer_retention_test.go::TestEntriesDecodedFromAJoinedReadDoNotPinTheRead`
- **Release note:** An entry read from a long session's file no longer keeps the whole shared read (up to 8 MiB) alive: each entry owns its record, so a context built from scattered records retains what it holds and not the gaps between them.

### BF-c952885-3

**A full disk or a killed process during a credential write could sign you out of every provider**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A full disk or a killed process during a credential write could sign you out of every provider.
- **Root cause:** auth.json was written in place (opened, truncated, written), so a full disk, a size limit or a killed process during the write left it empty or cut short. It is now replaced through a temporary file in the same directory (private from creation, fsynced, renamed over the file, directory flushed), so such a failure leaves the old file whole. The mode, the owner where the process may set it, and the extended attributes (the POSIX ACL on Linux, the user's attributes on macOS) where the file system takes them are kept; a symlinked auth.json is followed; on Windows ReplaceFileW keeps the replaced file's DACL. A read-only auth.json is refused as before. A file with more than one hard link, or whose extended attributes cannot be carried over, is written in place as before, as in Pi, and so are a single file mounted into a container, a file in a directory that cannot be written, and a device or named pipe.
- **User impact:** Credential or permission exposure
- **Platform:** Windows, macOS, Linux
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `c9528855cf` (2026-11-15, #488)
- **Tests:** `ai/auth_compromised_persist_test.go::TestRefreshedCredentialSurvivesALockTakenMeanwhile`, `ai/auth_in_place_test.go::TestCredentialWritesGoInPlaceThroughAHardLink`, `ai/auth_pi_lock_test.go::TestAuthStorageModifierPersistsItsCredentialAfterTheLockWasTaken`, `ai/auth_takeover_same_provider_upstream_test.go::TestAuthStorageTakeoverSameProviderLastWriterWinsLikePiUpstream`, `ai/auth_write_failure_test.go::TestCredentialWriteThatFailsLeavesEveryProvider`, `automation/ci/bugledger/corrections_test.go::TestACorrectionForAnEntryTheLedgerDoesNotHaveFailsTheCheckAndTheGenerator`, `automation/ci/bugledger/corrections_test.go::TestACorrectionThatIsMalformedFailsTheGenerator`, `automation/ci/bugledger/corrections_test.go::TestACorrectionThatRepeatsWhatTheGeneratorDerivesFailsTheCheck` and 60 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** A full disk or a killed process during a credential write could sign you out of every provider. `auth.json` was rewritten in place, so a write that stopped half way left it empty or cut short, and the next login or token refresh then saved a file holding that one provider. The file is now replaced as a whole through a temporary file in the same directory, so where it can be replaced a failed write leaves the old file untouched. A file that exists keeps its mode, owner (where pig may set it), extended attributes (the POSIX ACL on Linux, the user's attributes on macOS) where the file system takes them, exactly the access it had (an ACL the directory would hand a new file is not added), a symlinked `auth.json` and, on Windows, its access rights; a file that does not exist yet gets the mode that is asked for with your umask taken out, as in Pi. pig replaces a file only when that changes nothing but the file itself: where a credential file cannot be replaced atomically, for example a single file mounted into a container, a file in a directory pig cannot write into, a file with more than one hard link, a file whose extended attributes cannot be carried over, or a device or named pipe, pig writes it in place as before, as Pi does, and the debug log (`PIG_DEBUG`) says so. That guarantee does not cover an in-place write: one that fails half way can still leave the file empty or cut short, as before.

### BF-c98e9f9

**Without `HOME` set, the project trust check takes the home directory from the user database, as Pi's…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Without `HOME` set, the project trust check takes the home directory from the user database, as Pi's `os.homedir()` does, instead of treating the working directory as the home directory.
- **Root cause:** hasTrustRequiringProjectResources canonicalizes process.env.HOME || homedir() (trust-manager.ts:187), and Node's os.homedir() reads the user database when HOME is unset or empty. PiG fell back to os.UserHomeDir, which reads only HOME, and resolved the empty result against the working directory: the working directory then counted as the user's home, its .agents/skills never required project trust, and every trust check realpathed the working directory twice.
- **User impact:** Wrong output or ordering
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `02c405c179` (2026-10-13), `c98e9f9bbd` (2026-10-13)
- **Tests:** `coding/cli/path_resolve_ports_test.go::TestPathPortsReportAnUnreadableWorkingDirectory`, `coding/cli/path_resolve_ports_test.go::TestSamePathAndAncestorSkillDirsResolveLikeNode`, `internal/codingagent/trust_manager_test.go::TestHasTrustRequiringProjectResourcesWithoutHOMEStillChecksTheWorkingDirectory`
- **Release note:** Without `HOME` set, the project trust check takes the home directory from the user database, as Pi's `os.homedir()` does, instead of treating the working directory as the home directory. A working directory's `.agents/skills` now requires project trust in that case too.

### BF-c9acbea

**A Session listener that queues more messages than the Session's event buffer holds (64 by default), while it…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A Session listener that queues more messages than the Session's event buffer holds (64 by default), while it runs on the goroutine that emitted its event, publishes its `queue_update` events in order.
- **Root cause:** The Session's event goroutine waited for execMu, a sync.Mutex, while a producer ran a callback inline under it. testing/synctest does not count a Mutex waiter as durably blocked, so synctest.Wait never returned while the callback was held: TestSessionObservationCloseJoinsClaimedCallback hung on its first run (the executor's shutdown waited for execMu), and TestCompactionFailureWaitsForEndListeners needed a synctest.Wait before compaction to dodge the same wait. execMu is now a lock whose waiters block on a channel receive; taking a free lock is one atomic add. The compaction test's workaround is removed.
- **User impact:** Wrong output or ordering
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `375de4a98c` (2026-10-12), `c9acbead45` (2026-10-13)
- **Tests:** `coding/cli/strip_providers_binary_test.go::TestStripBedrockConverseStreamBuildOmitsAWSSDK`, `coding/session_compaction_event_order_test.go::TestCompactionFailureWaitsForEndListeners`, `coding/session_queue_publication_test.go::TestSessionMessageSubscriberQueueBurstPreservesPublicationOrder`, `coding/session_queue_publication_test.go::TestSessionQueuePublicationOverflowIsReleasedOnClose`, `coding/session_rpc33_observation_test.go::TestSessionObservationCloseJoinsClaimedCallback`, `coding/session_rpc33_observation_test.go::TestSessionObservationReservationCanceledBeforeAdmission`, `third_party/awssdk/internal/endpoints/v2/lazy_test.go::TestLazyRegexpMatchesLikeRegexp`
- **Release note:** A Session listener that queues more messages than the Session's event buffer holds (64 by default), while it runs on the goroutine that emitted its event, publishes its `queue_update` events in order. An update could reach `Events` ahead of the one published just before it, so a subscriber saw a queue with one message too many. Every event published after such a burst now runs after it.

### BF-c9acbea-2

**A goroutine that waits to run Session events, such as the Session's event goroutine while a producer runs a…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A goroutine that waits to run Session events, such as the Session's event goroutine while a producer runs a listener itself, now blocks on a channel receive instead of a `sync.Mutex`, so `testing/synctest` counts it as durably blocked.
- **Root cause:** The Session's event goroutine waited for execMu, a sync.Mutex, while a producer ran a callback inline under it. testing/synctest does not count a Mutex waiter as durably blocked, so synctest.Wait never returned while the callback was held: TestSessionObservationCloseJoinsClaimedCallback hung on its first run (the executor's shutdown waited for execMu), and TestCompactionFailureWaitsForEndListeners needed a synctest.Wait before compaction to dodge the same wait. execMu is now a lock whose waiters block on a channel receive; taking a free lock is one atomic add. The compaction test's workaround is removed.
- **User impact:** Crash, hang or runaway process
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `375de4a98c` (2026-10-12), `c9acbead45` (2026-10-13)
- **Tests:** `coding/cli/strip_providers_binary_test.go::TestStripBedrockConverseStreamBuildOmitsAWSSDK`, `coding/session_compaction_event_order_test.go::TestCompactionFailureWaitsForEndListeners`, `coding/session_queue_publication_test.go::TestSessionMessageSubscriberQueueBurstPreservesPublicationOrder`, `coding/session_queue_publication_test.go::TestSessionQueuePublicationOverflowIsReleasedOnClose`, `coding/session_rpc33_observation_test.go::TestSessionObservationCloseJoinsClaimedCallback`, `coding/session_rpc33_observation_test.go::TestSessionObservationReservationCanceledBeforeAdmission`, `third_party/awssdk/internal/endpoints/v2/lazy_test.go::TestLazyRegexpMatchesLikeRegexp`
- **Release note:** A goroutine that waits to run Session events, such as the Session's event goroutine while a producer runs a listener itself, now blocks on a channel receive instead of a `sync.Mutex`, so `testing/synctest` counts it as durably blocked. A synctest test that waited while a listener was held no longer hangs until the package timeout.

### BF-c9f1cff

**The experimental client takes Pi's `ByteTransportFactory` shape: `ClientOptions.TransportFactory` returns a…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The experimental client takes Pi's `ByteTransportFactory` shape: `ClientOptions.TransportFactory` returns a `ByteTransport` whose `Send(ctx, chunk)` returns when the write settles.
- **Root cause:** Production keeps Pi's semantics through the Pi shape: a handler call made during the factory is live (the handler gate is removed; the unix transport starts reading when the Connection has taken it, readStarter), a transport that admits sends itself (Submit) is handed each frame before Connection.Send returns (finding 22; pipelining, finding 23), and a failed Connect joins the transport's lifetime. The package experimental seam and binding-guard tests use the Pi shape.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `4789fa51f0` (2026-10-08), `5dbfed1576` (2026-10-08), `8655ff6ae5` (2026-10-08), `c9f1cffbd5` (2026-10-08)
- **Tests:** `ai/faux_duration_test.go::TestFauxScriptedDurationMsReachesEveryMessage`, `ai/faux_scripted_fields_oracle_test.go::TestFauxScriptedMessageMembersMatchPi`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/runtime_node_user_bash_operations_test.go::TestNodeRuntimeUserBashOperations`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/user_bash_operations_test.go::TestUserBashOperationsExecAbortsWithTheContext`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/user_bash_operations_test.go::TestUserBashOperationsReleaseTheExtensionHandleWhenTheHostDropsThem`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/user_bash_operations_test.go::TestUserBashOperationsReplyWithResultOrWithoutHandleIsLeftRaw`, `extensions/sdk-py/tests/test_user_bash_operations.py`, `extensions/sdk/user_bash_operations_test.go::TestUserBashOperationsStayInTheExtensionUntilTheHostReleasesThem` and 3 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** The experimental client takes Pi's `ByteTransportFactory` shape: `ClientOptions.TransportFactory` returns a `ByteTransport` whose `Send(ctx, chunk)` returns when the write settles. The unix transport uses it, and a transport that admits sends itself (`Submit`) is handed each frame before `Connection.Send` returns.

### BF-ca675e0

**A list item whose text is `[ ] ` or `[x] ` with nothing after the spaces on the line is plain text, not a…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A list item whose text is `[ ] ` or `[x] ` with nothing after the spaces on the line is plain text, not a task item (marked's listIsTask needs a non-whitespace character after the spaces), so `- [ ] ` renders as `- [ ]` like Pi.
- **Root cause:** marked's listIsTask is /^\[[ xX]\] +\S/. splitListTaskMarker accepted `[ ] ` followed by the end of the text or a newline (`- [ ] `, `- [ ] \n c`), so the item rendered with a checkbox marker and a continuation indent of six; Pi keeps `[ ]` as the item's text under a plain bullet.
- **User impact:** Wrong display
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `ca675e0af0` (2026-10-11)
- **Tests:** `tui/markdown_task_item_oracle_test.go::TestMarkdownTaskItemFirstLineIsTextMatchesPi`, `tui/markdown_task_item_oracle_test.go::TestMarkdownTaskItemNeedsATextAfterTheSpacesMatchesPi`

**In RPC mode, `exit.log` no longer says "received SIGTERM" for a single signal that arrived during a shutdown…**

- **Symptom:** In RPC mode, `exit.log` no longer says "received SIGTERM" for a single signal that arrived during a shutdown that stdin's end or `ctx.shutdown()` had started and that finished with exit status 0.

### BF-cb21ee0

**Markdown resolves link reference definitions as Pi does: `[text][label]`, `[label][]` and `[label]` link to a…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Markdown resolves link reference definitions as Pi does: `[text][label]`, `[label][]` and `[label]` link to a `[label]: url` defined anywhere in the message, and the definition line is no longer printed.
- **Root cause:** Markdown now ports marked 18.0.11's link reference definitions. The def block tokenizer runs after HTML blocks. Definitions go into a links map for the whole document, where the first definition of a tag wins. Reference, collapsed and shortcut links resolve against that map, and references to defined tags are masked for emphasis, including the link-in-text check. marked registers every definition before it lexes any inline text. So a document whose definition follows a "[" is rendered a second time with the full map. A definition renders no lines, as in Pi: blanks around it are kept, and text that renders nothing returns [""].
- **User impact:** Wrong display
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `c5796c60b1` (2026-10-05), `b2a820387a` (2026-10-06), `cb21ee0405` (2026-10-06), `d90c2f41b7` (2026-10-08)
- **Tests:** `test/parity/scenarios/interactive-rendering/44-assistant-underscore-emphasis.toml`, `tui/highlight_strip_test.go::TestStripSyntaxHighlightBuildOmitsHljs`, `tui/markdown_autolink_test.go::TestAutoLinkTokensMatchMarked`, `tui/markdown_autolink_test.go::TestAutoLinkURLRuleAtTokenStarts`, `tui/markdown_blockquote_style_test.go::TestMarkdownBlockquoteDefaultStyleMatchesUpstreamBytes`, `tui/markdown_blockquote_style_test.go::TestMarkdownEmphasisAndSetextMatchUpstreamBytes`, `tui/markdown_blockquote_style_test.go::TestMarkdownParagraphSpacingBeforeInterruptingBlockMatchesUpstream`, `tui/markdown_marked_corpus_test.go::TestMarkdownMarkedCorpusMatchesPi` and 6 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** Markdown resolves link reference definitions as Pi does: `[text][label]`, `[label][]` and `[label]` link to a `[label]: url` defined anywhere in the message, and the definition line is no longer printed. A list item whose text starts more than four spaces after its marker, as after a tab, renders as an indented code block.
