### BF-fbe92b6

**A login refresh that took more than fifteen seconds while another pig process opened the credential file lost…**

- **Source:** A Pi defect that PiG fixed first (divergence D651)
- **Symptom:** A login refresh that took more than fifteen seconds while another pig process opened the credential file lost its lock, and the refreshed login was thrown away.
- **Root cause:** the async lock heartbeat (stale/2 = 15 s) was longer than the sync acquirers stale window (10 s), so a live holder looked stale to them.
- **User impact:** Credential or permission exposure
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Pi issue:** none recorded
- **Removed when Pi fixes it:** (A) Pi writes these files through a temporary file and a rename, or otherwise keeps a failed write from truncating them; (C) Pi renews its async lock faster than its sync stale window, or raises the sync stale window to at least twice the async heartbeat.
- **Fix commits:** `73cb76959b` (2026-11-14), `a7f0835033` (2026-11-14), `d5b70c4804` (2026-11-14), `fbe92b66a0` (2026-11-14)
- **Tests:** `internal/atomicfile/atomicfile_test.go::TestWriteFileCreatesPrivateAndKeepsMode`, `internal/atomicfile/atomicfile_test.go::TestWriteFileFollowsSymlink`, `internal/atomicfile/atomicfile_test.go::TestWriteFileRefusesReadOnlyFile`, `internal/atomicfile/inplace_test.go::TestWriteFileCannotCreateAFileInADirectoryItCannotWrite`, `internal/atomicfile/inplace_test.go::TestWriteFileKeepsTheFileWhenTheRenameFailsForAnotherReason`, `internal/atomicfile/inplace_test.go::TestWriteFileReplacesAPlainFileAndReportsNothing`, `internal/atomicfile/inplace_test.go::TestWriteFileReportsARealFailureOfTheInPlaceWrite`, `internal/atomicfile/inplace_test.go::TestWriteFileWritesInPlaceInADirectoryItCannotWrite` and 6 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** A login refresh that took more than fifteen seconds while another pig process opened the credential file lost its lock, and the refreshed login was thrown away. The lock is now renewed every five seconds, so a slow refresh keeps it. Divergence D651 (approved by the owner, 2026-11-14T14:10:39Z "proceed"): Pi renews its async auth lock every 15 s (proper-lockfile stale/2) while its sync readers take any lock older than 10 s; pig renews every 5 s. Why: a live holder is never taken over, so a rotating refresh token is not spent twice. Remove when: Pi renews faster than its sync stale window.

### BF-fc028ee

**The reference web client no longer erases what the user is typing when a view is updated: an `input` or…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The reference web client no longer erases what the user is typing when a view is updated: an `input` or `editor` whose `id` is in the next view keeps its text, selection and the focus, unless the extension changed its `value`.
- **Root cause:** The page rebuilt a mount on every changed digest, so an update of one node (a new mail in the list) erased a half-typed reply in another and could drop the focus. A mount now keeps its element and the new view is morphed into the drawn one: a node of the same kind under the same id keeps its element, so an input or editor keeps its text, selection and the focus; a value the extension changes still replaces the text; a text node that moved to another parent hands its text and the focus to its new element. Nodes with an id are matched by id only, so a node that is gone never lends its text to another id.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `fc028ee6d6` (2026-11-12)
- **Tests:** `examples/ui-view-web/bridge_test.go::TestPageKeepsTypedTextAcrossUpdates`
- **Release note:** The reference web client no longer erases what the user is typing when a view is updated: an `input` or `editor` whose `id` is in the next view keeps its text, selection and the focus, unless the extension changed its `value`.

### BF-fc1703f

**Durable's `tool_search` and Code Mode `searchTools()` rank like the coding agent's tool search: a query that…**

- **Source:** A fix Pi shipped that PiG ported
- **Symptom:** Durable's `tool_search` and Code Mode `searchTools()` rank like the coding agent's tool search: a query that is exactly a tool's name ranks it first, a tool matching more of the query's distinct terms ranks above one matching fewer, a query term in the name outweighs any number of mentions in the description, and a tool whose whole name is in the query gets a large bonus.
- **Root cause:** durable/internal/search ranks the way the coding agent's Bm25Ranker does: the name is a field of its own (three times its IDF per term), the namespace text a second field (half its IDF, not length-normalized), a tool whose whole local name is in the query gets a bonus worth one more match of every query term, a query that is exactly a tool's name ranks it first, and a tool matching more of the query's distinct terms ranks above one matching fewer.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.7.0
- **Fix commits:** `fc1703f003` (2026-10-30, #11631)
- **Tests:** `durable/codemode/search_limit_test.go::TestSearchToolsSearchesNamespaceInstructions`, `durable/internal/search/search_carried_test.go::TestRankDocumentsMatchesPiTheLatestCarriedRanker`, `durable/internal/search/search_pi_oracle_test.go::TestTokenizeAndRankDocumentsMatchPiOnSeededInputs`, `durable/internal/search/search_test.go::TestRankDocumentsMatchesPi`, `durable/internal/search/search_test.go::TestRankDocumentsNormalizesByDocumentLength`, `durable/internal/search/search_test.go::TestRankDocumentsRoundsEveryOperationLikeJavaScript`, `durable/toolsearch/toolsearch_carried_test.go::TestToolSearchMatchesPiTheLatestCarriedRanking`, `durable/toolsearch/toolsearch_carried_test.go::TestToolSearchRanksAToolByItsName` and 1 more in docs/bug-ledger.json
- **Release note:** Durable's `tool_search` and Code Mode `searchTools()` rank like the coding agent's tool search: a query that is exactly a tool's name ranks it first, a tool matching more of the query's distinct terms ranks above one matching fewer, a query term in the name outweighs any number of mentions in the description, and a tool whose whole name is in the query gets a large bonus. `thread_read` with a limit of 1 no longer loads `queue_read`, and `peekaboo app` finds `mcp__peekaboo__app`. `searchTools()` also searches the namespace instructions, as a low-weight field that does not lower the scores of the namespace's tools. Carried forward from Pi c7372af4 (earendil-works/pi#11631), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin.

### BF-fc5baaf

**`pi.exec`'s `timeout` starts once the command has been spawned, as in Pi, so time spent finding and starting…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** `pi.exec`'s `timeout` starts once the command has been spawned, as in Pi, so time spent finding and starting the program no longer counts against it.
- **Root cause:** exec.ts:75 sets the timer after spawn has returned, so finding and starting the program does not count against options.timeout. ExecCommand started it before the PATH search and the fork, so a slow spawn (a long PATH, a loaded host) killed the child before it ran where Pi lets it finish.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `fc5baaf077` (2026-10-13)
- **Tests:** `coding/extension/exec_oracle_test.go::TestExecCommandMatchesPi`, `coding/extension/exec_timeout_unix_test.go::TestExecCommandStartsTheTimeoutAfterTheSpawnAsPiDoes`
- **Release note:** `pi.exec`'s `timeout` starts once the command has been spawned, as in Pi, so time spent finding and starting the program no longer counts against it.

### BF-fc749ad

**A task list item whose first line looks like a heading, quote, rule, bullet, fence, table row or HTML tag…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A task list item whose first line looks like a heading, quote, rule, bullet, fence, table row or HTML tag renders that line as text, and a setext heading over it keeps the checkbox marker, as Pi does.
- **Root cause:** marked splits `[ ] ` into a checkbox token and lexes the rest of the first line as a text token, so `- [ ] # h`, `- [ ] > q`, `- [ ] ---`, `- [ ] - a`, a fence, a table row, a definition or an HTML tag renders as text, while the lines after it are lexed normally; a setext heading over the first line (`- [ ] t` / `===`) takes the marker into its text and the item has no checkbox. Pig stripped the marker and rendered the block. renderList now keeps the marker when setextHeadingEnd matches the original text, and otherwise lexes the first block with a leading control character that no block rule matches, removed from the rendered rows.
- **User impact:** Wrong display
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `fc749adcb9` (2026-10-11)
- **Tests:** `tui/markdown_task_item_oracle_test.go::TestMarkdownTaskItemFirstLineIsTextMatchesPi`
- **Release note:** A task list item whose first line looks like a heading, quote, rule, bullet, fence, table row or HTML tag renders that line as text, and a setext heading over it keeps the checkbox marker, as Pi does.

### BF-fcb3ef3

**`/reload` no longer hangs when extensions that share a packed process (Go, Rust, Python or Lisp) subscribe to…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** `/reload` no longer hangs when extensions that share a packed process (Go, Rust, Python or Lisp) subscribe to the event bus with `pi.events.on` while their factory runs.
- **Root cause:** the Host admitted every retained member of a packed process before it accepted the first connection, while a factory that subscribes to the event bus waits for the Host to serve its own member's connection and the Host serves the members in order
- **User impact:** Crash, hang or runaway process
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `fcb3ef3f9d` (2026-11-16)
- **Tests:** `coding/extension/host/subprocess/retained_factory_bus_test.go::TestGoFactoryReloadRetainedMembersBesideAChangedMemberDeliverOnce`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/retained_factory_bus_test.go::TestGoFactoryReloadWithFactoryTimeSubscriptionsCompletesAndDeliversOnce`, `test/extension-conformance/events_bridge_reload_test.go::TestNativeEventBusReloadKeepsEveryFactoryTimeListenerOnce`
- **Release note:** `/reload` no longer hangs when extensions that share a packed process (Go, Rust, Python or Lisp) subscribe to the event bus with `pi.events.on` while their factory runs. The Host wrote the admissions of every retained member before it accepted the first connection. A runner starts each admitted factory on its own goroutine or thread and takes them in whatever order the scheduler picks, and a factory that calls the Host before it returns waits for the Host to serve its member's connection. When a later member took the factory turn first, the Host waited for an earlier member that could not start its factory, so the reload never returned. The Host now admits each retained member after the members before it have registered, which is the order Pi loads its factories in, and every listener hears an emit once after a reload. PiG 0.5.2 through 0.7.0 have the defect.

### BF-fcb3ef3-2

**fix(extension): admit each retained packed member after the members before it have registered**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** fix(extension): admit each retained packed member after the members before it have registered
- **Root cause:** A reload that keeps a packed process wrote the admissions of every retained member before the host accepted the first connection. The runner starts each admitted factory on its own goroutine, and a factory that calls the host before it returns (pi.events.on, as the factories of Pi do) waits for the host to serve the connection of its own member. The host serves the connections in member order, so when a later member took the factory turn of the runner first, the host waited for an earlier member that could not start its factory, and /reload never returned.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `fcb3ef3f9d` (2026-11-16)
- **Tests:** `coding/extension/host/subprocess/reload_fused_events_test.go::TestHostReloadFusedFactoriesWithFactoryTimeSubscriptionsDeliverOnce`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/retained_factory_bus_test.go::TestGoFactoryReloadWithFactoryTimeSubscriptionsCompletesAndDeliversOnce`, `test/extension-conformance/events_bridge_reload_test.go::TestNativeEventBusReloadKeepsEveryFactoryTimeListenerOnce`

### BF-fdfb748

**A surrogate pair split across two concatenated string halves is written as its character in session files…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A surrogate pair split across two concatenated string halves is written as its character in session files, extension frames and Durable records, as Pi's `JSON.stringify` writes it, instead of as two `\u` escapes.
- **Root cause:** Sibling of (durable/core/jv). The shared host/Go-SDK codec writes WTF-8 surrogate units as \u escapes; a high unit directly followed by a low unit (two WTF-8 halves concatenated in Go) is one code point in a JavaScript string, and JSON.stringify writes the character (node 24: JSON.stringify("\ud83d" + "\ude00") === '"😀"'). appendString now joins such a pair into its four-byte UTF-8; unpaired units stay escapes. This codec writes session entries (jsstring.MarshalJSON), extension frames and Durable storage.
- **User impact:** Wrong output or ordering
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `89338b7eac` (2026-10-10), `fdfb74849c` (2026-10-10), `fe16108cc7` (2026-10-10)

- **Release note:** A surrogate pair split across two concatenated string halves is written as its character in session files, extension frames and Durable records, as Pi's `JSON.stringify` writes it, instead of as two `\u` escapes.

### BF-fe0d5a3

**Chord: waiting for a host to settle now waits for the rest of a handler that parked (a method handler's or a…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** The rest of such a handler ran on a goroutine the settle did not count, so a check made right after the settle could see a state from before it.
- **Root cause:** Lifetimes are unchanged: each task started as a Loop.Go task before (the loop's WaitGroup, which the host's close does not call: Loop.Wait has no production caller) and ends when what it waits for ends at close (the watch, the turn, the ending, the store's refusal of an ended object); the ones that run plugin code (a root fn, a job's Run, an `Awaiting` work) end when the plugin returns, as before, with their context aborted at the seal. Nothing here makes a task outlive its owner that did not.
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `f0020ca3a4` (2026-11-15), `fe0d5a32ce` (2026-11-15)
- **Tests:** `chord/next/host/host_loop_join_test.go::TestLoopJoinDoesNotWaitForAHandlerInSleepAndItResumesAtTheDeadlineAndAtAnAbort`, `chord/next/host/host_loop_join_test.go::TestLoopJoinDoesNotWaitForAHandlerInUntilAbortedAndWaitsForItsRestOnceItIsAborted`, `chord/next/host/host_loop_join_test.go::TestLoopJoinDoesNotWaitForAHandlerParkedOnAGateAndWaitsForItsRestOnceTheGateIsReleased`, `chord/next/host/host_loop_join_test.go::TestLoopJoinWaitsForWhatIsLeftOfAHandlerThatParked`
- **Release note:** Chord: waiting for a host to settle now waits for the rest of a handler that parked (a method handler's or a route's `resolve` after its first wait), for the continuations of every unawaited promise of the host (the close tail, host-data turns, flushes and retries of an object, a reference's follow and release, a root scope's handler, a routine's wait, a job's record) and of the documents. Before, the rest of such a handler ran on a goroutine the settle did not count, so a check made right after the settle could see a state from before it.

### BF-fe16108

**Provider request bodies (OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, Codex, Anthropic, Google and Mistral) write…**

- **Symptom:** Provider request bodies (OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, Codex, Anthropic, Google and Mistral) write `<`, `>`, `&`, U+2028 and U+2029 as they are, as Pi's `JSON.stringify` does, instead of as `\u` escapes.
- **Root cause:** Pi's provider SDKs send JSON.stringify(body) (openai 7.19.0 internal/request-options.js:29; the Anthropic, Google GenAI and Mistral SDKs stringify the same way), which writes these five characters as they are. - **Release note:** Provider request bodies (OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, Codex, Anthropic, Google and Mistral) write `<`, `>`, `&`, U+2028 and U+2029 as they are, as Pi's `JSON.stringify` does, instead of as `\u` escapes.

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** `PI_TUI_ESC_TIMEOUT` now waits as Node's `setTimeout` does for the lone-Escape timer: a fractional value is truncated, and a value under one millisecond or over 2147483647 waits one millisecond instead of that many nanoseconds or about a month.

- **Release note:** When an extension's `before_provider_request` handler returns a replacement body for OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, Codex, Pi Messages, Mistral or Google, PiG sends it as Pi's `JSON.stringify` writes what `JSON.parse` read: `\u00e9` becomes `é`, `1.50` becomes `1.5`, a repeated key keeps its first place with its last value, and array-index keys come first. PiG sent the handler's text unchanged.

### BF-ff6b95e

**Chord's terminal launcher no longer ends the session when a stop and continue (Ctrl+Z, then `fg`) interrupts…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Chord's terminal launcher no longer ends the session when a stop and continue (Ctrl+Z, then `fg`) interrupts the termios ioctl of raw mode: macOS reports that as EINTR, and Node's `setRawMode` retries it, but the launcher's `SetRaw` called `x/term` directly and failed with `interrupted system call`.
- **Root cause:** ProcessTerminal.SetRaw called x/term MakeRaw and Restore directly. A stop and continue (Ctrl+Z, fg) resumes inside the termios ioctl, which macOS reports as EINTR, where Node's setRawMode retries it (libuv uv_tty_set_mode). tui.TestTerminalSyscallsThatCanSleepRetryEINTR flagged both calls. Chord may not link the Pi tui package, so raw mode now has its own copy: unix ioctls in retry loops (platform request constants split by OS) and the Windows console-mode form.
- **User impact:** An operation failed or was rejected
- **Platform:** macOS
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `aadacbc03e` (2026-11-09), `ff6b95eb25` (2026-11-09)
- **Tests:** `tui/terminal_syscall_eintr_audit_test.go::TestEINTRAuditCoversTheWholeRepository`, `tui/terminal_syscall_eintr_audit_test.go::TestTerminalSyscallsThatCanSleepRetryEINTR`
- **Release note:** Chord's terminal launcher no longer ends the session when a stop and continue (Ctrl+Z, then `fg`) interrupts the termios ioctl of raw mode: macOS reports that as EINTR, and Node's `setRawMode` retries it, but the launcher's `SetRaw` called `x/term` directly and failed with `interrupted system call`. Entering and leaving raw mode now retries the ioctls on EINTR.

### BF-ff7b272

**A command's reply is no longer held back by calls or dialogs an extension handler starts after it began to…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A command's reply is no longer held back by calls or dialogs an extension handler starts after it began to wait (`Conn.readLoop` seals `ackHold` on a non-`host_call` `blocked` report and records `ackCounted` on `Envelope` so only calls read before the report hold or release the acknowledgment).
- **Root cause:** ackHold counted host calls and blocked:host_call announcements by when Conn.readLoop read them rather than whether the handler sent them before its blocked report, so a post-report call or announcement read before stateCh was drained raised unapplied or announced and falsely held the acknowledgment
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** Unreleased
- **Fix commits:** `6c102b39a7` (2026-11-22), `ff7b27274e` (2026-11-22)
- **Tests:** None recorded.
- **Release note:** A command's reply is no longer held back by calls or dialogs an extension handler starts after it began to wait (`Conn.readLoop` seals `ackHold` on a non-`host_call` `blocked` report and records `ackCounted` on `Envelope` so only calls read before the report hold or release the acknowledgment).

### BF-ffcd800

**Text after an empty heading follows the same space-token rule as after any other block: blank lines or spaces…**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** Text after an empty heading follows the same space-token rule as after any other block: blank lines or spaces after a final empty heading add the empty row Pi shows.
- **Root cause:** marked trims a heading's raw of its newlines, so the text after it is a space token when longer than one character, as after any block ('# \n\n', '#\n ', 'a\n#\n ' render two or more rows in Pi). The earlier guard that kept the heading's own row from a trailing token is replaced by one for the row a list already added. 9 new rows (6 red before).
- **User impact:** Behavior differed from Pi
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `2a919a4c3c` (2026-10-10), `4e5b684ecd` (2026-10-10), `ac0dc3bee4` (2026-10-10), `cdf0be76e4` (2026-10-10), `ffcd800f73` (2026-10-10)
- **Tests:** `tui/markdown_render_oracle_test.go::TestMarkdownRenderMatchesPi`
- **Release note:** Text after an empty heading follows the same space-token rule as after any other block: blank lines or spaces after a final empty heading add the empty row Pi shows.

### BF-ffeb469

**A long session keeps less memory for each turn it has compacted away**

- **Source:** PiG's own defect
- **Symptom:** A long session keeps less memory for each turn it has compacted away.
- **Root cause:** A 21,000-turn RPC session with automatic compaction grew its live heap by 1.75 KiB per turn. Three parts of that were not entries Pi also keeps: - the /tree search text of an entry compaction moved out of the context was built at eviction (about 340 B per turn); it is now read from the entry's record on the first search, as after an open - the ai tool-call argument encoding cache kept the encodings of dropped calls until its 16 MiB limit (about 480 B per turn); an encoding is now released when its arguments are unreachable - agent.Recorder appended a duration per turn; it keeps the count and the last duration
- **User impact:** Wrong output or ordering
- **Platform:** All platforms
- **Fixed in:** 0.5.0
- **Fix commits:** `ffeb469492` (2026-10-14)
- **Tests:** `agent/timings_test.go::TestRecorderRetainsNothingPerTurn`, `agent/timings_test.go::TestRecorderTurnRoundTrip`, `ai/tool_call_arguments_lifetime_test.go::TestArgumentEncodingsAreReleasedWithTheirArguments`, `ai/tool_call_arguments_lifetime_test.go::TestToolCallArgumentsJSONKeepsNothingForADroppedCall`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/runtime_node_sdk_bundle_test.go::TestNodeLibraryBundlesRegenerateExactly`, `coding/extension/host/subprocess/runtime_node_sdk_bundle_test.go::TestNodeSDKBundleRegeneratesExactly`, `internal/codingagent/session_retained_growth_norace_test.go::TestSessionKeepsNoSearchTextForEntriesNobodySearched`, `internal/codingagent/session_retained_growth_norace_test.go::TestSessionLiveHeapPerExchange`
- **Release note:** A long session keeps less memory for each turn it has compacted away. The `/tree` search text of an entry that compaction moves out of the context is no longer built and kept when the entry leaves memory: the first search reads it from the entry's record, as it already did after opening a session, and a session nobody searches keeps none. The cache of encoded tool-call arguments releases an encoding when the arguments it encodes are no longer reachable, where it kept the encodings of dropped calls until its 16 MiB limit. The agent's turn timer keeps the number of completed turns and the last duration instead of one duration per turn. In a 21,000-turn RPC session with automatic compaction on a 32k window, live heap growth falls from about 1.7 KiB per turn to the index of the session's entries (slots, compressed records, compaction entries), which Pi's in-memory session also keeps, as whole entries.
